To *not falter* was read as the sūrah’s steadiness: the same discipline that makes prayer a writ at fixed times (4:103) makes pursuit a writ where justice requires it. The sūrah elsewhere says *“do not be like those who left homes boastfully and hinder from God’s way”* (8:47), but here the command is internal: let not wound become weakness.

**But You Hope From God What They Never Can**

The distinction *wa tarjūna mina Allāhi mā lā yarjūn* — but you can hope to receive from God what they can never hope for — was explained as the sūrah’s asymmetry of hope. *Tarjūn* — you hope, expect, await — was read as hope for ranks, forgiveness. Mercy from Him (4:96), for many havens and secured reward even if death overtakes on hijrah (4:100), for the humiliating punishment prepared for disbelievers where you guarded prayer (4:102), and for the Gardens where the prayer writ is kept (4:103). That hope was explained as the believers’ exclusive because the disbeliever, by turning away from trust and referral to the Messenger (4:58–61), has no standing to expect it. The clause therefore does not deny the enemy’s pain but denies his hope, as the sūrah elsewhere says *“do not think those who disbelieve prolonging time is good; they increase in sin”* (3:178). The hope is not a claim of victory only; it is forgiveness for the mistaken, mercy for the helpless, and reward for the striver — all sealed *Ghafūr Raḥīm* (4:96, 4:100) or *ʿAfuww Ghafūr* (4:99). The sufferers on one side have a door that sufferers on the other do not: the same suffering, divergent destination.

**And God Is All-Knowing, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAlīman Ḥakīmā* — And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise — was read as the knowledge that weighs faltering and wisdom that times pursuit. *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — was explained as knowing who falters from wound and who from desire to deviate (4:27), who verifies before fighting (4:94) and who seeks fleeting gain by denying peace (4:94), whose earth is wide yet unreachable (4:98) and whose heart can still seek pardon. *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — was read as wisdom that commands pursuit where the oppressed cry (4:75), permits shortening where travel and fear constrict (4:101–102), establishes prayer at fixed time (4:103), and will send the Book to judge by what He shows (4:105). The pair *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* has sealed the law for mistake by fasting (4:92) and for judging between people. Here it seals the ethic of pursuit: He knows pain and knows who bears it for hope and who bears it without hope, and He judges with the wisdom that does not command beyond weakness yet does not excuse faltering where hope is offered.

The comparison was linked to *“if a wound touches you, a like wound touched the other people”* (3:140), revealed after Uḥud where both sides were wounded yet the believers faltered.
verses.105:
> Indeed, We have sent down the Book to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth to judge between people by means of what Allah has shown you. So do not be an advocate for the deceitful

**We Have Sent Down the Book in Truth to Judge Between People**

The verse opens *innā anzalnā ilayka al-kitāba bi al-ḥaqqi li taḥkuma bayna al-nāsi bi mā arāka Allāhu* — Indeed We have sent down the Book to you in truth, with truth, to judge between people by what God has shown you, made you see. *Anzalnā* — We sent down — was read as divine descent, the Book given as the noble command from the All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:58) and as the referral point where disputes are taken (4:59). *Bi al-ḥaqqi* — in truth, with truth, as truth — was explained as that the Book’s content is true and its descent is true and its judgment is true, against the false judges — *ṭāghūt* — sought by those who claim belief (4:60). *Li taḥkuma bayna al-nāsi* — to judge between people — was read as judging among humanity without faction — the same *bayna al-nāsi* as *“when you judge between people judge with fairness”* (4:58). *Bi mā arāka Allāhu* — by what God has shown you — was explained as by what He taught, inspired, made clear, not by outward claim alone; the sūrah has shown that God teaches what you did not know (4:113) and that He is the One who guides to noble ways (4:26). Early reports attached the verse to a theft dispute where a Muslim of the Banū Ẓafar was suspected, his armour hidden with a Jew, and pressure came to shield the Muslim — the verse forbade it, commanding judgment by what God shows, which settled on evidence, not tribal tie.

The term *khāʾinīn* — deceitful, treacherous — was read as weighty: those who hide deception from people but cannot hide from God in whose presence they plot by night what He displeases (4:108). The sūrah has shown deceit’s kin: lagging behind with two faces (4:72–73), double safety while plunging into *fitnah* (4:91), denying peace for fleeting gain (4:94), and spending to show off without belief (4:38). To be an advocate for the deceitful was explained as joining that partnership, taking deceit as associate — and whoever takes Satan as associate, what an evil associate (4:38). The sūrah will say God does not like the deceitful, sinful (4:107) and that there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114); advocacy for deceit falls outside that good. The Prophet ﷺ was therefore told not to be *khaṣīm* for them, just as earlier he was told to turn away from hypocrites who turn away stubbornly (4:63) and to put trust in God as Trustee (4:81).

**A Judging Verse Placed After Prayer and Pursuit**

Placed after pursuit without faltering where both sides suffer yet only the believer hopes (4:104), this verse assigns the judge his hope’s discipline: the same hope that steadies pursuit — hoping from God what the enemy does not — steadies judgment — judging by what God shows rather than by clan. The sūrah that began from a single soul (4:1), that promised many havens to the emigrant (4:100), that shortened and guarded prayer (4:101–102) and fixed it at appointed writ (4:103), now places the Book as the haven for disputes, where a people bound by treaty are paid blood-money even if mistakenly killed (4:92, 4:90) because the *mīthāq* is part of what God shows. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened (4:28), the verse is a shield: where power tempts to be advocate for the deceitful, the Book in truth is the advocate for the deceitful’s victim, showing the judge what to see. The next verses will unfold that prohibition: seek forgiveness (4:106) and do not advocate for those who wrong themselves (4:107), for they hide from people what they cannot hide from God (4:108).

**The Judge Is Only a Human Being**

The Prophet ﷺ described the limit of his own office in a report that governs every judge after him: "I am but a human. You bring disputes to me, and some may be more eloquent, so if I give one his brother's right by his eloquence, it is a piece of fire" (al-Bukhārī 2680; Muslim 1713). The verse tells the Prophet to judge by what God shows him; the hadith tells the parties that eloquence does not change ownership. Both halves protect the same thing: a right must not be carried out of the courtroom by the better speaker.
verses.106:
> And seek Allah’s forgiveness—indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful

**And Seek God’s Forgiveness**

The verse states *wa astaghfiri Allāha* — and seek God’s forgiveness, ask Him to forgive, to cover and efface. *Istaghfara* — to seek *maghfirah* — was explained as requesting covering of fault and wiping of trace, as the sūrah has shown that even religious error before prayer is covered by purification with earth where water lacks (4:43) and that mistaken killing is covered by freeing or consecutive fasting as repentance (4:92). The command was addressed to the Prophet ﷺ directly after *“do not be an advocate for the deceitful”* (4:105), showing that even the thought of inclining to defend the deceitful, or the distress of having nearly done so, calls for seeking forgiveness. Through him the command reaches every judge and every believer: where judgment was to be by what God shows (4:105) and not by clan, the fear of having favoured tie over truth requires seeking cover. The sūrah has taught that if wrongdoers came after wronging themselves seeking forgiveness and the Messenger prayed for them they would find Him ever Accepting of Repentance (4:64), and that whoever does evil or wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness will find Him All-Forgiving, Most Merciful (4:110).

**Indeed God Is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful**

The seal *inna Allāha kāna Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — indeed God is, was ever, All-Forgiving, Most Merciful — was explained as reason for the command, not merely its afterthought. *Ghafūr* — All-Forgiving, much covering — and *Raḥīm* — Most Merciful, ever Merciful — have sealed the wages of strivers (4:96), the emigrant’s secured reward (4:100), and the hope for the helpless (4:99) with *ʿAfuww Ghafūr*, and the law of mistake (4:92); here they seal the judge’s recourse. To name these two names right after prohibiting advocacy for the deceitful was explained as opening the door that advocacy would close: the deceitful themselves, if they abandon plotting by night what displeases Him (4:108) and seek forgiveness, will also find Him All-Forgiving, as the next verses make clear that the door is for all who commit evil then seek — *“whoever commits evil… then seeks God’s forgiveness will find Him”* (4:110).

**A Short Verse Between Two Prohibitions**

The verse’s brevity — *“seek forgiveness, God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful”* — placed between *“do not be advocate for the deceitful”* (4:105) and *“do not advocate for those who wrong themselves”* (4:107) was explained as deliberate interruption. The sūrah inserts seeking forgiveness between the two advocacy warnings so that judgment is not left as mere negation — do not defend — but as positive turn — seek cover. The pattern matches the sūrah’s earlier insertion: between asking *“was not God’s earth spacious?”* (4:97) and promising many havens (4:100) the sūrah inserted exception and hope for the helpless (4:98–99). Here between two warnings to advocates the sūrah inserts the remedy that corrects both advocate and wrongdoer. Classical notes added that the sequence shows that the advocate’s fault, if he inclined, is not equal to the deceitful’s treachery (4:107) in degree, but both need the same Names; the judge’s seeking is for inclination, the wrongdoer’s for act. The verse therefore holds the community that was divided into two groups about hypocrites (4:88) together under one covering: whichever group erred by advocating, the path back is seeking.
verses.107:
> Do not advocate for those who wrong themselves. Surely Allah does not like those who are deceitful, sinful

**Do Not Advocate for Those Who Wrong Themselves**

The verse states *wa lā tujādil ʿani alladhīna yakhtānūna anfusahum* — and do not plead, do not advocate, dispute for those who betray, deceive themselves. *Tujādil* — to argue, to plead, to dispute — was explained as standing as *khaṣīm* — disputant, advocate — the same prohibition just given to the Prophet ﷺ not to be advocate for the deceitful (4:105). *Alladhīna yakhtānūna anfusahum* — those who betray, wrong themselves — was read as that betrayal of another is betrayal of the self, as the sūrah has shown that those who consume orphans’ wealth consume fire into bellies (4:10) and that whoever earns sin earns it only against himself (4:111). To betray the community’s trust by theft and then conceal it is to wrong the self before wronging the other, because the Book was sent to judge by what God shows (4:105) and hiding from Him by night displeases Him (4:108). The prohibition therefore forbids advocacy for self-wrongers even where kinship pulls, as the sūrah earlier forbade taking the hostile who wish you alike as allies (4:89) and warned not to say to a bearer of peace “you are no believer” for gain (4:94): ties do not convert wrong into right.

**Surely God Does Not Like the Deceitful Sinful**

The reason *inna Allāha lā yuḥibbu man kāna khawwānan athīmā* — surely God does not like, does not love, every deceitful, treacherous, sinful one — was explained with two intensives: *khawwān* — much betraying, repeatedly treacherous — and *athīm* — much sinning, burdened with sin. Both were read as persistent traits, not a single slip; the sūrah has pardoned error soon after with repentance (4:17) and accepted repentance for mistake by freeing or fasting (4:92). *khawwān athīm* names the one who plots by night what He displeases (4:108) and hides it from people. *Lā yuḥibbu* — does not like, does not love — was explained as removal of divine love and support, as the sūrah said He does not like the arrogant boastful who withhold bounty (4:36–37) and said He will prepare humiliation for disbelievers where the guarded prayer stands (4:102). To be not loved while being *khawwān athīm* means no advocacy can bring love where treachery remains. The phrase was also linked to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40): His not loving the treacherous is not wrong; it is the accurate measure of treachery that chose to betray itself before betraying others.

**A Verse That Generalises the Advocate Warning**

Placed after *“do not be advocate for the deceitful”* to the Prophet ﷺ (4:105) and the insertion *“seek forgiveness”* (4:106), this verse generalises to every advocate: do not plead for those who wrong themselves. The sūrah has shown that advocates were pleading for the accused before evidence was seen, as the community was divided into two groups about hypocrites (4:88) and as reports are to be referred to the Messenger and those in authority for validation (4:83). The generalisation shows that the law is not personal: no one — not the Prophet as judge, not the tribe as pleader — may make treachery lovable by advocacy. The sūrah’s ethic of returning trusts and judging fairly as noble command from the All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:58), and of verifying before fighting (4:94), here becomes ethic of arguing: do not dispute for the self-betrayer, for the Disliked — *lā yuḥibbu* — will not be made loved by dispute. The verse was read as closing clan advocacy where theft was at stake: the armour stolen and hidden with a Jew was not made clean by the Muslim’s clan pleading, because the self had already been betrayed by hiding.
verses.108:
> They try to hide ˹their deception˺ from people, but they can never hide it from Allah—in Whose presence they plot by night what is displeasing to Him. And Allah is Fully Aware of what they do

**In Whose Presence They Plot by Night What Displeases Him**

The circumstance *wa huwa maʿahum idh yubayyitūna mā lā yarḍā mina al-qawli* — and He is with them when they plot, harbour by night what is displeasing, not approved, of speech — was explained as divine presence not as indwelling but as knowledge and witnessing. *Yubayyitūn* — to harbour by night, to plot by night, to contrive in darkness — was read as the same root *b-y-t* seen where a group spends the night contradicting what they said before you and God records their schemes (4:81): *yubayyitūna* is their night speech that does not match day speech. *Mā lā yarḍā mina al-qawli* — what He does not approve of speech, what is displeasing Him — was explained as the false defence, the projection onto the innocent (4:112), the counsel to shift guilt. The sūrah has said that God records schemes (4:81) and that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114); night plotting that shifts theft onto a Jew is the evil secret talk. That He is *maʿahum* — with them — at that hour was read as terrifying gentleness: the plotting is not done in absence, but in presence, as the sūrah elsewhere says *“He is with you wherever you are”* (57:4) by knowledge, and here adds displeasure — *lā yarḍā* — at the speech.

**And God Is Fully Aware of What They Do**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu bi mā yaʿmalūna muḥīṭā* — And God is Fully Aware, Encompassing, of what they do — was explained as *muḥīṭ* — encompassing, surrounding, comprehending — not merely aware but encircling. *Muḥīṭ* appears where the sūrah says God encompasses all things in knowledge (4:126), and where He is enough as Trustee (4:132). To be *muḥīṭ* of what they do means no night speech escapes perimeter: the theft, the moving of goods, the coaching, the advocacy sought (4:107), the advocacy given (4:109), and the advocacy withheld when the Book judges (4:105). The sūrah has sealed knowledge names diversely — All-Knowing, All-Wise where mistake law and pursuit meet (4:92, 4:104), All-Hearing, All-Seeing where trusts are judged (4:58) — here *Muḥīṭ* fits night, whose darkness seems to create enclosure; the verse says the night is itself enclosed. The attribute was also linked to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40): His encompassing does not add weight; it measures the atom exact, including the atom of night speech.

**A Verse That Turns Night Into Presence**

Placed after the two prohibitions to advocates (4:105, 4:107) and the insertion to seek forgiveness (4:106), this verse turns night into presence. The sūrah has shown that those who spend the night contradicting what they said are recorded (4:81) and that reflection on the Qur’an would reveal many inconsistencies had it been from other than God (4:82); inconsistency between day claim and night plot is the deceitful’s equivalent. The sūrah that warns not to take disbelievers as allies for honour (4:139) and that declares hypocrites will be in lowest depth (4:145) here shows the advocate’s risk: to plead by day for what was plotted by night in His presence is to plead for speech He displeases while He encompasses. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, the verse is not a burden but a clearing: where you were asked to hide a kinsman’s theft by day after he plotted by night, you need not hide, because hiding from people is not hiding from the Encompassing. The honest word that *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness finds Him”* (4:110) remains open to the plotter if he leaves night plotting.
verses.109:
> Here you are! You ˹believers˺ are advocating for them in this life, but who will ˹dare to˺ advocate for them before Allah on the Day of Judgment? Or who will come to their defence

**Here You Are — Advocating for Them in This Life**

The verse opens *hā antum hāʾulāʾi jādatum ʿanhum fī al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* — Here you are, you believers are, you are these who have disputed for them, advocated for them, in the life of this world. *Hā antum* — behold you, here you are — was explained as summons and gentle rebuke, as the sūrah summons witnesses for justice though against yourselves (4:135). *Jādaltum ʿanhum* — you disputed for them, advocated — repeats the same *jādala/jādal[tum]* as *“do not advocate for those who wrong themselves”* (4:107) and *“do not be advocate for the deceitful”* (4:105), showing the community indeed did dispute after the theft. *Fī al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* — in the nearer life — was read as the place where advocacy can seem to work because judges must weigh oaths and eloquence — *“some of you may be more eloquent”* (Bukhārī 2680) — and where kinship pulls. The sūrah has shown that enjoyment of this world is little and the Hereafter better for the mindful (4:77), that fleeting gain is sought by denying peace (4:94) and that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114). Disputing for the deceitful in this life is another fleeting gain — a kinsman saved from shame — sought where speaking truth would have cost shame but gained the Book’s favour. The phrase was also read as the sūrah’s reminder that this life is the only court where human advocacy can affect verdict before divine.

**But Who Will Advocate for Them Before God**

The question *fa man yujādilu Allāha ʿanhum yawma al-qiyāmati am man yakūnu ʿalayhim wakīlā* — but who will dispute, advocate for them before God on Resurrection Day? Or who will be their defender, trustee, agent over them — was explained as two challenges. *Man yujādilu Allāha ʿanhum* — who will dispute God on their behalf — was read as impossible: there is no disputant against God’s knowledge, for He is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108) and Encompassing of it. He records night plotting while with them at what displeases Him. *Yawma al-qiyāmati* — on the Day of Standing — was explained as the Day about which there is no doubt where He will gather you all (4:87) and where each will be judged by the Book sent in truth (4:105). *Man yakūnu ʿalayhim wakīlā* — who will be their *wakīl*, defender, trustee, agent — was read as the same *wakīl* the sūrah commanded to trust: *“God is sufficient as Trustee of Affairs”* (4:81), *“God is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132). The verse was linked to *“on that Day those who denied and disobeyed the Messenger will wish they were dust”* (4:42), for advocacy will have no ground where every hidden night saying is present.

**A Verse That Measures This Life’s Advocacy by the Next**

The comparison — *fī al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* versus *yawma al-qiyāma* — was read as the sūrah’s measurement of advocacy. In this life to dispute for the self-wrongers may succeed where a story is coached, where armour is said to be with a Jew, where oaths are divided. On the Day, the Judge is the One who was with them while they plotted by night (4:108) and who will not be disputed because He was never absent. The sūrah has said that God will gather all together — about which there is no doubt (4:87) — and that those who were oppressed and wronged themselves will be asked *“what were you doing?”* at soul-taking (4:97); advocacy that might deflect a human question will not deflect that. The sūrah has also shown that seeking forgiveness is still open — *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness finds Him”* (4:110) — which is the only advocacy that works on the Day: not a pleader for deceit, but a sinner’s own seeking that meets the All-Forgiving. The question therefore reframes advocacy: the advocate’s eloquence in this life is real, but the forum is small; the forum that matters has no *khaṣīm* for deceit and no *wakīl* besides Him who does not love the deceitful sinner (4:107).
verses.110:
> Whoever commits evil or wrongs themselves then seeks Allah’s forgiveness will certainly find Allah All-Forgiving, Most Merciful

**Whoever Commits Evil or Wrongs Themselves**

The verse opens *wa man yaʿmal sūʾan aw yaẓlim nafsahū* — whoever commits evil, does a bad deed, or wrongs themselves. *Sūʾ* — evil, bad deed — was explained as harm to another: theft, false accusation, consuming wealth unjustly, the theft of armour and its projection onto the innocent that the preceding passage exposed (4:105–112). *Yaẓlim nafsah* — wrongs themselves — was explained as that the same act is self-wrong, as the sūrah has said *“do not advocate for those who wrong themselves”* (4:107), *“whoever earns sin earns it only against himself”* (4:111), and *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness”* is the pattern of repentance. The pairing *sūʾan aw yaẓlim nafsah* was read as comprehensive: evil outward toward people and wrong inward toward the soul are not two categories but two faces of one act, because to betray trust (4:58) is to betray the self that will stand before God who is with you when you plot by night (4:108). The sūrah has shown that human weakness makes evil possible — *humankind was created weak* (4:28), desires wish you deviate greatly (4:27), envy wishes you alike in disbelief (4:89) — yet the same weakness, acknowledged, opens the next clause. Classical notes stressed the *man* — whoever — as unrestricted: believer, companion who erred, deceitful who plotted, even the Jew falsely accused — the door is for whoever acted.

**Will Certainly Find God All-Forgiving, Most Merciful**

The promise *yajid Allāha Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — will certainly find God All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, will find Him so — was explained as certainty of finding: *yajid* — will find — not *perhaps will find*. The same *yajid* was used where the wrongers coming to the Prophet ﷺ would *certainly find Him ever Accepting of Repentance, Most Merciful* (4:64); here every evil-doer seeking will find the same. *Ghafūr* — All-Forgiving, much covering — and *Raḥīm* — Most Merciful, ever Merciful — were explained as the two that make finding more than acquittal: covering the evil, removing trace of self-wrong, and bestowing mercy beyond covering — ranks, havens, secure reward as with the emigrant (4:100). The sūrah has sealed forgiveness diversely — *Ghafūr Raḥīm* for strivers (4:96), *ʿAfuww Ghafūr* for helpless (4:99), *Ghafūr Raḥīm* for the judge told to seek (4:106); here the pair is the universal seal for every *sūʾ* and self-wrong that turns. The promise was linked to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40): to seek and not find would be a wrong measured in less than atom; the *yajid* declares He does not wrong. The verse was also placed against the threat for intentional killing where anger, curse, and mighty preparation remain unless sought away (4:93): seeking is the opening even there where it is most needed.

**A Verse That Opens the Door Advocacy Could Not**

Placed after *“you advocate for them in this life, who will advocate on the Day?”* (4:109) and *“they hide from people but not from God with whom they plotted by night”* (4:108), this verse opens the door advocacy could not: seeking forgiveness finds. The sūrah that pronounced *God does not like the deceitful sinner* (4:107) and that said there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), here says the good that remains open after the evil secret talk is to seek. The sūrah that warned the enemy wishes you neglect for a sweep (4:102) and that commanded not to falter in pursuit (4:104) yet to judge only by what God shows (4:105), here steadies the heart that fears judgment has been corrupted by advocacy: whoever — advocate or wrongdoer — commits evil then seeks will find. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, this is the lightest of all: after teaching prayer shortened and guarded (4:101–102) and remembered standing, sitting, lying (4:103), the sūrah lightens the heaviest burden — guilt — by making finding certain upon seeking.
verses.111:
> And whoever commits a sin—it is only to their own loss. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise

**Whoever Commits a Sin — Only to Own Loss**

The verse states *wa man yaksib ithman fa innamā yaksibuhū ʿalā nafsihī* — and whoever commits, earns, a sin, it is only upon, against, his own self, to his own loss. *Yaksib* — to earn, to acquire, to commit — was explained as the Book’s commerce language: sin is earning, as a good deed is multiplied many times over by grace (4:40). As striving earns degree (4:96). *ʿAlā nafsihī* — only upon himself, against his self — was explained as that the weight does not transfer to the advocate who disputed for him in this life (4:109) nor to the innocent upon whom it is later thrown (4:112). The sūrah has shown the same principle where *“those who wrong themselves”* are not to be advocated for (4:107), where *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness finds Him”* (4:110), and where *“whoever does evil or wrongs themselves”* is the broadest door to seeking. Here the principle is the ledger: to *earn* sin is to deposit loss into the self’s account, because God does not wrong even an atom — He measures the atom exact (4:40) and knows what is in hearts (4:63). Early commentators stressed the *innamā* — only — as restriction: the sin’s burden is not on the clan, not on the Jew falsely accused, not on the community divided into two groups (4:88); it is on the earner.

**Allah Is All-Knowing, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAlīman Ḥakīmā* — And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise — was explained as the attribution that makes the ledger certain. *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — was read as knowing the earning while hidden from people but not from Him in whose presence they plot by night (4:108), encompassing what they do (4:108), hearing the advocacy in this life and the lack of advocate on the Day (4:109). *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — was read as wisdom that places each earning on its earner with exactness, that judges between people by what He shows (4:105) and not by eloquence, and that distinguishes mistake requiring freeing or fasting (4:92) from intent requiring Hell unless sought away (4:93). The pair *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* has sealed mistake law (4:92) and pursuit without faltering (4:104); here it seals earning. The sūrah has said that God is enough as Witness (4:79) and Reckoner (4:86); to be All-Knowing is to be the Witness who never misses, to be All-Wise is to be the Reckoner who never wrongs. The burden on the self is therefore not a metaphor but a measured account with the One who knows and judges with wisdom.

**Earning Sin as Commerce That Only Loses**

The verb *yaksib* was read to keep commerce in view: the sinner thinks to *earn* — gain, profit — by theft, by shifting blame, by seeking fleeting gain denying peace (4:94), yet the verse says the earning is *ʿalā* — upon, against — the self, as a debt, not *lahū* — for him as profit. The sūrah has contrasted true earning — *“God has promised each a fine reward”* (4:95) and *“many havens and abundance”* for the emigrant (4:100) — with false earning — devouring orphans’ fire (4:10) and taking dowry unjustly (4:20). To *earn* sin is therefore to be the merchant who puts loss into his own pouch while thinking he put gain. Classical notes added that the *ithm* here is the general term that includes *khaṭīʾah* — error — and *buhtān* — slander — made explicit next (4:112); all are earned only as loss. The only reversal of that loss is not another’s advocacy (4:109) but seeking forgiveness, which finds Him All-Forgiving, Most Merciful (4:110), and even then the original earning remains recorded until covered.
verses.112:
> And whoever commits an evil or sinful deed then blames it on an innocent person, they will definitely bear the guilt of slander and blatant sin

**Whoever Earns an Evil or Sin Then Throws It on the Innocent**

The verse states *wa man yaksib khaṭīʾatan aw ithman thumma yarmi bihī barīʾan* — and whoever earns an error, a mistake, or a sin — *khaṭīʾah* as unintentional or lesser fault, *ithm* as sin — then throws it, casts it upon the innocent, the clear, the free. *Yaksib* — to earn — continues the ledger language: sin is earned only upon the self (4:111), not transferable by advocacy (4:109). *Thumma yarmi bihī* — then throws it with it, casts — was explained as adding projection to earning: having earned slander’s occasion, he throws the blame, as the deceitful threw the stolen armour’s guilt onto the Jewish neighbour and plotted by night speech displeasing to Him (4:105–108). *Barīʾ* — innocent, free, clear — was read as one free of the act, as the Jew was, as any person is until shown otherwise by what God shows the judge (4:105). The sūrah has warned against devouring wealth unjustly (4:29) and against calling a bearer of peace “you are no believer” for gain (4:94); to throw sin on the innocent is the judicial equivalent — to devour honour as wealth. The disjunction *khaṭīʾatan aw ithman* — error or sin — was read as covering both degrees: whether the original fault was smaller error or grave sin, throwing makes it heavier, as the verse closes.

**They Bear Slander and Blatant Sin**

The recompense *fa qad iḥtamala buhtānan wa ithman mubīnā* — they will definitely bear, have carried, slander and blatant, manifest sin — was explained with two loads: *buhtān* — slander, false accusation, calumny — and *ithm mubīn* — clear, manifest sin. *Iḥtamala* — to bear, to carry on the back — was read as carrying as a burden, the opposite of the ranks borne as honour (4:69) and humiliating punishment prepared for disbelievers (4:102). *Buhtān* was explained as the lie that begets bewilderment — *bahata* — to confound with false charge; the sūrah has shown that the deceitful hide from people but cannot hide from the Encompassing (4:108), so the slander confounds people for a night but not Him. The doubling was stressed: before throwing he bore *khaṭīʾah* or *ithm* upon himself (4:111); after throwing he bears that plus *buhtān* plus another *ithm mubīn* — a multiplication of burden unlike God’s multiplication of good many times over (4:40). Early reports noted this verse completed the theft case: the Muslim thief’s clan sought to make the Jew bear the theft; the verse says the thrower bears slander and manifest sin, not the innocent.

**From Night Plotting to Double Burden**

The sequence was read as moral causality: night plotting displeasing to Him while He is with them (4:108) → human advocacy in this life attempting to sustain it (4:109) → earning that stays on self (4:111) → throwing that adds slander and blatant sin. The *thumma* — then — marks not time only but increase: the second burden is added to the first, so that hiding from people (4:108) and disputing before a human judge (4:109) does not reduce but increases the load where the innocent is targeted. The sūrah has paired *Ghafūr Raḥīm* for seeker of forgiveness (4:110) — covering and mercy — and pairs here *buhtān* and *ithm mubīn* — exposure and manifest sin — for thrower who does not seek. The contrast was linked to *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds”* (4:110): the thrower could still seek and find, but throwing while persisting keeps the slander as carried. The verse was also linked to *“those who conceal testimony wrong the heart”* (2:283) and to *“do not let hatred of people cause you to deviate from justice”* (5:8), showing that throwing sin inherits both false speech and injustice.
verses.113:
> Had it not been for Allah’s grace and mercy, a group of them would have sought to deceive you ˹O Prophet˺. Yet they would deceive none but themselves, nor can they harm you in the least. Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you never knew. Great ˹indeed˺ is Allah’s favour upon you

**Had Not God’s Grace and Mercy Been Upon You**

The verse opens *wa law lā faḍlu Allāhi ʿalayka wa raḥmatuhū la hammat ṭāʾifatun minhum a yuḍillūka* — had it not been for God’s grace, bounty, upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved, intended, to deceive, to lead astray, you. *Faḍl* — grace, bounty, surplus — and *raḥmah* — mercy — were explained as the two that preserve the Prophet ﷺ where human eloquence and kin pleading pull (4:105–112). *Law lā* — had not, were it not for — was read as the sūrah’s counterfactual that declares actual protection, as earlier *“had it not been for God’s grace and mercy you would have followed Satan except few”* (4:83). *Hammat* — resolved, intended, concerned itself — was explained as firm intent: the group intended to make the judge misjudge, to make the Book-sent-to-judge (4:105) seem to support the deceitful. *An yuḍillūka* — to lead you astray, to deceive you, to make you deviate from right judgment — was read as seeking to make the Prophet ﷺ advocate for the deceitful despite the prohibition not to be advocate for the treacherous (4:105) and not to plead for self-wrongers (4:107). The group — *ṭāʾifah minhum* — was explained as the clan of the thief and its advocates, who hid armour with a Jew, coached night speech displeasing to Him (4:108), and argued in this life expecting advocacy to succeed (4:109).

**Yet They Deceive None But Themselves and Cannot Harm You**

The counter *wa mā yuḍillūna illā anfusahum wa mā yaḍurrūnaka min shayʾ* — yet they would deceive none but themselves, nor can they harm you at all — was explained with two restrictions: deception returns to the deceiver and harm does not reach the protected. *Yuḍillūna illā anfusahum* — they deceive only themselves — matches the prior principle *whoever earns sin earns only upon himself* (4:111) and *bears slander and blatant sin where he throws on the innocent* (4:112). To seek to deceive the Prophet ﷺ where God is with the plotters by night encompassing what they do (4:108) is to deceive the self that thinks night hides. *Wa mā yaḍurrūnaka min shayʾ* — they cannot harm you in the least, with anything — was read as divine protection of the messenger’s judgment, as the sūrah said He is enough as Trustee (4:81, 4:132) and told the Prophet ﷺ to put trust in Him and turn aside from those who contradict by night (4:81). Early reports noted the Prophet was distressed at nearly defending the wrong party; the verse comforts that distress was not harm, as *“God will protect you from people”* (5:67) protects the message though not from feeling the pressure. The clause also generalises: whoever throws sin on the innocent (4:112) harms only himself with slander.

**A Verse That Closes the Judgment Passage With Grace**

Placed after the double burden of throwing sin on the innocent (4:112) and before the rule that no good is in most secret talks except three (4:114), this verse closes the judgment passage with grace. The sūrah that began the passage *“do not be advocate for the deceitful”* (4:105) traverses seeking forgiveness (4:106), not advocating for self-wrongers (4:107), hiding from people not from the Encompassing (4:108), advocating in this life versus no advocate on the Day (4:109), seeking then finding (4:110), earning only upon self (4:111), throwing that adds slander (4:112). Ends where it began — had not grace and mercy been upon you, you would have been deceived. The passage is therefore not a lesson in distrust of people but in trust in the Book and wisdom taught. The sūrah that declared disbelievers your clear enemies (4:101) and that promised humiliating punishment where prayer was guarded (4:102) here declares the Prophet’s protection as the community’s protection. That judgment between people — including those bound by treaty whose blood-money is paid even where mistaken (4:92) — remains by what God shows, and great is His favour upon the one shown.
verses.114:
> There is no good in most of their secret talks—except those encouraging charity, kindness, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does this seeking Allah’s pleasure, We will grant them a great reward

**No Good in Most Secret Talks**

The verse states *lā khayra fī kathīrin min najwāhum* — there is no good in much, in most, of their secret talks, private counsels. *Najwā* — secret talk, whispering, private counsel — was explained as the night plotting just exposed: *yubayyitūna mā lā yarḍā mina al-qawli* — harbouring by night what displeases Him (4:108) — and advocating for self-wrongers (4:107) and throwing sin on the innocent (4:112). *Lā khayra* — no good — was read as no benefit, no virtue, no reward, as the sūrah has said of those who hide from people while God is with them where they plot (4:108) and of advocates who dispute in this life but will find no disputant on the Day (4:109). *Kathīrin* — much, many — was stressed: most secret talks are not good, though some are, so that secrecy itself is not condemned, only its content. The sūrah has shown that reports are to be referred to the Messenger and those in authority for validation (4:83) and that verification before fighting is required (4:94); secret talk that bypasses referral and verification is the opposite. Classical notes added that the *hum* — their — refers to the deceitful group and by extension any private counsel not turned to good; the generality widens the rule beyond the theft case to every confidentiality that hides deceit.

**Whoever Does This Seeking God’s Pleasure — Great Reward**

The promise *wa man yafʿal dhālika ibtighāʾa marḍāti Allāhi fa sawfa nuʾtīhi ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and whoever does this seeking God’s pleasure, favour, approval, We will grant them a great, mighty reward — was explained with two conditions: doing the commanded good — *yafʿal* — and seeking by this God’s pleasure — *ibtighāʾa marḍāti Allāhi* — not reputation. *Marḍāt* — pleasure, approval — was read as the same seeking that distinguishes true striving with wealth and lives (4:95) from seeking fleeting gain by denying peace (4:94) and from spending to show off without belief (4:38). *Fa sawfa nuʾtīhi ajran ʿaẓīmā* — We will grant great reward — was explained as the same *ajr ʿaẓīm* promised to the striver above the sitter (4:95–96) and to the one who holds fast after repentance (4:146); the reward for commanding charity, kindness, reconciliation in secret is therefore ranked with striving. The *sawfa* — will, soon — was read as certainty, as the emigrant’s reward already secured where death overtakes (4:100). Early reports illustrated *iṣlāḥ* with a man who reconciles two disputants by private counsel where public speech would shame, achieving without humiliating preparation for disbelievers (4:102) a peace that is itself worship.

**A Verse That Generalises the Theft Case Into an Ethic of Speech**

Placed after the Prophet’s preservation by grace and teaching (4:113), this verse generalises the theft case into an ethic of speech. The Book and wisdom taught him what he did not know — the hidden moving of armour, the night counsel — and by that teaching the community learns that most private counsels are not good unless they encourage the three. The sūrah has shown that *“God wishes to lighten burdens”* (4:28), that purification is eased with earth (4:43), that prayer is shortened on travel (4:101). That precaution remains even when arms are laid aside (4:102); here speech is eased: private talk is not burdened with prohibition, only guided — make it about charity, kindness, reconciliation, and it is great reward. The sūrah has also warned that to follow desires is to deviate greatly (4:27) and that Satan commands altering creation and deluding with hopes (4:119–20); secret talk that deludes is Satan’s *najwā* (58:10), while secret talk that reconciles is God’s. For the weak the sūrah lightens, this is a practical lightening: you need not be present at every dispute, but if you whisper, whisper toward giving, kindness, mending.

*Ṣadaqah* — charity, alms — was read as giving from what God provided, the opposite of devouring orphans’ wealth and of withholding bounty (4:37–40), and as the blood-money waived charitably (4:92) and dowry graciously adjusted (4:4).
verses.115:
> And whoever defies the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them and follows a path other than that of the believers, We will let them pursue what they have chosen, then burn them in Hell—what an evil end

**And Follows a Path Other Than That of the Believers**

The second condition *wa yattabiʿ ghayra sabīli al-muʾminīna* — and follows a path other than that, a way other than the way, of the believers — was explained as taking a way distinct from the community’s way. *Sabīl* — path, way — was read as the sūrah’s path language: God wills to make path clear and guide to noble ways (4:26), Satan wishes the deviant path far away (4:60), verification is the path before fighting (4:94), earth’s spacious path is for emigration (4:97–100). *Sabīl al-muʾminīn* — path of the believers — was explained as the believers’ collective way in creed, law, and conduct, the same congregation commanded to go forth together (4:71) and to stand for justice even against selves (4:135). Early authorities including al-Shāfiʿī inferred from this phrase the authority of consensus — *ijmāʿ* — where the believers’ path in understanding the Book is protected, though the core meaning remains moral: to follow other than their path after guidance is clear is to follow desires that deviate greatly (4:27) and to join Satan’s party. The sūrah has warned that most secret talks have no good except three that seek God’s pleasure (4:114); following other than the believers’ path was read as the secret talk made public as doctrine — private deceit become alternative way.

**We Will Let Him Pursue What He Has Chosen**

The recompense *nuwallihī mā tawallā* — We will let, turn him to what he turned to, leave him to what he chose, entrust him to his direction — was explained as handing the defier over to his choice, as the sūrah said God allowed hypocrites to regress because of misdeeds (4:88) and as *“whoever is left to stray you will never find a way”* (4:143, 4:88). *Nuwallihī* — to turn, to make *walī* — guardian of — was read as divine leave: he chose the other side after clarity. God leaves him there, as the emigrant who chose God’s side finds many havens (4:100) and the helpless who could not choose are hoped to be pardoned (4:99). The phrase was linked to *“We will turn their hearts and eyes as they did not believe at first”* (6:110) and to *“He leaves to stray whom He wills”*; the *tawallā* — turned — that began as human act becomes divine *nuwallihī* — We turn him. The sūrah has said that God does not wrong even an atom (4:40); to let the defier pursue his chosen side is not wrong, it is the atom measured exact.

**Then Burn Them in Hell — What an Evil End**

The outcome *wa nuṣlihī Jahannam wa sāʾat maṣīrā* — then We will burn, roast them in Hell, enter them into Fire. Evil as destination, as becoming — was explained with *nuṣlihī* — to cause to burn, to roast, to enter into burning — the same verb for those who consume orphans’ wealth will be burned in blazing Hell (4:10) and those who reject signs will be cast into Fire where skins are replaced (4:56). *Jahannam* was read as the abode already assigned to the intentional killer with anger and curse (4:93) and to those who wronged themselves while earth was wide (4:97); here it is for defiance after clarity and following other than believers’ way. *Wa sāʾat maṣīrā* — evil as destination, evil as becoming — was explained as the sūrah’s closing formula for abodes of those who choose other than God’s cause, matching *evil destination* for the self-wronger (4:97, 4:115). The phrase was linked to the beginning where limits set by God admit to Gardens forever (4:13) and exceeding limits casts into Hell forever (4:14); defying the Messenger after guidance is exceeding that limit at its root — the referral to God and Messenger where disputes are taken (4:59).

The same verb *shāqqa* appears where *“whoever defies God and Messenger, God is severe in punishment”* (8:13), marking defiance as more than disagreement — it is adoption of enmity.
verses.116:
> Surely Allah does not forgive associating ˹others˺ with Him ˹in worship˺, but forgives anything else of whoever He wills. Indeed, whoever associates ˹others˺ with Allah has clearly gone far astray

**God Does Not Forgive Association — But Forgives What Is Less**

The verse states *inna Allāha lā yaghfiru a yushraka bihī wa yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika li man yashāʾ* — God does not forgive that others be associated with Him, but forgives what is below that — anything less — for whomever He wills. The same sentence was given at 4:48, and its return here was explained as deliberate closure after defiance after guidance and following other than believers’ path whose end is burning (4:115). *An yushraka bihī* — that association be made with Him — was read as setting a partner beside God in worship, the *shirk* repeatedly defined where limits were set and the caller was warned not to go to extremes about faith (4:171) and where *“He does not forgive associating”* anchors the whole sūrah’s monotheism. *Mā dūna dhālika* — what is below that, less than that — was explained as every sin besides association: error, sin, throwing sin on the innocent (4:111–112), deceit, advocacy for deceit, even intentional killing where repentance might yet be sought. The sūrah has shown that whoever earns sin earns only upon himself (4:111) and whoever commits evil then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110); the limit is that association, persisted in without repentance, is not covered. The seal *li man yashāʾ* — for whom He wills — was read as divine will in forgiveness, not human claim: *“Divine grace is neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book”* (4:123), but by His will after justice to His measure.

**A Verse That Follows Threat of Burning With the Unforgivable Root**

Placed after *“We will let him pursue what he chose and burn, evil destination”* (4:115), this verse names the root that makes burning not arbitrary: association is the one sin not forgiven without repentance because it denies the very One to whom forgiveness is sought. The sūrah has traced *shirk*’s allies — devouring wealth unjustly (4:29), envy of God’s bounties (4:54), believing in *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* (4:51) — and here gathers them: to associate is to have gone far. The helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) and the emigrant finds many havens (4:100) remain within forgiven range. The repetition from 4:48 to 4:116 was explained as bracketing the judgment passage: the first came before the limits of inheritance and the second after the law of deceit and advocacy, both saying: the framework — trusts returned, disputes referred, prayer guarded, judgment by Book — assumes the One to whom referral is made. To associate while referring to Him is the contradiction the Book in truth came to remove (4:105, 4:105).

**Forgives What Is Less — But Only for Whom He Wills**

The clause *wa yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika li man yashāʾ* was explained as opening hope without opening presumption. The sūrah has shown that intentional killing earns Hell with anger and curse yet the door of seeking remains (4:93, 4:110), that throwing sin on the innocent earns double burden yet seeking remains, that defying the Messenger earns burning yet seeking before that end remains. *Li man yashāʾ* — for whom He wills — was read to prevent the wishful — *“neither by your wishes”* (4:123) — from counting forgiveness as debt. The sūrah pairs this will with knowledge and wisdom: *All-Knowing, All-Wise* where earning stays on self (4:111), *All-Hearing, All-Seeing* where trusts are judged (4:58). Forgiveness below association is therefore not automatic, nor random, but will governed by knowledge of repentance, of plotting by night, of advocacy, of throwing. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, the verse is steadying: what is below association remains within the spaciousness that Earth’s havens image (4:100) — many exits — yet association removes the earth itself, because the earth’s spaciousness is *His* earth (4:97).
verses.117:
> Instead of Allah, they only invoke female gods and they ˹actually˺ invoke none but a rebellious Satan—

**They Invoke Nothing Besides Him Except Females**

The verse states *in yadʿūna min dūnihī illā ināthan* — they call, they invoke, besides Him — instead of God — except females, female ones. *Yadʿūna* — to call, to invoke, to pray to — was explained as worship by invocation, the same calling that the sūrah condemns where people call upon another god with God (25:68 cited) and where association is not forgiven (4:116). *Min dūnihī* — besides Him, instead of Him, short of Him — was read as departure from the Single Source to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126). *Illā ināthan* — except females, female gods — was explained as the Meccan invocation of female-named deities — al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, Manāt — called daughters of God. More broadly as weak, powerless beings chosen as partners, the female being taken as symbol of weakness in that culture’s idolatry though in reality both male and female beyond God are powerless. The sūrah has shown that those given a portion believe in *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* (4:51) and wish you deviate. That devouring wealth unjustly is condemned (4:29); invoking females besides God was read as the religious form of that deviation: to give what belongs to the Creator of the single soul (4:1) to imagined females. The phrase was linked to *“they only invoke female gods”* as sign of the far straying — *ḍalālan baʿīdā* (4:116) — where association takes the form of venerating the weakest claimants.

**A Verse That Unmasks Idolatry as Satanism**

Placed after *whoever associates has gone far astray* (4:116), this verse unmasks idolatry as Satanism. The arc from defying the Messenger and following other than believers’ path (4:115) to association’s far straying (4:116) to invoking females besides Him is the path of deviation: guidance was clear, yet *ṭāghūt* was sought (4:60), trust betrayed (4:107), night plot hidden from people (4:108). The religious expression is to call upon what cannot hear. The sūrah elsewhere says *“have you not seen those given a portion who believe in *jibt* and *ṭāghūt*”* (4:51); here *ināth* and *shayṭān marīd* are that *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* named in Meccan form. The identification — females but really Satan — was read as the Book’s demystification: the many gods dissolve into one enemy, the rebellious Satan, whose promise is only delusion (4:120) and whose portion is Hell without escape (4:121). Where the sūrah promised great reward for commanding charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114), this verse shows the opposite command — Satan orders slitting ears of cattle and altering creation (4:119) — and promises nothing but loss.

**A Short Verse That Bridges Association and Satan’s Vow**

Though only *“they invoke beside Him only females, and they invoke only rebellious Satan,”* the verse bridges association’s doctrine (4:116) and Satan’s vow (4:118–119). The sūrah has shown that the Devil’s cause is fought for by disbelievers (4:76), that his followers wish you deviate greatly (4:27), and that whoever takes Satan as guardian instead of God suffers tremendous loss (4:119). To invoke females besides Him is the act; to invoke rebellious Satan is the agency. The verse was read as the sūrah’s answer to those who claim *“we only worship them to bring us near to God”* (39:3): you claim nearness by females, but you arrive at Satan, for his command is behind the rite. The next verses will let Satan speak: cursed, he says *I will take a share, mislead, delude with hopes, order slitting and altering* (4:118–119), and *he promises only delusion* (4:120), whose end is Hell without escape (4:121) versus the Gardens promised truly to those who believe and do good (4:122).

*Shayṭān* — Satan, the adversary — was read as Iblīs who was granted respite until the appointed Day and who vowed to sit in ambush (7:15–17), whose schemes are weak (4:76) yet whose whisper deludes.

The Qur’an elsewhere says that when a daughter is announced, faces darken (16:58); yet they assign daughters to God, showing desire not for truth but for a partner that cannot challenge.
verses.118:
> cursed by Allah—who said, “I will surely take hold of a certain number of Your servants

**Cursed by God**

The verse opens *laʿanahu Allāhu* — cursed by God, expelled from mercy, removed from favour, condemned. *Laʿanahu* — He cursed him — was explained as God’s removal of the rebellious Satan — *shayṭān marīd* — invoked besides Him as female gods (4:117) — from mercy, as the sūrah earlier said God is angry, curses. Prepares mighty punishment for the intentional killer (4:93) and as it said the deceitful are not loved (4:107). The curse here was read as the original curse upon Iblīs after refusing to prostrate to Adam and after requesting respite until the appointed Day (7:12–15; 15:34–35; 38:77–78), where *“cursed”* — *malʿūn*, *rajīm* — is named. The sūrah has said that the Devil’s schemes are weak (4:76) yet must be curbed, and that whoever takes Satan as guardian instead of God suffers tremendous loss (4:119); the curse is the foundation of that loss: the guardian taken is already expelled. Early reports linked the curse to the declaration *“upon you is curse until the Day of Recompense”* (38:78) after he said *“I will surely take a share.”* The sūrah’s seal *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) frames the curse: it is not arbitrary. It is the measure for rebellion — *marīd* — after guidance was clear and prostration refused.

**Who Said — I Will Surely Take a Share of Your Servants**

The vow *wa qāla la attakhidhanna min ʿibādika naṣīban mafrūḍā* — and he said, I will surely take hold, seize for myself, from Your servants a certain, appointed, share, portion — was explained as Satan’s declared program after being cursed. *La attakhidhanna* — surely I will take — emphatic with oath and *nūn* of certainty, as the hostile who wish you to disbelieve as they have (4:89) and who plot by night (4:108) also speak with emphasis. Satan’s oath here is before God Himself. *Min ʿibādika* — from Your servants — was read as from humanity created from a single soul (4:1) and to whom the earth was made spacious (4:97, 4:100). *Naṣīban mafrūḍan* — a share appointed, a portion fixed, due — was explained as a portion he will claim as if due, a fixed share of those who follow him besides God to call females (4:117), to believe in *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* (4:51), to desire deviation greatly (4:27). The phrase *mafrūḍ* — appointed — was linked to inheritance shares appointed as *farīḍah* (4:11–12) where God’s apportioning is just; Satan’s *mafrūḍ* is the counterfeit apportioning where he claims servants as if inheritance. The sūrah has shown that those given a portion trade it for misguidance (4:44); here Satan claims a portion for misguidance.

**A Verse That Places Curse Before Program**

Placed between *they invoke only rebellious Satan* (4:117) and *I will mislead, delude, order slitting ears and altering creation* (4:119), this verse places curse before program. He is not cursed because he takes a share; he takes a share because he is cursed — expelled, then vowing. The order was read as the sūrah’s causal chain after association’s far straying (4:116): association is the human side of accepting the share Satan claimed, and Hell without escape (4:121) is the share’s end. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose (4:115); to accept Satan’s share is that defiance in worship. Where the emigrant’s reward is said to have fallen upon God secure (4:100) and the striver’s wages are ranks from Him (4:96), the Satanic share is the inverse inheritance — a portion that fell upon the cursed, not upon God. The verse generalises the theft case’s throwing sin on the innocent (4:112): Satan throws his curse-burden onto his share, but the burden stays with the thrower and is borne as slander — here as *buhtān* upon creation.
verses.119:
> I will certainly mislead them and delude them with empty hopes. Also, I will order them and they will slit the ears of cattle and alter Allah’s creation.” And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a tremendous loss

**I Will Certainly Mislead and Delude With Empty Hopes**

The vow continues *wa la uḍillannahum wa la umanniyannahum* — I will certainly mislead them and certainly delude them with hopes, with wishing, with *umniyah* — empty promising. *Uḍillannahum* — to lead astray, to cause deviation — was explained as Satan’s first work upon his appointed share (4:118) after curse, the *ḍalāl baʿīd* — far straying — of association (4:116). *Ummaniyahum* — to delude with hopes, to cast wishes, to promise — was read as the mechanism of misguidance: not force but hopes, as the sūrah has shown that Satan promises only delusion (4:120) and that his hopes are empty — *ghurūr* — while God’s promise is true (4:122). The sūrah has shown desires that wish you deviate greatly (4:27), and that the deceitful hide from people but God is with them where they plot by night (4:108); empty hopes delude because they hide consequence. The one who is misled thinks he is given respite as generosity — the sūrah’s *istidrāj* without name but present — while the Book says *“He delays but His plan is flawless”* (68:44 cited in sūrah 7:183). The hopes delude where the emigrant’s true hope is for ranks, forgiveness, mercy (4:96) and many havens (4:100); Satan’s hope is the counterfeit that spending to show off (4:38) or withholding bounty (4:37) is honour preserved.

**And Whoever Takes Satan as Guardian Instead of God Suffers Tremendous Loss**

The verdict *wa man yattakhidh al-shayṭāna waliyyan min dūni Allāhi fa qad khasira khusrānan mubīnā* — and whoever takes Satan as guardian, protector, ally instead of God has certainly suffered a tremendous, manifest, clear loss — was explained with *walī* — guardian, patron, protector — the same *walī* and *naṣīr* the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45). To take Satan as *walī* instead — *min dūni Allāhi* — was read as choosing the cursed (4:118) as guardian whose promise is delusion (4:120). *Khasara khusrānan mubīnā* — suffered tremendous, clear loss — was explained as loss manifest in both worlds: in this world by slitting what was wholesome and altering what was created balanced, in the next by Hell without escape (4:121) versus Gardens forever under true promise (4:122). The sūrah has shown that whoever takes Satan as associate, what an evil associate (4:38), and that the share Satan takes is the share of those who invoke besides Him (4:117–118); to take him as *walī* is to become that share. The loss is *mubīn* — clear — because the alternative — the Book and wisdom taught (4:113), the great reward for charity and reconciliation (4:114), the forgiveness found upon seeking (4:110) — was clear, and the choice of the cutter over the Creator is clear deviation.

**A Verse That Makes Satan’s Program Concrete**

Placed after curse and appointed share (4:118), this verse makes Satan’s program concrete: mislead, delude with hopes, order slitting ears and altering creation. The sūrah that warned not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to follow other than believers’ path (4:115) here shows what the other path orders and what its followers execute: cutting creation to mark it for another. The sūrah that began with unity from a single soul (4:1) and that will say to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He encompasses all (4:126) sees altering creation as assault on that unity. For the weak this is protective: to alter creation is not light craft but tremendous loss, clear, because the Creator who made humanity weak yet wills to lighten (4:28) and who gives many havens (4:100) is replaced by a commander who orders cutting. The next verse will summarise the commander’s economy: he promises and deludes with empty hopes, he promises nothing but delusion (4:120), whose end is Hell without escape (4:121).

*Yubattikunna* — to slit, to cut lengthwise, to notch — *ādhāna al-anʿāmi* — ears of cattle — was explained as the Meccan custom of dedicating livestock to idols — *baḥīrah, sāʾibah, waṣīlah, ḥām* (5:103) — by slitting ears as mark, forbidding its use, devoting it to the female gods (4:117).
verses.120:
> Satan only makes them ˹false˺ promises and deludes them with ˹empty˺ hopes. Truly Satan promises them nothing but delusion

**Satan Promises and Deludes With Empty Hopes**

The verse states *yaʿiduhum wa yummanīhim* — he promises them and deludes them with hopes, with *umniyah*, wishing. *Yaʿiduhum* — to promise, to hold out — was explained as Satan’s currency after being cursed and taking an appointed share (4:118) and ordering misleading, slitting ears, altering creation (4:119). The promises were explained as the hopes already named — *ummaniyahum* — empty hopes: that association is nearness, that invoking females brings intercession (4:117), that cutting cattle is devotion, that altering creation is honour, that throwing sin on the innocent cleans the thrower (4:112), that advocacy in this life will have advocacy on the Day (4:109). The sūrah has shown that those who wish you deviate wish it greatly (4:27), that the lagger wishes to share gain without sharing faith (4:73), that the regressed wish you alike in disbelief (4:89); Satan’s promising is the source wish that generates those. *Wa yummanīhim* — and he deludes with hopes — was read as keeping them in wishing — *tamannī* — so that the wish never becomes turning, as the sūrah warns that repentance delayed until death says “now I repent” is not accepted (4:18).

**Truly He Promises Nothing But Delusion**

The qualification *wa mā yaʿiduhumu al-shayṭānu illā ghurūrā* — Satan promises them nothing but delusion, deception, vanity — was explained with *ghurūr* — delusion, deceptive vanity, gloss that vanishes. *Ghurūr* was read as promise that looks like benefit but is harm, as goods neglected for a sweeping assault where weapons are unguarded (4:102) looked safe for a moment. The sūrah elsewhere says *“do not let the deceiver deceive you about God”* (31:33; 35:5) with *gharūr* as Satan’s name, showing that delusion is his title. To say he promises *only* delusion — *illā ghurūra* — was explained as exclusivity: there is no true promise in his portfolio, as the next verses contrast his delusion with Hell without escape (4:121) and with Gardens where God’s promise is always true (4:122). Early notes linked *ghurūr* to the world’s fleeting enjoyment — *matāʿ qalīl* — the little enjoyment the sūrah said is little versus the Hereafter better for the mindful (4:77), and the fleeting gain sought by denying peace (4:94); Satan promises that little as if great. The sūrah has shown that good and evil are both destined while evil from the self as means (4:79); Satan’s delusion is to make the means — altering creation, slitting ears — seem as if it changes destiny toward good.

**A Verse That Follows Altering Creation With Its True Price**

Placed after *he will order slitting ears and altering creation and whoever takes him as guardian suffers tremendous loss* (4:119), this verse follows the order with its true price: the order is paid in delusion. The sūrah that warns there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) here unmasks the secret talks that command altering: their payment is *ghurūr*. The sūrah that commands to verify reports (4:83) and to be sure before fighting (4:94) shows verification failing where hope is empty: the deluded do not verify Satan’s promise because it is a hope, not a proof. The sūrah has shown that God’s promise — *“We will admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow forever; God’s promise is always true, whose word is more truthful than God’s?”* (4:122) — is tied to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40); Satan’s promise is tied to loss manifest.
verses.121:
> It is they who will have Hell as their home, and they will find no escape from it

**They Will Have Hell as Home**

The verse states *ulāʾika maʾwāhum Jahannam* — it is they — those who take Satan as guardian instead of God (4:119), who follow his promises that are only delusion (4:120), who invoke female gods besides Him (4:117) — whose refuge, shelter, home is Hell, *Jahannam*. *Maʾwā* — refuge, shelter, place of return — was explained as the home that receives, as the emigrant finds *murāgham* — many havens — and abundance where God’s earth is spacious (4:100), while these find *maʾwā* as Hell, the inverse haven. The sūrah has used *maʾwā* for the self-wronger who remained where earth was wide — Hell as home, evil destination (4:97) — and for the defier left to what he chose — burning, evil destination (4:115). Here the pronoun *ulāʾika* — it is they — restricts to Satan’s share — the appointed portion he claimed (4:118). *Jahannam* was read as the Fire where skins are replaced to taste punishment (4:56), where the intentional killer abides with anger and curse (4:93), where the prepared torment is humiliating for disbelievers who would sweep upon neglect (4:102). To have Hell as *maʾwā* means it is not a passing visit but the place of stay, as Gardens are *maʾwā* for those who believe and do good who stay forever (4:122).

**And They Will Find No Escape From It**

The clause *wa lā yajidūna ʿanhā maḥīṣā* — and they will find no escape, no flight, no diversion from it — was explained with *maḥīṣ* — escape, refuge from, place to incline away. *Lā yajidūna* — they will not find — contrasts with the emigrant’s *yajid* — will find — many havens (4:100) and the helpless hoped to be pardoned where finding was impossible (4:98–99). *ʿAnhā* — from it, away from it — was read as Hell’s encompassing: there is no *murāgham* from Hell, no spaciousness away from it, because the curse that took Satan as guardian cut off the only guardian who could provide escape — *“whoever takes Satan as guardian instead of God suffers tremendous loss”* (4:119) — and promises only delusion (4:120). The sūrah has said that the wronged who sought *murāgham* found it (4:100) and that prayer at fixed time (4:103) is the writ that secures times; Hell without *maḥīṣ* is the writ that secures consequence where promise was delusion. *Lā yajidūna maḥīṣā* was also compared to *“they will not find protector or helper besides God”* for whoever commits evil (4:123): no *walī* and no *naṣīr*, no escape, no diversion.

**No Escape Because No Guardian Was Taken**

The phrase *wa lā yajidūna ʿanhā maḥīṣā* was explained as consequence of taking Satan as *walī* (4:119). The sūrah has repeated that God is enough as Guardian and Helper (4:45), that the oppressed cry for a guardian and helper from grace (4:75), that the Messenger ﷺ is told to put trust in Him as Trustee (4:81, 4:132). To take Satan as *walī* instead of Him is to choose a guardian who was cursed (4:118) and whose promise is delusion (4:120). On the Day where advocates in this life will find no advocate before God (4:109), there will be no *maḥīṣ* because the only *walī* and *naṣīr* who could provide it was rejected. Classical notes added that *maḥīṣ* — escape place — matches *murāgham* — haven — as both are places of turning; the emigrant who turned to God finds many turnings, the follower of Satan who turned to him finds none. The sūrah that promised the emigrant his reward secured even if death overtakes (4:100) here promises the follower of Satan his loss secured where death overtakes into Hell.
verses.122:
> And those who believe and do good, We will soon admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true. And whose word is more truthful than Allah’s

**Those Who Believe and Do Good — Into Gardens Forever**

The verse states *wa alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti sa nudkhiluhum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhāru khālidīna fīhā abadan* — and those who believe and do good, do righteous, We will soon admit them into Gardens — orchards, enclosed gardens — under which rivers flow, to stay there forever and ever — *abadan*. *Āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt* — faith and righteous deeds — was explained as the sūrah’s shorthand for the faithful: opposed to those who take Satan as guardian (4:119), who invoke others besides Him (4:117), who follow other than believers’ path (4:115). Who will have Hell without escape (4:121). *Sa nudkhiluhum* — We will soon admit, We will enter — was read as divine assurance that admission is from Us, as the emigrant’s reward falls upon God secure (4:100) and as forgiveness is found upon seeking (4:110). *Jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhāru* — Gardens under which rivers flow — was explained as the sūrah’s repeated promise: the same phrase as for those who believe and do good earlier (4:57) and as for the obedient limits-keeping (4:13). *Khālidīna fīhā abadan* — staying in it forever and ever — was read with double emphasis — *khālidīn* and *abadan* — unlike *khālidan* alone for the intentional killer (4:93) or the self-wronger’s Hell (4:97): for belief and good, abiding is forever and ever with no exit. Hell’s abiding is also described without *maḥīṣ* (4:121), keeping the symmetry that each *maʾwā* is lasting in its direction.

**God’s Promise Is Always True**

The affirmation *waʿda Allāhi ḥaqqan* — God’s promise as truth, truly, as right — was explained as the contrast to Satan’s promise that is nothing but delusion (4:120). *Waʿd Allāh* — God’s promise — was read as His word that Gardens are for the faithful, that good is multiplied, that ranks, forgiveness. Mercy are from Him (4:96), that many havens are found (4:100), that prayer at fixed time is writ (4:103), that whoever seeks finds forgiveness (4:110). *Ḥaqqan* — truly, as truth, as right, as due — was explained as that the promise corresponds to reality, not wish, unlike empty wishes that claim grace by belonging (4:123). The sūrah has said that the Book was sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* (4:105) — to judge by what He shows; to say His promise is *ḥaqq* is to say judgment by it will be true, as *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40). Where Satan orders cutting and altering (4:119) promising honour, God’s promise to keep creation intact ends in Gardens whose rivers flow under, not cut away.

**A Verse That Completes the Contrast of Two Maws**

Placed after Hell as home without escape (4:121), this verse completes the contrast of two *maʾwās* — refuges — the sūrah has built since the angels’ question about spacious earth (4:97). One branch — helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99), emigrant finds many havens (4:100), traveller shortens and guards prayer (4:101–102), remembers in all postures (4:103), pursues without faltering for hope (4:104), judges by Book (4:105) — ends in Gardens forever whose promise is truth. The other — invoking others, following Satan, accepting his appointed share, cutting creation, hoping his empty hope (4:117–120) — ends in Hell without *maḥīṣ*. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to follow other than believers’ path (4:115) here shows that the two paths end in two homes whose endurance was named with the same verb — *khālid* — yet opposite quality: one as mercy — *Ghafūr Raḥīm* — one as humiliation prepared (4:102). For the weak the verse is the lightest of weights: belief and good, which the sūrah elsewhere defines as faith in God, Messenger, Books, angels, Last Day without distinction (4:136, 4:152) together with doing what is maʿrūf — charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) — is tied to an always-true promise, while Satan’s promise is nothing but delusion.
verses.123:
> ˹Divine grace is˺ neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book! Whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly, and they will find no protector or helper besides Allah

**Neither by Your Wishes Nor Those of the People of the Book**

The verse opens *laysa bi amāniyyikum wa lā amāniy ahla al-kitābi* — Divine grace — matter, recompense — is neither by your wishes nor wishes of the People of the Book. *Amāniy* — wishes, fancies, empty hopes — was explained as the *tamannī* — wishing — already unmasked as Satan’s delusion — *yummanīhim* (4:119–120) — and as the human wish that grace be by claim. The sūrah has shown wishes that mislead — those who wish you deviate greatly (4:27), who wish you alike in disbelief (4:89), who wish you neglect weapons for a sweep (4:102) — here it says neither set of wishes governs divine grace. *Laysa bi amāniyyikum* — not by your, Muslims’, wishes — was read as addressing the companions who might count on belief alone while committing evil. *wa lā amāniyyi ahla al-kitābi* — nor by People of the Book’s wishes — as addressing Jews and Christians who claimed *“we are God’s children”* or *“none enters Paradise except our group.”* The sūrah has said that the People of the Book demanded a written revelation from heaven and were struck for wrongdoing (4:153) and that some Jews distort words (4:46); both groups’ wishes are set aside.

**Whoever Commits Evil Will Be Rewarded Accordingly**

The rule *man yaʿmal sūʾan yujza bihī* — whoever commits, does, evil will be rewarded, recompensed accordingly, with it — was explained as the ledger law already given — *whoever earns sin earns only upon himself* (4:111) and *whoever earns evil or sin then throws on innocent bears slander* (4:112) — now as recompense law for all. *Sūʾ* — evil — was read broadly: associating, falling to Satan’s promises, hidden night plotting, devouring wealth, killing a believer, throwing sin. *Yujza bihī* — will be recompensed with it, rewarded accordingly — was explained as exact recompense — *jazāʾ* — the same root for the intentional killer’s *jazāʾ* is Hell (4:93) and for the believer’s *jazāʾ* is Gardens (4:122). The sūrah has said *“God does not wrong even an atom; if it is good He multiplies many times”* (4:40) — punishment is according, reward is multiplied — so *yujza bihī* is the atom-measured side. The pronoun *bihī* — with it, by this — was read as equivalence: the evil’s own weight as recompense, not another’s, not less than atom. The Book’s promise being true (4:122) and whose word more truthful (4:122) was linked here: to say *yujza bihī* is the Most Truthful’s word about consequence, not a wish.

**And They Will Find No Protector or Helper Besides God**

The closure *wa lā yajid lahū min dūni Allāhi waliyyan wa lā naṣīrā* — and they will find for themselves no protector, guardian, nor helper besides God — was explained with *walī* and *naṣīr* — the same pair the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45). That the self-wronger’s advocate cannot provide on the Day (4:109). *Min dūni Allāhi* — besides God, apart from Him, short of Him — was read as the failure of every alternative guardian: clan, People of the Book status, female gods invoked (4:117), Satan the rebellious guardian (4:119) whose promise is delusion, whose abode is Hell without *maḥīṣ* (4:121). To find no *walī* and no *naṣīr* where evil is committed and not sought away (4:110) is the law’s complement to *“whoever seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving, Most Merciful”* — the only *walī* and *naṣīr* besides Him that could rescue is none. The sūrah has warned *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers”* (4:139, 4:144) and *“do not take them as allies unless they emigrate”* (4:89); here the ally beside God is declared absent where evil is choice.

The sūrah has said that to Allah belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware (4:126, 4:131–132), and that He is enough as Trustee (4:132); recompense *bihī* is therefore not by your computation but by His awareness, yet measured exact as not wronging an atom.
verses.124:
> But those who do good—whether male or female—and have faith will enter Paradise and will never be wronged ˹even as much as˺ the speck on a date stone

**Those Who Do Good — Male or Female — With Faith**

The verse states *wa man yaʿmal mina al-ṣāliḥāti min dhakarin aw unthā wa huwa muʾminun fa ulāʾika yadkhulūna al-jannata* — but those who do, who act, righteous deeds from among good acts — whether male or female — and are believers, while being faithful — will enter Paradise. *Man yaʿmal mina al-ṣāliḥāt* — whoever does righteous deeds — was explained as the Book’s shorthand for the faithful act: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114), standing firm for justice though against selves (4:135), spending from what God provided not to show off (4:38–40), striving with wealth and lives (4:95) and the good whose reward is multiplied many times over (4:40). *Min dhakarin aw unthā* — whether male or female — was read as the sūrah’s consistent equalisation where the single soul spread into countless men and women (4:1), where shares for men and women are obligatory (4:7, 4:11–12), where marry-able bonds include the believing bondwoman where harm is feared (4:25). Where helpless men, women, children are each named for pardon and for haven (4:98, 4:75).
