To name both was to remove the wish that grace is by belonging — *neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — and to place it on act plus faith. *Wa huwa muʾmin* — while being faithful. He is a believer — was stressed: good alone without faith is not the entry described, as *“O believers, have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He sent”* (4:136) commands renewal of faith as basis; the sūrah has shown that association is not forgiven (4:116) because it breaks the faith itself.

**And Will Never Be Wronged Even as Speck on a Date Stone**

The assurance *wa lā yuẓlamūna naqīrā* — and they will never be wronged even as much as the speck, the groove, on a date stone — was explained with *naqīr* — the tiny pit, speck on the stone’s back, the small hollow — the sūrah’s smallest measure. The same measure appeared where envy wishes deviation and God’s kingdom share would not give even a speck (4:53) and where enjoyment of world is little and none will be wronged even by speck (4:77) and where those given understanding do good will not be wronged (4:49). *Lā yuẓlamūna* — never be wronged — was read with the sūrah’s principle *“God does not wrong even an atom; if it is good He multiplies”* (4:40): not wronging is baseline, multiplying is grace. The sūrah has also said that whoever earns sin earns only upon himself (4:111) and whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly with no protector besides Him (4:123); here the complement is that whoever does good with faith will not be wronged even to a speck’s weight.

**A Verse That Follows Recompense According With Reward Without Wrong**

Placed after *whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides God* (4:123), this verse follows recompense with reward without wrong. The sūrah has moved from two homes — Hell without escape (4:121) and Gardens forever where promise is true (4:122) — through the rule of wishes — neither yours nor theirs (4:123) — to the entry — *they will enter Paradise and not be wronged a speck* (4:124). The symmetry was noted: evil is rewarded *bihī* — with it, exactly — and no *walī* besides Him rescues; good is rewarded into Paradise and not wronged even a speck, with His promise true whose speech none exceeds (4:122). Where the sūrah says *“do not consume wealth unjustly; trade by mutual consent”* (4:29) and says taking dowry unjustly bears sin (4:20), working good with faith is the trade by mutual consent with Him where no wronging occurs. The verse was also placed against the sūrah’s warning not to crave what God gave some over others but to ask of His bounties (4:32): the speck not wronged is the bounty asked and given without envy.
verses.125:
> And who is better in faith than those who ˹fully˺ submit themselves to Allah, do good, and follow the Way of Abraham, the upright? Allah chose Abraham as a close friend

**Who Is Better in Faith Than Those Who Submit and Do Good**

The verse opens *wa man aḥsanu dīnan mimman aslama wajhahū li Allāhi wa huwa muḥsinun wa attabaʿa millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* — and who is better in faith, in religion, than those who fully submit their face, themselves, to God and are doers of good. Follow the Way of Abraham, the upright. *Man aḥsanu dīnan* — who is better in religion, in faith — was explained as rhetorical negation: none is better, as earlier *who is more truthful than God in speech?* (4:87, 4:122). *Aslama wajhahū li Allāhi* — submitted his face to God — was read as full submission, face as the noblest part and the direction of prayer, as the sūrah commands *“submit yourselves to God”* in trust. *Wa huwa muḥsin* — while being doer of good, beautiful in deed — was explained as *iḥsān* — doing good, making good, worship as if seeing — the same *muḥsin* who does charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114) and who does good male or female with faith (4:124). *Wa attabaʿa millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* — and follows the way, the creed, the community of Abraham, the upright, the inclining from crooked to straight — was read as the *ḥanīf* — pure monotheist who turns away from associators, as Abraham turned from his people’s female gods (4:117) and obeyed command without altering creation (4:119). The three — submission, goodness, following Abraham pure — were explained as the sūrah’s definition of best *dīn*, against wishes that claimed grace by belonging (4:123) and against taking Satan as guardian instead of God (4:119).

**The Way of Abraham the Upright**

The phrase *millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* was explained with history. *Millah* — way, creed, path — was read as the path God made clear as noble ways of those before you (4:26), which Abraham exemplifies. *Ḥanīf* — upright, inclining, pure — was explained as one who inclines from associating (4:116) to the Single, as Abraham was not of the associators (6:161) and was tested with commands and fulfilled them (2:124). The sūrah has said that the People of the Book claim wishes yet some distort words (4:46, 4:153) and that the Qur’an came confirming your scriptures (4:47); following Abraham *ḥanīf* was read as return to the common monotheism before distortions, where invocation is only of God, not female gods nor Satan (4:117). The Way of Abraham was also linked to *“We have given descendants of Abraham the Book and wisdom and great authority”* (4:54) and to *“He chose Abraham as close friend”* here — Abraham’s way is not tribal claim but submitted face and beautiful deed, the same *islām* that began from a single soul’s creation (4:1) and that remains spacious as earth’s havens (4:100).

**A Verse That Answers Wishes With Abraham’s Submission**

Placed after *those who do good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck* (4:124) and before *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware* (4:126), this verse answers wishes with Abraham’s submission. The sūrah removed *“neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book, whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) and gave Paradise by belief and good without wrong (4:124). Now it asks *who is better than the submitter, the doer of good, the follower of Abraham ḥanīf?* — answer: none. The sūrah has shown Satan’s path — defying the Messenger after guidance (4:115), associating far astray (4:116), invoking females/Satan (4:117), cursed taking share (4:118), ordering cutting and altering (4:119), promising only delusion (4:120) — versus God’s path — Book in truth (4:105), wisdom taught (4:113), no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114). Abraham is the human embodiment of God’s path, who left his people’s idols, submitted face to fire, and was made *khalīl*. For the weak this is an accessible model: best *dīn* is not speculation about wishes but submission of face, beautification of deed, and following the upright way whose owner owns heavens and earth.

**The Friend of God**

*Khalīl* names a friendship that has taken hold of the whole heart. When the companions wished the rank for him, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Had I taken a *khalīl* among you I would have taken Abū Bakr, but your companion is God's *khalīl*" (al-Bukhārī 466; Muslim 2383). The report shows that the station is not inherited or claimed; God chooses. Abraham's honour answers exactly what this verse describes — submission of the face and doing good — so the title is not a privilege that closes the road, but a mark that shows where the road leads.
verses.126:
> To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Fully Aware of everything

**To God Alone Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth**

The verse states *wa li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — and to God, for God, belongs whatever, all that, is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. *Mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — whatever is in heavens and on earth — was explained as absolute ownership: angels nearest to Him who would never be too proud to be servants (4:172), the Messiah a servant not too proud (4:172), the single soul spread into humanity (4:1), the orphans’ wealth held as trust (4:2, 4:10), the women whose dowries are gracious (4:4), the inheritance shares appointed (4:11–12), the earth made spacious for emigration (4:100), the prayer shortened on travel (4:101). The promise true whose abode is Gardens or Hell (4:122, 4:121). *Li Allāhi* — to Him, for Him — was read as exclusive belonging, as the sūrah repeats *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:131, 4:132, 4:170) to bracket the passage on women, reconciliation, and trusteeship. The phrase was explained as the reply to invoking female gods besides Him (4:117) — they belong to Him, not beside Him — and to taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119) — the guardian taken belongs to Him, cursed (4:118). The sūrah has said that the People of the Book claim wishes yet grace is not by wishes (4:123), that Abraham was taken as close friend (4:125) — friendship with the Owner of all is the highest honour — and that whoever desires world’s reward, with Him are both worlds’ rewards (4:134); ownership here is the ground of those promises.

**And God Is Fully Aware of Everything**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu bi kulli shayʾin muḥīṭā* — And God is Fully Aware, Encompassing, of everything, of every thing — was explained as *muḥīṭ* — encompassing, encircling, comprehending — the same name that sealed night plotting in His presence — *He is Fully Aware of what they do* (4:108) — now universalised to *bi kulli shayʾ* — of everything. *Bi kulli shayʾin* — of every thing — was read as covering the heavens and earth just said to belong to Him, the charity and kindness and reconciliation commanded (4:114), the dispute judged by what He shows (4:105), the good male or female with faith (4:124). The speck not wronging (*naqīrā* — 4:124) and the atom not wronging (4:40). The sūrah has sealed knowledge diversely — All-Knowing, All-Wise where sin is earned (4:111), All-Hearing, All-Seeing where trusts are judged (4:58), All-Aware of what you do where verification was commanded (4:94), *Muḥīṭ* where night hides (4:108) — here *Muḥīṭ* of everything gathers them: nothing escapes perimeter because everything belongs. Early notes linked *muḥīṭ* to spaciousness: earth was said to be spacious (4:97, 4:100), yet His awareness is more spacious, encompassing the spacious.

**Ownership That Makes Wishes Void and Promises True**

The pairing — *to Him belongs* and *He encompasses everything* — was explained as making *“neither by your wishes”* (4:123) void and *“God’s promise ever true, whose word more truthful?”* (4:122) true. The sūrah has moved from two abodes — Hell without escape (4:121) and Gardens forever true (4:122) — through the law of wishes, through the entry of doers of good with faith not wronged a speck (4:124), through best faith as submission to Owner and following Abraham whom Owner took as friend — to the Owner’s declaration that all belongs and all is encompassed. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, the declaration is lightening: the One to whom your weak *ḥīlah* and *sabīl* were unknown to others (4:98) is the One who owns heavens and earth and encompasses. Your helplessness hoped to be pardoned (4:99) and your emigration where you find many havens (4:100) and your prayer shortened (4:101) are under the same Ownership. The next passage will use that ownership to teach about women: they ask about women, say He instructs you about them, instruction already revealed about orphan women deprived yet wished to marry, helpless children, orphans’ rights, and whatever good you do is well known to Him (4:127).
verses.127:
> They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding women. Say, “It is Allah Who instructs you regarding them. Instruction has ˹already˺ been revealed in the Book concerning the orphan women you deprive of their due rights but still wish to marry, also helpless children, as well as standing up for orphans’ rights. And whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah.”

**They Ask You Regarding Women — God Instructs**

The verse states *wa yastaftūnaka fī al-nisāʾi quli Allāhu yuftīkum fīhinna* — they ask you, they seek your ruling, about women — say, God instructs you, gives ruling, about them. *Yastaftūnaka* — to seek *fatwā*, ruling — was explained as the community asking the Prophet ﷺ about women’s rights, as earlier at the chapter’s start they were taught to marry orphan women with justice or marry others two, three, four where justice is feared (4:3), to give dowries graciously (4:4). To return orphans’ property with witnesses (4:6). *Quli Allāhu yuftīkum fīhinna* — say, God gives ruling about them — was read as referral to the Owner to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and who is Fully Aware of everything (4:126). Instruction is not by wishes (4:123) nor by Satan’s ordering to alter creation (4:119), but by the One who created from a single soul and spread men and women (4:1). The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent in truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and that wisdom was taught (4:113); here the Book judges between men and women as between peoples. Early reports linked the asking to questions about orphan girls under guardianship where the guardian desired to marry them without full dowry; the verse ties past instruction to present asking, showing a single instruction extended.

**Also Helpless Children and Standing Up for Orphans’ Rights**

The continuation *wa al-mustaḍʿafīna mina al-wildāni wa a taqūmū li al-yatāmā bi al-qisṭ* — also helpless children, also that you stand up, establish, for orphans with justice — was explained as the same inclusive justice seen where men, women, children were named for pardon and haven (4:98, 4:75). *Mustaḍʿafīn mina al-wildān* — helpless among children, deemed weak children — were those without guardian, whose shares hypocrites might diminish. *Wa a taqūmū li al-yatāmā bi al-qisṭ* — and that you stand up for orphans with equity, with justice, with the balance — was read as the command to *return trusts, judge fairly* (4:58) applied to orphans as the prime trust: the sūrah that warns against devouring orphans’ wealth as fire in bellies (4:10) and that commands to test orphans until judicious then return property with witnesses (4:6) here generalizes: stand up — *qūmū* — as you stand for prayer at appointed time (4:103) and for justice though against yourselves (4:135). The sūrah has said that God is enough as Witness and Trustee (4:132, 4:79); to stand for orphans *bi al-qisṭ* is to stand with Him as witness.

**And Whatever Good You Do Is Well Known to God**

The seal *wa mā tafʿalū min khayrin fa inna Allāha kāna bihī ʿalīmā* — and whatever good you do, of good, then indeed God is, was ever, All-Knowing of it — was explained as the encouragement matching the warning. *Mā tafʿalū min khayr* — whatever good you do — was read as the good commanded for secret talks — charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) — and the good of submitting face to Him doing good as Abraham (4:125) and the good male or female with faith entering Paradise without wrong of speck (4:124). *Fa inna Allāha kāna bihī ʿalīmā* — He is All-Knowing of it — was explained as that He who owns heavens and earth (4:126) and is Fully Aware of everything knows the speck of good as He knows the speck not wronged (*naqīrā* — 4:124) and does not wrong even an atom but multiplies (4:40). The sūrah has said *“you do not know who is more beneficial”* among parents and children (4:11); here *He* knows the good done for orphan women deprived yet desired, for helpless children, for orphans stood for.

The circle closes where the sūrah began with orphans’ wealth and marriage justice (4:2–4). The question reopens it, and the answer cites the earlier verses as still recited, still ruling, so that the chapter’s ethic — return trusts, judge fairly, verify reports, be sure before fighting, do not advocate for deceit — is again applied to the household.
verses.128:
> If a woman fears indifference or neglect from her husband, there is no blame on either of them if they seek ˹fair˺ settlement, which is best. Humans are ever inclined to selfishness. But if you are gracious and mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do

The verse opens *wa in imraʾatun khāfat min baʿlihā nushūzan aw iʿrāḍā fa lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā a yuṣliḥā baynahumā ṣulḥā* — and if a woman fears, anticipates, from her husband perverseness, rising — *nushūz* — or neglect, turning away — *iʿrāḍ* — then no blame upon them both to seek, to effect, settlement, reconciliation between them, a settlement. *Khāfat* — feared — was explained as sensed, apprehended, with signs, as earlier *if you fear ill conduct* from women advice and measures were given (4:34) and *if you anticipate a split appoint mediators* (4:35) — fear here is the moral perception that precedes action, not mere anxiety. *Nushūz* — rising, perverseness, elevation — was read as the husband’s rising above, being high, refusing right; *iʿrāḍ* — turning aside, neglect — as withdrawal, not sharing bed, not intending, leaving hanging (4:129). *Fa lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā* — no blame upon them both — was explained as the law’s lightening where shortening prayer carries no blame (4:101), where laying aside weapons in rain carries no blame though precaution remains (4:102). Where standing for orphans must be with justice (4:127) — here settlement carries no sin nor blame. The sūrah has said that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114); settlement is that reconciliation.

**Settlement — Which Is Best**

The affirmation *wa al-ṣulḥu khayr* — and settlement, reconciliation, is best, is good, is better — was explained as the sūrah’s maxim for dispute. *Al-ṣulḥ* — settlement — was read as the peace that mends, the *iṣlāḥ bayna al-nāsi* commanded as good secret talk (4:114) and as the mediators’ goal (4:35). *Khayr* — best, good — was explained as better than splitting where the woman fears *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* yet a fair settlement keeps ties honoured (4:1), as the single soul’s creation spread into families whose ties are to be honoured. The phrase was linked to *“appoint a mediator from his family and hers, if they desire reconciliation God will bring harmony”* (4:35): settlement is not the enemy of justice but its embodiment where justice is equity plus mercy. The sūrah has said humans crave what God gave some over others (4:32) and that burdens are lightened because weak (4:28); to prefer settlement where the alternative is hanging is to prefer the light, kind path where the writ of prayer still holds at fixed time (4:103). Classical notes added that *al-ṣulḥu khayr* is general: wherever reconciliation is possible, it is best, provided rights prescribed for orphan women (4:127) are not voided.

**But If You Are Gracious and Mindful — God Is All-Aware**

The encouragement *wa in tuḥsinū wa tattaqū fa inna Allāha kāna bi mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — but if you do good, act graciously, beautifully. Are mindful of God, then indeed God was ever All-Aware of what you do — was explained with *tuḥsinū* — to do *iḥsān*, to be gracious, to do good beautifully — the same *muḥsin* who submits face and does good following Abraham (4:125) and who does good male or female with faith (4:124). *Wa tattaqū* — and are mindful, God-wary — was read as the sūrah’s *taqwā* that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) and that seals settlement between spouses (4:129) — if you do what is right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. *Fa inna Allāha kāna bi mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — He is Ever Aware of what you do — was explained as that He who owns heavens and earth (4:126) and knows whatever good you do (4:127) is aware of the settlement sought, of the selfishness present, of the graciousness where offered. The sūrah has sealed knowledge diversely — *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* where sin is earned (4:111), *Muḥīṭ* where night plots (4:108), *Khabīr* where verification was commanded (4:94) — here *Khabīr* fits act: He is aware of what you do in settlement where your doing is waiving and being gracious.
verses.129:
> You will never be able to maintain ˹emotional˺ justice between your wives—no matter how keen you are. So do not totally incline towards one leaving the other in suspense. And if you do what is right and are mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful

**So Do Not Incline Entirely, Leaving the Other Suspended**

The command *fa lā tamīlū kulla al-mayli fa tadharūhā ka al-muʿallaqah* — so do not incline, lean, completely, with total inclining. That you leave her as the suspended, hanging — was explained with *mayl* — inclination, leaning, bias — the same *mayl* the hostile wished you deviate — *mayl ʿaẓīmā* — greatly (4:27) and where night plotting wished you neglect for a sweep — *maylatan wāḥidah* (4:102). *Kulla al-mayli* — completely of inclination — was read as total turning to one and away from another: not sharing nights, not providing, not speaking, so that the wife remains *muʿallaqah* — suspended, hanging — neither married in full nor divorced free, as if tied to a rope without ground. *Fa tadharūhā ka al-muʿallaqah* — so you leave her as the hanging one — was explained as the sūrah’s protection of the wife who earlier feared *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* (4:128): the remedy there was settlement where both sought it, which is best. Here the remedy is prohibition of total inclining that creates the hanging. The sūrah elsewhere says *“do not incline towards one leaving the other in suspense”* is the counterpart to *“be mindful of God”* where settlement was taught with *shuḥḥ* present (4:128); not to incline completely is to practice *taqwā* where love cannot be equal.

The encouragement *wa in tuṣliḥū wa tattaqū fa inna Allāha kāna Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — and if you set right, reconcile, do good. Are mindful, then indeed God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, was ever — was explained with *tuṣliḥū* — to set right, to reconcile, to do good — the same *iṣlāḥ* as reconciliation between people (4:114) and mediators desiring reconciliation (4:35) and settlement best (4:128). *Wa tattaqū* — and are mindful, God-wary — was read as the sūrah’s *taqwā* that began with mindfulness of the Lord who created from single soul (4:1) and that seals every marriage rule: where emotional justice is impossible yet legal justice is commanded, mindfulness and setting right cover the shortfall. *Fa inna Allāha kāna Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful — was explained as the Seal that excuses what you cannot equalise while holding you to what you can — not to incline completely. Where the intentional killer was sealed with anger and curse (4:93) and the self-wronger with not loved (4:107), the husband who cannot equalise love yet does not incline totally and is gracious and mindful is sealed with forgiveness and mercy. The same pair sealed the fear that settlement requires graciousness where *shuḥḥ* is present (4:128) with awareness — *Khabīr* — here with mercy, matching the earlier limit of justice where the sūrah says *“do not crave what God gave some over others. Ask Him for bounty”* (4:32): what you cannot equalise, seek from His forgiveness.

**A Verse That Places Limit Beside Permission**

Placed after settlement is best where she fears *nushūz* or turning away and selves were made present with *shuḥḥ* (4:128), this verse places limit beside permission. The sūrah permitted settlement waiving part of right to keep marriage; here it acknowledges that perfect equalising of hearts after settlement remains impossible. The two verses together teach the household ethic after the public ethic of judging by Book (4:105) and most secret talks (4:114): private settlement is best, yet private hearts remain unequal, so do not make inequality total. The sūrah has shown that the owner of heavens and earth is Fully Aware of everything (4:126) and Whatever good you do is well known to Him (4:127). He knows the inclination you cannot weigh and He is All-Forgiving for it where you do not incline completely and you set right and are mindful. For the weak this is protective: the wife suspended — *muʿallaqah* — is named as a wrong to be avoided, as orphan women deprived were protected from being married for profit (4:3, 4:127); protection is by prohibition of total inclining.
verses.130:
> But if they choose to separate, Allah will enrich both of them from His bounties. And Allah is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise

**But If They Separate — He Will Enrich Both**

The verse states *wa in yatafarraqā yughni Allāhu kullan min saʿatihī* — but if they two separate, become separate, part, God will enrich, make free of need, each from His bounty, His spaciousness, His abundance. *Yatafarraqā* — to separate, to split, to become distinct — was explained as divorce or separation after settlement was best (4:128) yet total inclining was prohibited (4:129) — where remaining together in hanging was not chosen and settlement could not hold. *Yughni* — to enrich, to suffice, to make independent — was read as God making each free of need where the other was expected to suffice, as the emigrant finds many havens and abundance where earth is spacious (4:100) and as the prayer shortened on travel is still writ at fixed time (4:103). *Kullan* — each, both, every one — was explained as each — the man and the woman — not only the husband upon whom maintenance lay nor only the wife who feared *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* (4:128); both are enriched. *Min saʿatihī* — from His spaciousness, His bounty, His amplitude — was explained as from His wide provision, the same *saʿah* as *murāgham kathīr wa saʿah* — many havens and spaciousness — promised to the emigrant (4:100). As *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131) whose spaciousness is the source.

**From His Bounties — Min Saʿatihī**

The phrase *min saʿatihī* was explained as from His amplitude that does not narrow when given, as the sūrah says *“ask God for His bounties. God has perfect knowledge of all things”* (4:32) where craving what others have is forbidden — here bounty is given to both from His bounty, not from taking between them. *Saʿah* — spaciousness — was read as breadth of provision, of dwelling, of tranquillity, of replacement — spouse, household, sustenance — as the sūrah says the single soul spread into countless men and women (4:1) showing that earth’s spaciousness holds replacements. The contrast with *shuḥḥ* — selfishness ever present with souls (4:128) — was noted: where settlement failed because *shuḥḥ* kept each grasping, separation enriched from *saʿah* removes grasping by giving each from Him, not by stripping one. Where the sūrah warns there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), separation where graciousness and mindfulness remain is itself counted as good where it removes hanging — *muʿallaqah* (4:129) — and enrichment from *saʿah* is the broad good that follows.

**The Wide Who Can Replace Without Diminishing**

The verb *yughni* — to enrich, to suffice — was linked to *“ask God for His bounties”* (4:32) and to *“with Him are rewards of this world and the Hereafter”* (4:134): the enrichment promised here is not a vague hope but a writ from the Wide. Classical notes added that *kullan min saʿatihī* — each from His bounty — proves that provision is not zero-sum between the two who part: His *saʿah* gives to each separately, as *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* (4:126) — so that the woman enriched is not enriched at man’s expense before God, though inter-human rights remain judged fairly as the Book judges (4:105, 4:135). The next passage will anchor that bounty in universal ownership: to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, We have commanded those given Scripture before you and you to be mindful, if you disobey to Him still belongs all, and He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131).
verses.131:
> To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, We have commanded those given the Scripture before you, as well as you, to be mindful of Allah. But if you disobey, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy

The verse opens *wa li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — and to God belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — repeated from 4:126 and to be repeated at 4:132, bracketing the passage on settlement and enrichment. *Mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — whatever is in heavens and on earth — was explained as absolute ownership encompassing the single soul spread into humanity (4:1), the orphans’ trusts (4:2), the dowries (4:4), the inheritance shares (4:11–12), the earth made spacious (4:100), the wives between whom justice cannot be perfected (4:129) yet whose separation is enriched from His bounty (4:130). *Wa la qad waṣṣaynā alladhīna ūtū al-kitāba min qablikum wa iyyākum ani ittaqū Allāh* — and indeed We have commanded, commanded, charged those given Scripture before you, as well as you, to be mindful of God — was explained as universal *waṣiyyah* — counsel, charge — the same mindfulness that began the sūrah — *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) — and that seals settlement — *“if you are gracious and mindful God is All-Aware”* (4:128) — and seals not inclining completely — *“if you set right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving”* (4:129). To command those given Scripture before you and you was read as continuity: the Scriptures before and the Qur’an command the same *taqwā*, as *“We have given descendants of Abraham the Book and wisdom and great authority”* (4:54) and *“He taught you what you did not know, great is His favour”* (4:113) — the teaching is one.

**A Verse That Brackets Settlement With Ownership and Command**

Placed after enrichment from His bounty where they separate and He is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise (4:130), this verse brackets settlement with ownership and universal command. The sūrah has moved from orphan women deprived yet desired, helpless children, orphans stood for with justice well known to Him (4:127) → wife fearing *nushūz* or turning away, settlement best though selves were made present with *shuḥḥ* yet graciousness and mindfulness are ever known (4:128) → impossibility of perfect emotional justice, prohibition of total inclining leaving hanging, setting right and mindfulness forgiven (4:129) → separation enriched from His spaciousness (4:130) — here to ground all in *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful, if you disobey to Him still belongs all, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy*. The sūrah that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* returns to *be mindful* as its abiding *waṣiyyah* for every Scripture people.

Where the deceitful hide from people but He is with them where they plot displeasing speech (4:108) and where night plotting seems to succeed in this life but not before Him on the Day (4:109), the *waṣiyyah* to be mindful is the daylight that night cannot void, because the Night’s owner is the One commanded mindfulness. The verse generalises the household law into the order of the universe: the same heavens and earth that belong to Him contain both the single soul spread (4:1) and the many havens for emigration (4:100), the prayer at fixed writ (4:103) and the two abodes true (4:121–122). To be mindful within them is to live inside ownership that is Self-Sufficient yet Praiseworthy, so that obedience adds no need and disobedience subtracts nothing except from the disobedient.
verses.132:
> To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs

**To God Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth — Again**

The verse restates *wa li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — and to God belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — the third repetition after 4:126 and 4:131, sealing the passage on women, settlement, enrichment. Universal *waṣiyyah* to be mindful. *Mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* was explained to include the same all as before: the single soul and its mate (4:1), the orphans’ wealth, the dowries, the shares, the earth spacious for haven (4:100), the wives between whom inclination is limited (4:129) yet each enriched from His bounty upon separation (4:130). The heavens under which the fear prayer was ranked with vigilance (4:102). To repeat ownership thrice was read as emphasis after law: where the chapter legislates for the weakest — the orphan girl deprived yet desired (4:127), the wife fearing *nushūz* where settlement is best (4:128), the hanging not left (4:129) — the Legislation is grounded in Ownership. That no wish (4:123) and no Satanic order to slit and alter (4:119) can claim title. The sūrah has said that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); to judge by that showing is to judge within His ownership, as witnesses for justice though against yourselves (4:135). Early reports noted that the Meccan assignment of daughters as female gods besides Him (4:117) and the claim of Satan’s appointed share (4:118) are both answered here: they belong to Him.

**And God Is Sufficient as Trustee of Affairs**

The seal *wa kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* — And God is enough, enough, as Trustee, as *Wakīl*, as Disposer of affairs, Agent — was explained with *wakīl* — trustee, agent, defender, disposer — the same *wakīl* asked about on the Day — *who will be their *wakīl*?* (4:109) — and the *wakīl* the Prophet ﷺ was told to trust — *“put trust in God, God is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:81) after turning away from night contradictors. *Kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* was read as that His trusteeship suffices for every affair where spouses fear, orphans are stood for, emigrants seek haven, prayers guard. The sūrah has sealed trusteeship diversely: enough as Guardian and Helper (4:45), enough as Helper where He knows enemies (4:45), enough as Trustee after recording night schemes (4:81); here *enough as Trustee* fits ownership — because to Him belongs all, He suffices to dispose all. To take Him as *wakīl* was explained as entrusting affairs after doing what is incumbent: settlement sought (4:128), total inclining avoided (4:129), separation where needed enriched from His bounty (4:130), mindfulness kept where commanded (4:131). Where deceitful advocates seek to be *khaṣīm* for self-wrongers in this life (4:107–109) and find no *wakīl* on the Day for deceit, the believer who seeks settlement graciously finds the *Wakīl* who suffices.

**Sufficiency That Makes Wishes Unnecessary and Promises True**

The pairing — *to Him belongs* and *He suffices as Trustee* — was explained as making *“neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book, whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) unnecessary to wish, and *“God’s promise ever true, whose word more truthful?”* (4:122) enough to trust. The sūrah has contrasted Satan’s promise only delusion (4:120) ending in Hell without escape (4:121) with God’s promise true ending in Gardens forever (4:122); to take the True Promiser as *wakīl* is to take the only promise that is not delusion as trustee. Where the sūrah says *“with Him are rewards of this world and Hereafter”* (4:134) for those who desire world’s reward, sufficiency as *wakīl* explains why both are with Him: He disposes both. For the weak this is direct: the orphan for whom you stand with justice (4:127), the wife suspended not left hanging (4:129), the both enriched after separation (4:130) — all are affairs whose *wakīl* suffices. That you need not be hanging nor make another hanging, but can settle or part entrusted to the Sufficient.
verses.133:
> If it is His Will, He can remove you altogether, O humanity, and replace you with others. And Allah is Most Capable to do so

**If He Will — He Can Remove You and Bring Others**

The verse states *in yashāʾ yudhhibkum ayyuhā al-nāsu wa yaʾti bi ākharīn* — if He wills, He can remove you, take you away altogether, O humanity. Bring others, replace you with others. *In yashāʾ* — if He wills, if it is His will — was explained with the will that governs ownership just declared — *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131, 4:132) — where *Wāsiʿ*, *Ghanī*, *Ḥamīd* show He does not need you. *Ayyuhā al-nāsu* — O humanity — was explained as address beyond the believers addressed for justice (4:135) to all, as the sūrah opened *“O humanity, be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) and here warns humanity that the single soul’s spread is not irreplaceable. *Wa yaʾti bi ākharīn* — and bring others, bring other peoples — was explained as replacement with those who are mindful where you disobey, as *“if you turn away He will replace you with another people then they will not be like you”* (47:38). Early reports illustrated *nas* here as the Meccans who invoked female gods besides Him (4:117) and took Satan as guardian (4:119); to tell them He can remove them is to tell them their claiming a share is not needed. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens where earth is spacious (4:100) — spaciousness that can receive others if you remain, and can do without you if you refuse.

**And God Is Most Capable to Do So**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿalā dhālika qadīrā* — And God is Most Capable, Powerful over that, to do that — was explained with *qadīr* — capable, powerful, measuring, determining — the One who created from single soul spread into countless (4:1) is capable to return spread to another spread. *ʿAlā dhālika* — over that, for that — removal and bringing — was read as that this is not threat only but capability, as *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) is measure, so *qadīr* over removal is measure of power. The sūrah has said He is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise where He enriches both after separation (4:130), Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy where mindfulness is commanded (4:131); to be Capable to remove is the power behind bounty and self-sufficiency: He enriches from His bounty because He can remove and bring without loss. Where the sūrah says *“with Him are rewards of this world and Hereafter”* (4:134) for those who desire world’s reward, capability to replace explains why both rewards are with Him — the Guardian and Helper enough (4:45) can give or withhold either.

**A Verse That Follows Trust With Warning**

Placed after *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee* (4:132) and before *whoever desires world’s reward, with Him are both rewards* (4:134), this verse follows trust with warning that trust’s Sufficer can do without the entruster. The sūrah bracketed women’s law — settlement best (4:128), no total inclining (4:129), enrichment from bounty (4:130) — with universal *waṣiyyah* to be mindful (4:131) and ownership-trusteeship (4:132); now it warns *O humanity* that mindfulness is not for His need. The sūrah has warned *do not be advocate for deceit* (4:105), *no good in most secret talks* (4:114), *whoever defies the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose* (4:115); those are instances of a humanity that could be removed if it persists, as prior communities were. For the weak this is protective: the One who can remove humanity and bring others is the One who was hoped to pardon the helpless (4:99) and who gives many havens to the emigrant (4:100) — His capability to replace is the same capability to rescue. To trust Him as *Wakīl* (4:132) where *He can* is to entrust to the Capable.
verses.134:
> Whoever desires the reward of this world, then ˹let them know that˺ with Allah are the rewards of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing

**Whoever Desires the Reward of This World — With Him Are Both**

The verse states *man kāna yurīdu thawāba al-dunyā fa ʿinda Allāhi thawābu al-dunyā wa al-ākhirati* — whoever desires, wants, seeks the reward, wage, of this nearer world, then let them know, then with God — at His disposal — are the rewards of this world and the Hereafter, together. *Thawāb* — reward, return, recompense — was explained as wage for deed, as the sūrah has promised *thawāb* — fine reward — to both sitter with excuse and striver yet greater for striver (4:95–96), great reward for seeking His pleasure via charity and reconciliation (4:114), tremendous loss for taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119). *yujza* — recompensed — for evil accordingly (4:123). *Yurīdu thawāba al-dunyā* — desires the world’s reward — was read as the shortcut: to act for world alone, as the lagger desired gain without sharing faith (4:73), as the denier of peace sought fleeting gain (4:94), as the wishers thought grace by wish (4:123). *Fa ʿinda Allāhi thawābu al-dunyā wa al-ākhirati* — with Him are both — was explained as exclusive possession: both rewards are *ʿinda Allāh* — with Him, at His side, from His bounty — as *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131) — so to desire world alone from other than Him is to seek little from the One who has much. *Wa* — and — joins the two: He has not divided them except where you divide desire. To ask Him is to get both, as the emigrant found many havens and abundance in earth (4:100) and the separator was enriched from His spaciousness (4:130) — world — while the believer hoping from Him finds forgiveness and mercy (4:96) — Hereafter.

**And God Is All-Hearing, All-Seeing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Samīʿan Baṣīrā* — And God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, was ever — was explained with *Samīʿ* — hearing every wish, every secret talk, every advocacy in this life (4:109), every dispute judged by what He shows (4:105) — and *Baṣīr* — seeing every act, every inclination not made equal between wives (4:129), every throwing sin on innocent (4:112), every charity meant for His pleasure (4:114). *Samīʿ Baṣīr* has sealed the command to return trusts and judge fairly — *noble command from the All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:58) — and now seals desire for reward: He hears the desire for world, sees the act for it, and measures accordingly without wronging even an atom but multiplying good many times (4:40). To say *with Him are both rewards* and He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing is to say seeking from Him is not unheard or unseen. The One who hears the wife fearing *nushūz* (4:128) and sees the *shuḥḥ* present with souls hears the desirer’s *yurīd* and sees whether desire is for Him or for little.

**Both Rewards With Him Makes Single Desire Small**

The phrase *ʿinda Allāhi thawābu al-dunyā wa al-ākhirati* was explained as making single desire small. If you desire world alone, you ask the Capable who can remove and bring (4:133) for what perishes; had you asked Him you would have both — world as *murāgham* and *saʿah* (4:100), and Hereafter as Gardens forever true (4:122). The sūrah has shown that the Hereafter is better for the mindful than little enjoyment (4:77), that prayer at fixed writ (4:103) secures both, that standing firm for justice though against yourselves (4:135) secures both though self-interest seems to favour world alone. *Samīʿ Baṣīr* as seal was linked to *do not let desires cause you to deviate from justice* (4:135): desire for world’s reward deviates where hearing and seeing are not recalled. To remember He hears and sees is to recall that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides Him”* (4:123) yet *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) — both measured by the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

The sūrah has shown that those who took Satan as guardian instead of Him suffered tremendous loss seeking what he promised as delusion (4:119–121) while those who believed and did good found Gardens ever true (4:122); to desire world alone is to take the deluder’s little.
verses.135:
> O believers! Stand firm for justice as witnesses for Allah even if it is against yourselves, your parents, or close relatives. Be they rich or poor, Allah is best to ensure their interests. So do not let your desires cause you to deviate ˹from justice˺. If you distort the testimony or refuse to give it, then ˹know that˺ Allah is certainly All-Aware of what you do

**Stand Firm for Justice as Witnesses for God Even Against Yourselves**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū kūnū qawwāmīna bi al-qisṭi shuhadāʾ li Allāhi wa law ʿalā anfusikum aw al-wālidayni wa al-aqrabīn* — O believers, be you steadfast, standing, upholders of justice, with equity, as witnesses for God even if against yourselves or parents or close kin. *Qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — upholders of justice, maintainers of equity, ever standing for fairness — was explained with *qawwām* — much standing, firm — the same root as *to stand up for orphans with justice* (4:127) and *to establish prayer* at fixed writ (4:103). *Shuhadāʾ li Allāhi* — witnesses for God — was read as testimony offered for Him, not for clan, as the sūrah commands to return trusts and judge fairly as noble command from the All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:58) and to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and to verify before fighting (4:94). *Wa law ʿalā anfusikum aw al-wālidayni wa al-aqrabīn* — even if against yourselves, parents, close relatives — was explained as the Book’s severest test of the single soul’s ties (4:1): to honour ties is not to hide a kinsman’s theft by night plotting (4:108) nor to advocate for self-wrongers (4:107). To be just even against those ties is to honour the Creator of the single soul more than the soul’s branch.

**So Do Not Let Desires Cause You to Deviate From Justice**

The warning *fa lā tattabiʿū al-hawā a taʿdilū* — so do not follow, do not let desires cause you to deviate, to incline from being just, from equitableness — was explained with *hawā* — desire, caprice, inclination — the same *hawā* that makes you deviate greatly if followed (4:27), that would make you follow other than believers’ path (4:115). That makes private talk about charity insincere if for show. *An taʿdilū* — deviating from being just — was read as lest you not be just, lest you swerve. The sūrah earlier warned *if you fear ill conduct advise, then do not share beds, then discipline gently* (4:34) — justice even in household — and warned *do not incline completely leaving the other suspended* (4:129) — justice even in polygyny. To follow *hawā* was linked to deceiving where eloquence persuades a judge to give a brother’s right as fire (Bukhārī 2680); desire there is eloquence, kin preference, pity, or greed for fleeting gain by denying peace (4:94). The command was read as the Book’s sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge by what He shows (4:105): to follow desire is to judge by what He did not show.

**A Verse That Follows Universal Ownership With Universal Justice**

Placed after two humanity addresses — *We commanded those before you and you to be mindful* (4:131), *to Him belongs all, He suffices as Trustee* (4:132), *He can remove O humanity and bring others* (4:133), *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) — this verse is the believers’ answer: stand firm for justice as witnesses for Him. The sūrah that began with honouring ties from a single soul (4:1), showed orphan girls deprived yet desired (4:127), wife fearing *nushūz* where settlement best (4:128), wives between whom inclination cannot be equalled (4:129), now says standing for justice may be against the very ties you honour — yourselves, parents, kin — and for the very rich or poor you once pitted — yet do not follow desire to deviate, lest you twist or turn away. The sūrah that taught verification before fighting (4:94) and judging by Book (4:105) here teaches verification before testifying: be *qawwām* — ever standing — so that twisting and refusing are not options. For the weak this is the highest protection: where wealth tempts and poverty pities, justice upheld for God is the haven as sure as many havens for the emigrant, and He who is All-Aware of what you do will not wrong a speck.
verses.136:
> O believers! Have faith in Allah, His Messenger, the Book He has revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before. Indeed, whoever denies Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has clearly gone far astray

**O Believers — Have Faith in God, Messenger, and Books**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū āminū bi Allāhi wa rasūlihī wa al-kitābi alladhī nazzala ʿalā rasūlihī wa al-kitābi alladhī anzala min qablu* — O believers, have faith — believe, continue believing — in God and His Messenger and the Book He has sent down upon His Messenger and the Scriptures He sent down before. *Āminū* to *āmanū* was explained not as contradiction but as command to firmness, renewal. Comprehensiveness: those who already believe are told to remain believers, to increase belief, to believe without distinction, as the sūrah has shown that those who believe and do good are admitted to Gardens (4:57, 4:122) yet belief must be in the full articles. *Bi Allāhi wa rasūlihī* — in God and Messenger — was read as the two inseparably taught where obeying the Messenger is obeying God (4:80), messengers are only sent to be obeyed by His leave (4:64), and the Messenger is taken as judge without resistance (4:65). *Al-kitābi alladhī nazzala ʿalā rasūlihī* — the Book He revealed to His Messenger — was explained as the Qur’an sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) whose word none is more truthful than (4:122). *Wa al-kitābi alladhī anzala min qablu* — and the Scriptures He revealed before — was read as the Books given before — Torah, Gospel — before distortion, matching *“Worship God alone, associate none”* (4:36) and *“We commanded those given Scripture before you and you to be mindful”* (4:131) — the command is one. The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book claim wishes (4:123) and distort words (4:46); to believe in Books before is to believe in them as revealed before distorting hands altered them, not to follow altered claim.

**And Whoever Denies — Has Gone Far Astray**

The threat *wa man yakfur bi Allāhi wa malāʾikatihī wa kutubihī wa rusulihī wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri fa qad ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — indeed whoever denies — covers, disbelieves in — God, His angels, His Books, His messengers. The Last Day has clearly gone far astray, wandered far — was explained with five articles. *Yakfur* — to deny, to cover — was read as the denial that makes association not forgiven (4:116) and that makes following other than believers’ path burning (4:115). The five — God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day — were explained as the Book’s summary of faith, matching *“whoever associates has gone far astray”* (4:116) where *ḍalālan baʿīdan* — far straying — also sealed; here the same seal for denying any of the five. Angels were read as the recorders of night schemes (4:81), the takers of souls asked *what were you doing?* (4:97), the supporters of prayer guard (4:102); to deny angels is to deny those realities. Books and messengers were read as the conveyors of the Book in truth and wisdom taught (4:113); Last Day as the Day about which there is no doubt where all will be gathered (4:87) and gathered together hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell (4:140). *Ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — gone far astray — was linked to going far after guidance became clear (4:115); denial of these articles after clarity is the farthest distance, because it denies the very witnesses who prove clarity.

**A Verse That Follows Justice With Creed**

Placed after *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves rich or poor, do not follow desire, if you twist or turn away He is All-Aware* (4:135), this verse follows justice with creed that secures it. The sūrah has judged between people by Book, warned no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), warned defying the Messenger and following other than believers’ path (4:115), named association far straying (4:116), female gods and Satan’s share (4:117–118), Satan’s orders and delusion (4:119–120), two abodes true (4:121–122), wishes not by wish (4:123), good with faith not wronged (4:124), best faith submission following Abraham whom God took as friend (4:125), ownership and encompassing (4:126), instruction for orphan women and helpless children (4:127), settlement best though selves brought with *shuḥḥ* (4:128), impossible emotional equality yet do not incline completely (4:129), enrichment after separation (4:130), universal command to be mindful though He is Self-Sufficient (4:131), sufficiency as Trustee (4:132), capability to replace humanity (4:133), both rewards with Him Hearing and Seeing (4:134). Now faith in the full articles is the root that makes justice — *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — possible without twisting. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by desire (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here names the content that desire most attacks — God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day — after which far straying is the fruit.
verses.137:
> Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed and again disbelieved—˹only˺ increasing in disbelief—Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to the ˹Right˺ Way

**Those Who Believed Then Disbelieved — Then Increased**

The verse states *inna alladhīna āmanū thumma kafarū thumma āmanū thumma kafarū thumma izdādū kufrā* — indeed those who believed then disbelieved, then believed then disbelieved — then only increasing in disbelief, adding disbelief. *Āmanū thumma kafarū* — believed then disbelieved — repeated twice was explained as oscillation, not mere lapse: belief then denial, then return to belief then again denial. Not as repentance accepted soon after error (4:17) but as performance, as hypocrisy’s rhythm. *Thumma izdādū kufrā* — then increased, added, in disbelief — was read as that the second disbelief is not return to first level but increase: associating after far straying (4:116), taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119), invoking female gods (4:117) — each step adds. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose (4:115) and whoever associates has gone far astray (4:116); to oscillate between belief and denial after clarity is to defy after clarity repeatedly, making guidance not firm. The generality was stressed: whoever trades belief for disbelief and returns only to trade again, increasing, is meant — the hypocrite described as *“torn between belief and disbelief, belonging neither to these nor those”* (4:143) and who seek to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142).

**Allah Will Neither Forgive Nor Guide to Right Way**

The seal *lam yakuni Allāhu li yaghfira lahum wa lā li yahdiyuhum sabīlā* — Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to a way — the Right Way — was explained with two negations: no forgiveness and no guidance. *Li yaghfira lahum* — to forgive them — was read as that *“whoever commits evil then seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving”* (4:110) has a condition — seeking after evil before death’s saying *now I repent* (4:18); these increase in disbelief instead of seeking. Forgiveness is not. *Wa lā li yahdiyuhum sabīlā* — nor guide them to a way, to path — was read as *sabīla* — way — the same *sabīl* the sūrah wills to make clear as noble ways (4:26), Satan wishes the deviant far path (4:60), believers’ path is not to be left (4:115). Those who oscillate and increase have closed the path by repeatedly turning. The phrase *lam yakun li yaghfira* — He will not forgive — was linked to *“He does not forgive associating, forgives what is less”* (4:48, 4:116): increase in disbelief is shown to settle into the unforgiven associate-level where pardon is not, unless the oscillation is broken by firm belief. The sūrah has said *“whoever is left to stray you will never find a way”* (4:88, 4:143) — *lan tajida lahū sabīlā* — here the way not found is forgiveness and guidance, because they left it.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Hypocrisy Before Its Portrait**

Though only *“those who believed then disbelieved then believed again then increased, He will neither forgive nor guide to Right Way,”* the verse anchors hypocrisy before its portrait. Immediately after: *“give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, seeking honour”* (4:138–139) — portraits of oscillation made alliance. Immediately after: *“when you hear revelations denied or ridiculed do not sit in that company else you are like them, He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell”* (4:140) — company of oscillation. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here warns that desire to keep options open — belief then disbelief — ends with neither forgiveness nor way, because the One who is Self-Sufficient (4:131) and whose promise is ever true (4:122) does not guide the one who increased after being shown. For the weak this is clarifying: belief is not a wish by which grace is claimed (4:123) nor a wavering between sides like those who wait to see what happens (4:141), but firm faith that finds Him All-Forgiving when it seeks after evil (4:110).
verses.138:
> Give good news of a painful punishment to hypocrites

**Give Good News of Painful Punishment to Hypocrites**

The verse states *bashshiri al-munāfiqīna bi anna lahum ʿadhāban alīmā* — give good news, announce, to hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment. *Bashshir* — to give good news, to announce joy — was explained as irony: to announce painful punishment as if good news, because the hypocrite’s own announcement is deceit — they seek to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142), they show prayer to be seen (4:142), they wait to see what happens to you and say to whichever side wins *were we not with you?* (4:141). *Al-munāfiqīn* — hypocrites — was read as those who believed then disbelieved then believed again then increased (4:137) and who are torn between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) and who will be in lowest depth of Fire without helper (4:145). *Bi anna lahum ʿadhāban alīman* — that for them is painful punishment — was explained as *alīm* — painful, aching — the same *alīm* prepared for those who consume orphans’ wealth after warning (4:10’s Fire) and for those who knowingly persist then say now I repent (4:18). The sūrah has traced hypocrisy from the community divided into two groups about them (4:88) where some wished you alike in disbelief (4:89) to the double-faced who plunge into *fitnah* (4:91), to the lagger who stays and envies (4:72–73), to the plotters by night (4:108). Here the announce is not warning but recompense — *painful punishment* — for the territory between belief and disbelief where they tried to keep both.

**A Verse That Follows Oscillation With Irony**

Placed after *those who believed then disbelieved then increased, He will neither forgive nor guide* (4:137), this verse follows oscillation with irony: the good news for the one who increased in disbelief after believing is painful punishment. The sūrah has shown that honour and power belongs to God (4:139) where hypocrites seek honour from disbelievers as allies, and that sitting with those who deny or ridicule revelations makes you like them and gathered together in Hell (4:140); the painful punishment is the announcement for that alliance and that sitting. The sūrah has also shown that the deceitful’s night speech displeases Him (4:108) and that advocacy for self-wrongers in this life will find no advocate on the Day (4:109); painful punishment is the Day’s answer to the night’s delight. Where the sūrah elsewhere says *“do not consume wealth unjustly, God is ever Merciful to you”* (4:29) yet *“whoever does this unjustly We will burn in Fire, easy for God”* (4:30) — easy where threats are — this painful punishment is the Fire easy for the One who can remove humanity and bring others (4:133).

**A Short Verse That Opens the Hypocrite Portrait**

Though only *“give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites,”* the verse opens the hypocrite portrait that follows. Immediately: *who choose disbelievers as allies instead of believers, do they seek honour through that company? Surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139) — portraits of their alliance. Then: *He has already revealed that when you hear revelations denied or ridiculed do not sit in that company else you are like them, He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) — portraits of their sitting. Then: *those who wait to see what happens to you, saying to each winner were we not on your side?* (4:141) — portraits of their waiting. All are branches of the oscillation that neither forgives nor guides (4:137). For the weak this is a clearing: where you were divided into two groups about hypocrites (4:88) and told not to take them as allies unless they emigrate (4:89), the painful punishment is the news that the division is not equal — to ally with disbelievers for honour is not the community’s way, as *millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* (4:125) was not alliance with many.
verses.139:
> who choose disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour and power through that company? Surely all honour and power belongs to Allah

**Who Choose Disbelievers as Allies Instead of Believers**

The verse states *alladhīna yattakhidhūna al-kāfirīna awliyāʾa min dūni al-muʾminīna* — those who take disbelievers as allies, guardians, close protectors instead, apart from, the believers. *Yattakhidhūna awliyāʾ* — to take as allies — was explained with *walī* — guardian, protector, helper — the same *walī* God alone suffices as (4:45), the help the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75), the trustee who suffices (4:132). *Min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers, apart from believers, short of believers — was read as choosing the other company while believers are available, as earlier *“do not take them as allies unless they emigrate”* (4:89) where alliance was conditioned on emigration. *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God proof against yourselves?”* (4:144) where alliance is warning. The sūrah has traced *awliyāʾ* from the lagger who had no bond — *ka a lam takun baynakum wa baynahu mawaddah* — as if no affection between you (4:73) — to the double safety seekers (4:91), to the treaty people excepted (4:90), to Satan taken as guardian instead of Him (4:119). Here the *awliyāʾ* taken are disbelievers instead of believers, for the hypocrites who oscillate (4:137, 4:143) the natural alliance is the side that promises *ʿizzah* without *qisṭ*.

**Surely All Honour and Power Belongs to God**

The answer *fa inna al-ʿizzata li Allāhi jamīʿā* — then surely all, completely, honour and power belongs to God — was explained with *jamīʿan* — completely, all together — the same totality as *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131) repeated thrice. As *with Him are both rewards* (4:134). *Al-ʿizzata li Allāhi* — honour belongs to Him — was read as that *ʿizzah* is not transferred by taking allies. It is His to give to whom He wills — *“you, the best *dīn* submits face and follows Abraham whom He took as friend”* (4:125) — friendship with the Owner of honour is honour. The sūrah has said that God suffices as Guardian and Helper (4:45) and suffices as Trustee (4:132) and is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131); to seek *ʿizzah* beside Him is to seek the encompassed (4:126) among the encompassed. The phrase was linked to *“do they seek honour through that company? Surely all honour belongs to Him”* as the sūrah’s ownership applied to honour: as all in heavens and earth belong to Him, all honour belongs to Him, so the seeker who takes disbelievers as allies seeks at the side of those who own nothing.

**A Verse That Names the Transaction Behind Oscillation**

Placed after *give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites* (4:138), this verse names the transaction behind oscillation: they believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137), torn between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) because they sought *ʿizzah* where alliance seemed to give it. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose (4:115) — choosing disbelievers as allies is that following — and that associating is far straying (4:116) — seeking *ʿizzah* among associators is that straying’s economy. Where the sūrah says *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves* (4:135) not letting desires deviate, seeking honour from wrong company is the desire that deviates: to witness for disbelievers to gain *ʿizzah* instead of witnessing for God though against yourselves is the precise inversion. For the weak this is steadying: honour is not with the company that wishes you deviate (4:27), nor with Satan’s delusion promise (4:120), but with Him whose earth is spacious (4:100) and whose promise ever true (4:122).
verses.140:
> He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s revelations being denied or ridiculed, then do not sit in that company unless they engage in a different topic, or else you will be like them. Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together in Hell

**When You Hear Revelations Denied or Ridiculed — Do Not Sit**
The verse states *wa qad nazzala ʿalaykum fī al-kitābi an idhā samiʿtum āyāti Allāhi yukfaru bihā wa yustahzaʾu bihā fa lā taqʿudū maʿahum ḥattā yakhūḍū fī ḥadīthin ghayrih* — He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear God’s signs, revelations, being denied, covered, or mocked, ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in another discourse, other topic. *Nazzala ʿalaykum fī al-kitābi* — He has revealed to you in the Book — was explained as the earlier revelation referenced at 6:68 — *when you see those who engage in Our signs then turn away until they engage in other talk* — the sūrah’s cross-reference where sitting with mockers is prohibited, recited again here for hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139). *Āyāti Allāhi yukfaru bihā wa yustahzaʾu bihā* — signs denied or ridiculed — was explained as the denial that makes association far straying (4:116) and the ridicule that is the mocker’s weapon, as the sūrah has shown that those given a portion distort words and say *“we hear and disobey”* (4:46) and that Satan promises only delusion (4:120). *Fa lā taqʿudū maʿahum* — do not sit with them — was read as prohibition of company, not merely speech, matching *no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) — sitting where signs are ridiculed is the secret talk without those goods. *Ḥattā yakhūḍū fī ḥadīthin ghayrih* — until they engage in another topic, plunge into other talk — was read as the limit: leaving until the subject changes, as *“do not sit in that company unless they engage in a different topic”* is the translation’s phrasing.
**He Will Gather Hypocrites and Disbelievers Together in Hell**
The gathering *inna Allāha jāmiʿu al-munāfiqīna wa al-kāfirīna fī Jahannama jamīʿā* — surely God will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together, completely, in Hell — was explained with *jāmiʿ* — gatherer — the same gatherer who will gather you on the Day about which there is no doubt (4:87) and who gathered revelation as Book with truth (4:105). *Jamīʿan* — all together, completely — was read as that sitting together in mockery in this life — *taqʿudū maʿahum* — ends as being gathered together in Hell: company chosen becomes company assigned. The sūrah has shown that the hypocrite oscillates between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) yet *innakum idhan mithluhum* counts the sitter as like the disbeliever; gathering together makes that likeness abiding — *khālidīn* — without escape (4:121) as that gathering is *“what an evil destination”* for self-wrongers (4:97). The phrase was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, God’s promise ever true”* (4:122) versus *“Hell as home no escape”* (4:121): the sitting that was for *ʿizzah* (4:139) ends in gathering for humiliation, as the guarded prayer’s preparation was humiliating punishment for disbelievers (4:102).
**A Verse That Follows Honour Sought With Company Prohibited**
Placed after *who choose disbelievers as allies seeking honour, surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139), this verse follows honour sought with company prohibited. The hypocrites sought honour through company with disbelievers (4:139); the verse says the company where signs are denied or mocked is precisely where you may not sit lest you be like them — so honour sought there is gathered as humiliation. The sūrah has shown that trusteeship suffices (4:132), that He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133), that both rewards are with Him (4:134); to sit with mockers for worldly *ʿizzah* is to desire world’s reward from beside Him where both rewards are with Him. The sūrah has also shown that standing for justice as witnesses for Him though against yourselves (4:135) requires leaving where justice is mocked; to remain seated where signs are denied is to distort testimony. The verse generalises the sūrah’s procedure: where report is heard of security or fear verify through Messenger and authority (4:83), and where a bearer of peace offers *salām* be sure (4:94), here where a sitter hears signs denied verify by leaving until other talk.

**Where the Verse Sits in the Sūrah**
The prohibition belongs to the long section of this sūrah on the community's internal life, where the Book deals with the hypocrites, the waverers and the arguments in the mosque. The verses around it return again and again to the same man: the one who listens to the mockery and stays seated, and the one who is told to turn away from the circle until the talk changes (6:68). The Sūrah of the Cattle states the same instruction in the same words, which is why the verse here begins by saying that God has already sent this down in the Book.
**What the Command Is Protecting**
A community that sits through the ridicule of its own foundations while saying nothing is being trained out of its convictions. The verse therefore makes the company itself a matter of law, and it does not confine the rule to one subject: the names and the signs can be mocked in a lecture hall as easily as in a market. The Book's other instructions on speech follow the same logic: avoid suspicion, do not spy, do not backbite (49:12), and the warning that a person will be asked about what he heard and saw and thought about (17:36). The rule is about the company a person keeps, and the sūrah states its limit in the same verse: if the talk changes, the seat is free again.
verses.141:
> ˹The hypocrites are˺ those who wait to see what happens to you. So if Allah grants you victory, they say ˹to you˺, “Were we not on your side?” But if the disbelievers have a share ˹of victory˺, they say ˹to them˺, “Did we not have the advantage over you, yet we protected you from the believers?” Allah will judge between ˹all of˺ you on the Day of Judgment. And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers

**Those Who Wait to See What Happens to You**

The verse states *alladhīna yatarabbaṣūna bikum* — those who wait, watch, lie in wait in expectation about you. *Yatarabbaṣūna* — to wait, to watch, to await outcome — was explained as the hypocrites’ posture between the community divided into two groups about them (4:88) and the gathering of hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140). To wait about you — *bikum* — was read as waiting upon believers’ affairs, battles. Turns, as the lagger waited — *la yabṭiʾannakum* — to lag behind and say if you suffer *God blessed us for not being there* and if you gain *would we had been with them* (4:72–73), and as party waiting for the Prophet’s judgment to be deceived (4:113). The waiters here are the same who took disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) and sat where revelations were mocked lest they be like them (4:140); waiting is sitting’s extension into war: not sitting in mosque where signs are denied, but lying in wait between armies to see who wins. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens by moving (4:100), that the traveller shortens and guards prayer by moving in ranks (4:101–102); the waiter moves toward neither haven nor rank but stays to see.

**God Will Judge Between You on Resurrection Day**

The adjudication *fa Allāhu yaḥkumu baynakum yawma al-qiyāmati* — then God will judge, decide, between you — all of you — on the Day of Standing — was explained as the sūrah’s gathering promise: He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140) after being gathered on the Day about which there is no doubt (4:87) and after being asked at soul-taking *what were you doing?* (4:97). *Yaḥkumu baynakum* — will judge between you — was read as between believers, hypocrites, and disbelievers, between the waiter and both winners he courted, between the *fatḥ* and *naṣīb* claims. The sūrah has said the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105). That He is enough as Trustee (4:132) and Witness (4:79). On the Day the Judge is not eloquence that might sway a human court where *“some may be more eloquent and I give his brother’s right as fire”* (Bukhārī 2680), but the All-Knowing who knows what was in hearts (4:63) and who is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108). The judgment separates the waiter’s *“were we not with you?”* from the true *with-ness* — *maʿiyyah* — that is with the believers for Gardens (4:122).

**And He Will Never Grant Disbelievers a Way Over Believers**

The assurance *wa lan yajʿala Allāhu li al-kāfirīna ʿalā al-muʾminīna sabīlā* — and God will never grant, make. Disbelievers over believers a way, a path, an argument — was explained with *sabīl* — way, path, proof, dominance — the same *sabīl* the sūrah said He will guide to noble ways (4:26), the path believers follow (4:115), and the *sabili al-muʾminīn* not to be left. To grant no *sabīl* for disbelievers over believers was read as promise that final argument and final dominance are not given to disbelief over faith, as *“He will judge between you”* ensures the argument is not the waiter’s double claim. Early authorities debated worldly reading — never granting disbelievers a way over believers in proof — versus Last-Day — the Day — where gathering separates. The sūrah holds both: on the Day no *sabīl* remains, and in this world where God wills to make clear and guide to noble ways (4:26) the believer’s *sabīl* is protected where he stands for justice (4:135). The promise was also linked to *all honour belongs to Him* (4:139): *sabīl* over believers as honour is not granted to disbelievers, though *naṣīb* or *fatḥ* in battle may be. For the weak this is steadying: waiting between sides promises no *sabīl* over you, as He who owns heavens and earth (4:126) grants none.

**A Verse That Follows Gathering With Waiting and Judgment**

Placed after gathering hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140), this verse follows gathering with waiting that made gathering inevitable and with judgment that decides waiting. The hypocrites who believed then disbelieved then increased (4:137), announced as painful punishment (4:138), who chose disbelievers as allies for honour (4:139), sat where revelations were mocked (4:140), now wait between armies to claim *were we not with you?* to whichever side wins. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here exposes the waiter’s desire: to belong without standing, to be *qawwām* nowhere yet claim *maʿiyya* everywhere. The next verses will anatomise that waiting: they seek to deceive God but He outwits them, they stand for prayer to be seen hardly remembering (4:142), torn between neither believers nor disbelievers, whoever He leaves to stray you will find no way (4:143).
verses.142:
> Surely the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He outwits them. When they stand up for prayer, they do it half-heartedly only to be seen by people—hardly remembering Allah at all

**The Hypocrites Seek to Deceive God — But He Outwits Them**

The verse opens *inna al-munāfiqīna yukhādiʿūna Allāha wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — surely the hypocrites seek to deceive, to trick, God. He is outwitting, deceiving them, repaying their deceit. *Yukhādiʿūna* — to seek to deceive, to pretend, to show other than what is — was explained as hypocrisy’s essence: belief then disbelief then increased (4:137), taking disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139), sitting where revelations are mocked (4:140), waiting between winners to claim *were we not with you?* (4:141). To deceive God was explained as showing Islam before believers while hiding alliance with disbelievers, as plotting by night what displeases Him while He is with them (4:108) and hiding from people but not from the Encompassing (4:108). *Wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — but He outwits them, He is their deceiver in return — was read as that His outwitting is recompense: He lets them pursue what they chose (4:115), gathers them with disbelievers together in Hell (4:140), will judge between all on the Day (4:141), and leaves to stray whom He leaves (4:143). The sūrah has said that God is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108) and knows what is in hearts (4:63); deception cannot reach Him, it returns. Early notes linked *khādiʿuhum* to *makr* — planning — where *“they plot and God plots, God is best of plotters”* (3:54); the outwitting is His plan that gathering together is the outcome of sitting together.

**When They Stand for Prayer — Half-Heartedly, To Be Seen**

The sign *wa idhā qāmū ilā al-ṣalāti qāmū kusālā yurāʾūna al-nāsa* — and when they stand up for prayer, head to prayer, they stand lazy, sluggish, half-heartedly, showing off to people, to be seen — was explained with *qāmū ilā al-ṣalāti* — standing to prayer — the same standing commanded as *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — ever standing for justice (4:135) — and *qūmū li al-yatāmā bi al-qisṭ* (4:127) — here the hypocrites stand to prayer as witnesses not for Him but for people. *Kusālā* — lazy, heavy, sluggish — was explained as heaviness where the sūrah earlier said prayer at appointed writ (4:103) and guarded prayer under arms (4:102) requires vigilance; their laziness is the opposite of vigilance and of pursuit without faltering (4:104). *Yurāʾūna al-nāsa* — they show off to people, make seen — *riyāʾ* — was read as the same showing off condemned where they spend wealth to show off and do not believe in God or Last Day (4:38) — *spending to be seen* — here *standing to be seen*. The sūrah has shown that there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114); to stand to be seen is to seek people’s pleasure, the *ʿizzah* sought among disbelievers (4:139), not His.

**Hardly Remembering God at All**
