The remainder *wa lā yadhkurūna Allāha illā qalīlā* — and they hardly remember, mention, invoke God at all, except a little — was explained with *yadhkurūna* — to remember, to mention — the same *adhkurū Allāha* commanded standing, sitting, lying down when prayer is finished (4:103). The sūrah has shown that remembrance in all postures is prayer’s extension; hypocrites remember a little — *qalīlan* — the minimum to be seen, not the standing, sitting, lying remembrance. *Illā qalīlan* — except a little — was explained as little in quantity and little in sincerity, as the sūrah says they stand lazily to be seen — their few remembrances are for seen-ness. Classical notes added that the *qalīl* matches the world’s little enjoyment — *matāʿ qalīl* (4:77) — that hypocrisy trades Gardens forever (4:122) for little seen-ness. The seal contrasts with *“whose word more truthful than God’s?”* (4:122) and *“God is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132): to remember little is to trust little.
verses.143:
> Torn between belief and disbelief—belonging neither to these ˹believers˺ nor those ˹disbelievers˺. And whoever Allah leaves to stray, you will never find for them a way

**Torn Between — Belonging Neither to Believers Nor Disbelievers**

The verse opens *mudhabdhabīna bayna dhālika lā ilā hāʾulāʾi wa lā ilā hāʾulāʾi* — torn, wavering, suspended between that, between this and that, belonging neither to these — believers — nor to those — disbelievers. *Mudhabdhab* — torn, swayed, fluttered, shaky — was explained as the hypocrites’ oscillation already named — believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137), waiting to see what happens to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted, standing lazy to be seen (4:142). *Bayna dhālika* — between that — was read as between belief and disbelief, between the host with many havens (4:100) and the host without escape (4:121), between Gardens true (4:122) and Hell prepared. The sūrah has shown two companies — hypocrites and disbelievers gathered together in Hell (4:140) versus those who believe and do good in Gardens forever (4:122) — and said *“do not sit with mockers else you are like them”* (4:140). The torn are those who sat and are like yet not counted fully until gathering makes like permanent. The image was also linked to the double safety seekers who wish safety from both sides (4:91) yet belong to neither where *fitnah* returns.

**And Whoever God Leaves to Stray, You Will Never Find a Way**

The seal *wa man yuḍlili Allāhu fa lan tajida lahū sabīlā* — and whoever God leaves to stray, causes to stray, leaves straying, you will never find for them a way — was explained with *yuḍlil* — to leave to stray, to allow deviation, to not guide — after they turned to what they chose. *Man yuḍlili Allāhu* matches *“do you wish to guide those left by God to stray?”* (4:88) where regressed hypocrites were allowed to regress because of misdeeds. *“We will let them pursue what they chose”* (4:115) after defying the Messenger and following other than believers’ path. *Fa lan tajida lahū sabīlā* — you will never find for them a way — was explained as *sabīl* — way, path, argument, means — the same *sabīl* the sūrah said He will guide to noble ways (4:26), the path believers follow (4:115). The way He will never grant disbelievers over believers (4:141). To find no way for the left-to-stray torn is to say no argument rescues, no alias of *ʿizzah* (4:139) provides way, no sitting as like them (4:140) provides way, no waiting as with winners (4:141) provides way, no outwitted deception (4:142) provides way.

**The Left to Stray After Many Clarities**

The phrase *wa man yuḍlili Allāhu* was explained as divine leaving after many clarities: association far astray (4:116), female gods invoked as Satan (4:117), Satan cursed taking share (4:118), ordering cutting and altering (4:119), promising only delusion (4:120), two abodes declared true (4:121–122), wishes not by wish (4:123), good with faith not wronged (4:124), best faith submission following Abraham (4:125), ownership and encompassing (4:126), instruction for orphan women (4:127), settlement best though selfishness present (4:128), impossible emotional equality yet do not incline completely (4:129), enrichment after separation (4:130), universal command to be mindful (4:131), sufficiency as Trustee (4:132) — after all that, to remain *mudhabdhab* is not ignorance but straying left. The sūrah has said *“He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26–28) — clarity was given; wavering after clarity is the human turning that He lets be. For the weak this is a call to belong: where the sūrah says *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God proof against yourselves?”* (4:144) next, the wavering between alliances is the proof to abandon, by choosing believers as like — *mithluhum* — for Gardens.
verses.144:
> O believers! Do not take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Would you like to give Allah solid proof against yourselves

**Would You Give God Solid Proof Against Yourselves?**

The question *a turīdūna a tajʿalū li Allāhi ʿalaykum sulṭānan mubīnā* — do you want to give, to make, for God against you a clear, manifest warrant, proof, authority? — was explained with *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant, manifest proof, evident authority — the same *sulṭān mubīn* given to you over the double-faced who do not withdraw or offer peace (4:91) — *We have given you clear warrant over such people*. Here the *sulṭān* is inverted: instead of clear warrant for you against the hostile turners, you give God clear warrant against yourselves by allying with disbelievers instead of believers. *Tajʿalū li Allāhi ʿalaykum* — to make for God against you — was explained as furnishing the prosecution evidence by act: to take allies instead of believers while the Book with truth judges between people (4:105) and while standing firm for justice though against yourselves is commanded (4:135) is to write your own proof. The sūrah has shown that association is not forgiven (4:116) and leaves far straying. That the gathered hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140) is the gathering of the like — *mithluhum*. To give *sulṭān mubīn* against yourselves is to make that gathering just, because the proof — *ʿizzah* sought among disbelievers (4:139), sitting where signs are mocked (4:140), waiting to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted (4:142) — is manifest.

**A Verse That Follows Torn Between With Choice**

Placed after *torn between neither these nor those, whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way* (4:143), this verse follows the frozen between with a choice and its evidence. The torn between is told: do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — decide the between. The sūrah has shown that guidance was made clear, noble ways taught, turning offered (4:26–28), and that He can remove you O humanity and bring others (4:133) — removal is the consequence of giving Him clear warrant against yourselves by choosing the other alliance. The sūrah has also shown that *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) — to seek reward from disbelievers as allies is to seek little where both are with Him whose awareness is *Khabīr* of what you do (4:135, 4:128). The question *a turīdūna* — do you want? — was read as the Book’s appeal to will: do you intend to give proof against yourselves, or would you rather stand for justice even against yourselves and find Him All-Forgiving where you set right and are mindful (4:129–130)? The choice is not between honour and humiliation invented, but between proof for you — *sulṭān* over hostile turners (4:91) — and proof against you — *sulṭān* for Him over you.

**Alliance Instead of Believers as Proof**

The phrase *min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers — was explained to show that alliance with disbelievers is not forbidden where treaty or haven requires intercourse — the sūrah excepted those allied to treaty people (4:90), allowed laying aside weapons in rain yet keep precaution (4:102). Promised many havens among people (4:100); the prohibition is taking them as *awliyāʾ* — intimate guardians — instead of believers, as the oppressed cry for guardian and helper from grace (4:75) — guardian is to be from Him. Early notes added that the *sulṭān mubīn* against yourselves is not a metaphorical phrase but the record: night plotting with them (4:108) while He is with you, advocating for self-wrongers among them (4:107), hiding from people not from the Encompassing (4:108), will be brought as witness. Where the emigrant’s reward falls upon God secure (4:100), the ally-taker’s proof falls against himself secure, because the Trustee enough (4:132) keeps record that encompasses everything (4:126).
verses.145:
> Surely the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire—and you will never find for them any helper—

**Hypocrites Will Be in the Lowest Depths of the Fire**

The verse states *inna al-munāfiqīna fī al-darki al-asfali mina al-nāri* — surely the hypocrites will be, are, in the lowest depth, the bottom layer, the nethermost reach, of the Fire. *Dark* — depth, level, abyss — *asfal* — lowest — was explained as the deepest layer of Hell, below disbelievers gathered together with hypocrites (4:140), below the self-wronger’s Hell as home (4:97), below the defier’s burning (4:115), below the follower of Satan’s Hell without escape (4:121). *Mina al-nāri* — of the Fire — was read as the Fire whose preparation was humiliating for disbelievers where prayer was guarded (4:102), whose truth is contrasted with Gardens true (4:122), whose lowest depth is for those who deceive God while He outwits them (4:142), stand lazy to be seen (4:142), are torn between neither these nor those (4:143). Take disbelievers as allies giving God clear warrant against themselves (4:144). Early reports noted that the Fire has layers — *darakāt* — unlike Paradise’s *darajāt* — elevated ranks (4:96) — the lowest *dark* is for hypocrisy because hypocrisy is lowest in deceit: to invoke female gods besides Him and Satan (4:117) is open, to deceive while claiming belief is hidden and therefore lower. The sūrah has shown that the sitter where signs are mocked is like them (4:140) and will be gathered together; the lowest depth is the belonging of the torn who belonged to none.

**And You Will Never Find for Them Any Helper**

The clause *wa lan tajida lahum naṣīrā* — and you will never find for them any helper, protector, supporter — was explained with *naṣīr* — helper — the same *naṣīr* the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45) and that disbelievers as allies were sought for instead of believers (4:144). To find no *naṣīr* for hypocrites was read as that no *walī* and no *naṣīr* remains where they gave Him clear proof against themselves (4:144) and where *“whoever God leaves to stray you will never find a way”* (4:143). The phrase *lan tajida* — you will never find — was addressed to the Prophet ﷺ and to every searcher: no helper will be found for them, as the deceitful’s advocates in this life found no advocate before God on the Day (4:109) and no *wakīl* (4:109). The lowest depth without helper contrasts with Gardens promised to those who believe and do good where rivers flow and promise is true (4:122) and with enrichment from His bounty for those who separate (4:130). Where the emigrant finds many havens (4:100) and many refuges, the hypocrite finds lowest Fire and no helper, because heavens and earth belong to the One they deceived while He was with them at night plotting (4:108).

**A Verse That Follows Clear Warrant Against Selves With Depth Without Helper**

Placed after *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?* (4:144), this verse follows the warning that taking that alliance gives clear *sulṭān* against yourselves with the consequence that follows manifest proof: lowest depth, no helper. The sūrah has built hypocrisy’s proof step by step: oscillation (4:137), announcing painful punishment (4:138), seeking honour among disbelievers (4:139), sitting where signs are mocked as like them (4:140), waiting to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted, standing lazy to be seen remembering little (4:142), torn between neither (4:143), taking allies instead of believers (4:144) — lowest depth is the depth of that accumulation, as Gardens’ *darajāt* are the elevation of accumulated good where charity, kindness, reconciliation were commanded (4:114) and where prayer was guarded and remembered (4:102–103). Where the sūrah says *“do not let desires deviate from justice; if you distort or refuse He is All-Aware”* (4:135), hypocrisy deviates maximally — twisting testimony and refusing it — so depth is maximal and helper none.
verses.146:
> except those who repent, mend their ways, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their devotion to Allah; they will be with the believers. And Allah will grant the believers a great reward

**Except Those Who Repent, Mend, Hold Fast, and Are Sincere**

The verse states *illā alladhīna tābū wa aṣlaḥū wa iʿtaṣamū bi Allāhi wa akhlaṣū dīnahum li Allāhi* — except those who repent, turned. Mended, set right, and held fast, clung, to God, and made their religion, devotion, sincere, pure for God. *Tābū* — to repent, to return — was explained with *tawbah* as the sūrah’s return after evil soon after error (4:17) before death’s *now I repent* (4:18), after deceit (4:106–110), after *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds”* (4:110). *Wa aṣlaḥū* — and mended, set right — was explained as mending what was corrupted: where night plotting disordered (4:108), where throwing sin on innocent burdened (4:112), where honour was sought among disbelievers (4:139), where sitting where signs are mocked made like them (4:140) — mending is *iṣlāḥ bayna al-nāsi* the good secret talk (4:114). *Wa iʿtaṣamū bi Allāhi* — and held fast to God, clung — was explained as the same *iʿtiṣām* commanded where those who believe in God and hold fast to Him will be admitted into mercy and guided through Straight Path (4:175), and where the emigrant to God has reward secured (4:100). *Wa akhlaṣū dīnahum li Allāhi* — and made devotion sincere, pure, for Him — was read as *ikhlāṣ* — purity from showing off where they stood lazy to be seen (4:142) and spent to show off (4:38); sincerity is the opposite of *riyāʾ* and of seeking *ʿizzah* among disbelievers (4:139). The four were explained as the hypocrite’s reversal: repentance reverses oscillation (4:137), mending reverses night plotting, holding fast reverses alliance with disbelievers instead of believers (4:144), sincerity reverses standing to be seen.

**They Will Be With the Believers**

The promise *fa ulāʾika maʿa al-muʾminīna* — then those — the repentant, mending, holding, sincere — will be with the believers, among them, counted as them — was explained with *maʿa* — with, together — the same *maʿa* the waiters claimed falsely — *were we not with you?* (4:141) — now true. To be *with believers* was read as not merely spared from lowest depth (4:145) but transferred to the other gathering: hypocrites and disbelievers gathered together in Hell (4:140) versus believers gathered with honourable company — prophets, truthful, martyrs, righteous (4:69). The sūrah has shown that those who obey God and Messenger will be with those blessed (4:69) and that whoever defies the Messenger and follows other than believers’ path is left to that path (4:115). Those who repent and are sincere are returned to the believers’ path — *sabili al-muʾminīn* — after being torn between neither (4:143). The phrase was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, God’s promise ever true”* (4:122): to be with believers is to share that promise whose word none exceeds.

**A Verse That Follows Lowest Depth With Highest Return**

Placed after *hypocrites in lowest depths of Fire, you will never find helper* (4:145), this verse follows lowest with return. The sūrah has announced painful punishment to hypocrites (4:138), shown honour sought wrongly, sitting where mocked, waiting between, deceiving, lazy prayer, wavering, alliance giving clear proof against selves (4:138–144); here the same hypocrites — the *munāfiqīn* — are given four steps: repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere. The sūrah has shown that *“why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing”* (4:147) — punishment is not needed where gratitude and faith are; these four are the gratitude and faith made operational. The sūrah that asks *“was not God’s earth spacious enough to emigrate?”* (4:97) and promises many havens (4:100) here says earth’s spaciousness includes a haven from lowest depth to being with believers, via sincerity. For the weak the sūrah lightens: where standing for justice though against yourselves was hard (4:135), holding fast to God is the stand; where settlement is best (4:128), mending is the settlement with Him; where *shuḥḥ* was present (4:128), sincerity removes it.
verses.147:
> Why should Allah punish you if you are grateful and faithful? Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing

**Why Should God Punish You If You Are Grateful and Faithful?**

The verse opens *mā yafʿalu Allāhu bi ʿadhābikum in shakartum wa āmantum* — what will God do with your punishment, why should He punish you, if you are grateful and have faith, are thankful and believing. *Mā yafʿalu bi ʿadhābikum* — what would He do with punishing you, what need for your punishment — was explained as rhetorical negation: He has no need to punish, as He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) though you disobey still to Him belongs all. He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet does not punish where gratitude and faith are. *In shakartum wa āmantum* — if you are grateful and faithful — was read with *shukr* — gratitude, thankfulness — and *īmān* — faith, belief — the two that make the four — repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere (4:146) — the gratitude and faith that replace being torn between neither (4:143) and taking allies instead of believers (4:144). *Shakartum* was explained as gratitude shown in act: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114), doing good male or female with faith (4:124), submitting face doing good following Abraham (4:125), standing for justice (4:135), holding fast to Him (4:175). *Wa āmantum* — and have faith — was explained as comprehensive faith in God, Messenger, Books, angels, Last Day (4:136) renewed without wavering (4:136) — steadfast versus the oscillation that increased (4:137). Early reports linked the verse to the repentant hypocrites just promised being with believers and great reward (4:146): why should He punish if they are now grateful and faithful? The sūrah has shown that whoever seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving after evil (4:110) and that He forgives what is less than association for whom He wills (4:116); gratitude and faith are the seeking made character.

**Allah Is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Shākiran ʿAlīmā* — And God is ever Appreciative, Thankful, Rewarding, All-Knowing — was explained with *Shākir* — Appreciative, Grateful, Repaying — the One who appreciates the grateful, rewards *shukr* with increase — *“if you are grateful I will increase you”* (14:7). *Shākir* was read as that He rewards the thankful who is grateful with great reward, as *“He will grant believers a great reward”* (4:146) and *“great is His favour upon you”* (4:113). *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — was explained as knowing gratitude and faith where they are hidden, as He is Fully Aware encompassing everything (4:126), All-Aware of what you do (4:128, 4:135), All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) — nothing of *shukr* or *īmān* escapes. The sūrah has sealed many acts with knowledge names — *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* where sin is earned (4:111), *Muḥīṭ* where night plots (4:108); here *Shākir ʿAlīm* seals grateful faith as the act He rewards.

**A Verse That Follows Repentance With Principle**

Placed after *except those who repent, mend, hold fast, are sincere, they will be with believers and He will grant believers great reward* (4:146), this verse follows repentance with principle that explains why repentance works: why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? The sūrah has announced painful punishment to hypocrites (4:138) and lowest depth without helper (4:145) — yet showed exception; the principle answers implied question: does He punish because He needs to? — *mā yafʿalu* — He has no need, as He is Self-Sufficient (4:131) and suffices as Trustee (4:132). Where He can remove and bring others (4:133), He does not need to keep punishing. Where with Him are both rewards (4:134), He needs not withhold. The principle therefore transforms threat into invitation: the same God who declared *“neither by your wishes”* (4:123) and *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) says His *ʿadhāb* is not sought for itself; gratitude and faith remove its cause, and being Appreciative He rewards them. The sūrah’s ethic — stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135), have faith entire (4:136) — is therefore not burden but gratitude that He appreciates.

The chapter that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* (4:1), showed ownership to Him of heavens and earth, sufficiency as Trustee, capability to replace (4:126–133), warned not to take allies instead of believers lest you give clear proof against yourselves (4:144), declared lowest depth without helper (4:145) yet opened except for four — now says punishment itself is not His need, gratitude and faith are what He appreciates and knows.
verses.148:
> Allah does not like negative thoughts to be voiced—except by those who have been wronged. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing

**God Does Not Like Negative Thoughts Voiced — Except by Wronged**

The verse states *lā yuḥibbu Allāhu al-jahra bi al-sūʾi mina al-qawli illā man ẓulim* — God does not like, does not love, the loud voicing — *jahr* — of evil, bad, of speech, except by those who have been wronged, oppressed. *Al-jahra bi al-sūʾi mina al-qawli* — to voice evil loudly, to proclaim bad speech — was explained as public negative speech, complaint, accusation, vile talk, prayer against, as the sūrah has shown that those who hide from people but God is with them where they plot displeasing speech (4:108) have *sūʾ al-qawl* — evil speech — that He dislikes. That advocates who dispute in this life for wrongdoers use evil loud speech (4:107–109). *Lā yuḥibbu* — does not like — parallels *does not like the deceitful sinner* (4:107) and *does not like the stingy boastful* (4:37); to voice *sūʾ* loudly is disliked as *shuḥḥ* and *khiyānah* are. *Illā man ẓulim* — except those who have been wronged — was explained as permission for the oppressed who cried for a helper — *mustaḍʿafīn* who cry *“deliver us from land of oppressors, appoint for us a saviour and helper”* (4:75) — to voice their wrong, to complain of oppression, to invoke against oppressor, to report injustice. The sūrah elsewhere commands to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135) and permits settlement best (4:128) yet acknowledges *“no good in most secret talks”* (4:114). Public *sūʾ* is the broad prohibition where secret plotting was already condemned, with exception for the wronged as the previous exception for helpless (4:98) — not every loud complaint is evil, the wronged’s is allowed.

**Allah Is All-Hearing, All-Knowing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Samīʿan ʿAlīman* — And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, was ever — was explained with *Samīʿ* — hearing every *jahr* — loud voicing — and every *najwā* — secret talk — (4:114) and every night plot displeasing (4:108) — and *ʿAlīm* — knowing whether loud voicing is *sūʾ* or complaint of wronged, whether settlement sought graciously (4:128) or inclination total (4:129). *Samīʿ ʿAlīm* has sealed the command to return trusts and judge fairly (4:58) as *Samīʿ Baṣīr*. The both rewards are with Him (4:134) as *Samīʿ Baṣīr*; here *Samīʿ ʿAlīm* fits speech: He hears loud evil and knows its motive, as He hears the oppressed cry (4:75) and knows the *ḥīla* absent (4:98). Early reports illustrated *man ẓulim* with one whose property was usurped or who was wronged by a spouse’s *nushūz* and who voices it for redress, not for slander — He hears and knows the difference between reporting wrong for justice and throwing sin on innocent as *buhtān* (4:112). The pairing says: public evil speech is disliked, yet He hears the wronged’s allowed voicing and knows its equity.

**A Verse That Follows Grateful Faith With Discipline of Loud Speech**

Placed after *why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing* (4:147), this verse follows grateful faith with discipline of loud speech. The sūrah has shown that whoever is grateful and faithful, He appreciates and knows; to voice *sūʾ* loudly is ingratitude in speech, as the deceitful’s night speech displeases Him (4:108) and advocates’ dispute for self-wrongers in this life is loud *sūʾ* — therefore *He does not like*. The exception *except wronged* was read as the sūrah’s justice: the oppressed whose help was commanded to be fought for (4:75), whose earth is made spacious (4:100), whose prayer is shortened and guarded (4:101–102) — their loud voicing is not *sūʾ* but *ḥaqq* — demand for right. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good* (4:114) except three, now warns *loud evil has no love* except one — the wronged’s. The sūrah that says *He wills to make clear* (4:26) and *taught you what you did not know* (4:113) makes loud evil undesirable because knowledge and wisdom will judge it as *ʿAlīm* hearing as *Samīʿ*.
verses.149:
> Whether you reveal or conceal a good or pardon an evil—surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable

**Whether You Reveal or Conceal a Good or Pardon Evil**

The verse states *in tubdū khayran aw tukhfūhu aw taʿfū ʿan sūʾin* — whether you reveal, display, a good, make it apparent, or conceal it, hide it, or pardon, efface, an evil, bad deed. *Tubdū khayran* — to reveal a good — was explained as doing good openly: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) where secret talk except those three has no good. Standing for justice as witnesses for Him even against yourselves (4:135) where testimony is revealing good. *Aw tukhfūhu* — or conceal it, hide it — was explained as doing good secretly: the charity waived charitably as blood-money (4:92) or dowry graciously waived (4:4), the good hidden where showing would be *riyāʾ* — showing off (4:38, 4:142). Both — revealing and concealing — were read as equal where intention is His pleasure, as *“whether you reveal or conceal a good”* the sūrah says both are known. *Aw taʿfū ʿan sūʾin* — or pardon an evil, overlook, efface a bad from another — was explained as pardoning the forgivable wrong done to you, after the permission for the wronged to voice loudly (4:148) was given; pardoning after voicing is the higher. The sūrah has shown that settlement is best where she fears *nushūz* (4:128) and that settlement involves mutual graciousness; pardoning evil is that graciousness where grievance was voiced.

**Surely God Is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable**

The seal *fa inna Allāha kāna ʿAfuwwan Qadīrā* — surely God is, was ever, Ever-Pardoning, effacing, Most Capable, Powerful — was explained with *ʿAfuww* — much effacing, wiping away trace — the name that seals the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) and the reminder that He is Ever-Pardoning before prayer where purity is sought (4:43). *Qadīr* — Most Capable, Powerful over all — was explained as that He pardons though capable to punish, as He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet appreciates gratitude (4:147), as He owns heavens and earth (4:126) yet forgives what is less than association (4:116). To be *ʿAfuww Qadīr* was read as that pardoning evil after being wronged is divine imitation: you pardon though you are capable to voice and retaliate, as He pardons though He is Most Capable to punish. The pairing was linked to *“He does not like loud negative speech except by wronged, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing”* (4:148) — the wronged is allowed to voice, yet the higher is to pardon, because the All-Hearing hears the wronged’s voicing and the *ʿAfuww Qadīr* shows the pardon that surpasses it. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant’s reward is secured though He could withhold (4:100), and that both rewards are with Him though He could give none; *ʿAfuww Qadīr* is that generosity made character for the believer.

**Revealing or Concealing — Both Known, Both Rewarded**

The equalisation — *in tubdū … aw tukhfūhu* — was explained as removing show: whether good is displayed or hidden, it is good before Him who owns heavens and earth (4:126) and who is Fully Aware (4:126) and All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134). To reveal is not automatically *riyāʾ*, to conceal not automatically sincerity; both are *khayr* where sought for His pleasure (4:114). The verse was linked to *“everyone will find whatever good they did present”* (?) and to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40): the revealed atom and the concealed atom are both present before the *ʿAlīm*. The addition *aw taʿfū ʿan sūʾ* was read as the highest *khayr*: pardoning the evil done to you is good concealed as forbearance, yet its effacement is most like His *ʿafw*. He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing”* (4:147) — gratitude for good is shown by doing good whether revealed or hidden, and pardoning evil is gratitude that He is *ʿAfuww*.

The next passage will turn from speech and pardon to creed: those who deny Him and His messengers making distinction between Him and messengers desiring compromise — they are true disbelievers, humiliating punishment prepared (4:150–151).
verses.150:
> Surely those who deny Allah and His messengers and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others,” desiring to forge a compromise

**Saying — We Believe in Some and Disbelieve in Others**

The speech *wa yaqūlūna nuʾminu bi baʿḍin wa nakfuru bi baʿḍin* — and they say, we believe in some and disbelieve in others, in some messengers we believe and in others we disbelieve — was explained as the distinction’s formula, the same compromise condemned where *“O believers, have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures He revealed before”* (4:136) commanded comprehensive faith without selecting. *Nuʾminu bi baʿḍ* — we believe in some — was read as the partial faith that wishes grace by belonging — *neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — here the wish is *we believe in some messengers* as our group. *Wa nakfuru bi baʿḍ* — we disbelieve in some — was read as denial of those sent before and after, as the sūrah will say *they are true disbelievers* (4:151) and *those who believe in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards* (4:152). The sūrah has shown that those who believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137) make similar speech; the formula *we believe in some and disbelieve in others* was explained as hypocrisy’s creedal side: to be *mudhabdhab* between neither these nor those (4:143) doctrinally. The phrase was linked to *“they say we hear and disobey”* (4:46) where Jews distort words; here distortion is selection of messengers.

**Desiring to Forge a Compromise**

The intention *wa yurīdūna a yattakhidhū bayna dhālika sabīlā* — and they wish, intend, to take, to forge between that — between belief in some and disbelief in some — a way, a path, a compromise — was explained with *sabīl* — way — the same *sabīl* the sūrah guides to noble ways (4:26), Satan wishes the deviant far path (4:60), believers’ path not to be left (4:115). Association far straying (4:116). *Bayna dhālika sabīlā* — between that a way — was read as seeking a middle way that is neither belief nor disbelief, neither *īmān* nor *kufr*, but a compromise doctrine where God is accepted and some messengers rejected. The sūrah has shown that *settlement is best* (4:128) where equitable compromise between spouses is good, but compromise between God and messengers is not settlement; it is *tafrīq*. The sūrah has also shown that *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) — to take a way between believing and denying is the secret talk that has no good. The verse generalises the particular hypocrisy of waiting between winners (4:141) into theology: waiting between messengers to believe some and disbelieve some is desiring a *sabīl bayna dhālika* that is not a *sabīl* but straying left where no way is found (4:143).

**The Distinction That the Sūrah Has Named Two Kinds**

The phrase *yufarriqū bayna Allāhi wa rusulihī* was contrasted with the two distinctions the sūrah has condemned: distinguishing between *wishes* — *your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — and distinguishing between *messengers* — *we believe in some and disbelieve in others*. Both are *tafrīq* that seeks a *sabī l bayna dhālika* where none is, and both are answered with comprehensive faith: *believe in God, Messenger, Book and Scriptures, angels, Last Day* (4:136) and *believe in God and His messengers accepting all* (4:152). The verse was read as the sūrah’s answer to compromise theology: the only *sabīl* that is — is the believers’ path (4:115), submission fully to Him doing good following Abraham ḥanīf (4:125) — not a path between distinguishing. The next verse will declare the verdict: they are indeed the true disbelievers, and We have prepared for disbelievers a humiliating punishment (4:151).
verses.151:
> they are indeed the true disbelievers. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment

**They Are Indeed the True Disbelievers**

The verse completes *ulāʾika humu al-kāfirūna ḥaqqan* — they are — those who deny God and messengers and wish to distinguish between Him and His messengers saying *we believe in some and disbelieve in some desiring a way between* (4:150) — indeed, truly, the disbelievers in truth, the true disbelievers. *Ḥaqqan* — truly, in truth, as right, as due — was explained as the Book’s verdict after judgment by what He shows (4:105) that distinguishing God from messengers is not compromise but *kufr* in full, as *“whoever denies God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day has gone far astray”* (4:136). *Humu al-kāfirūna* — they are the disbelievers — was read with emphasis: not merely among disbelievers. They are them, for the sūrah has shown that taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers gives Him clear warrant against yourselves (4:144) and sitting where revelations are denied makes you like them (4:140). To make distinction between God and messengers is that like-ness made creed, so the verdict is *ḥaqq* — true — as God’s promise is *ḥaqq* (4:122) and Book was sent *bi al-ḥaqq* with truth (4:105). The sūrah has said *“they do not believe except few”* where hearts were sealed for disbelief (4:155); here *ḥaqqan* marks those few who believe as distinct from those truly disbelievers. Early reports added that hypocrisy’s *mudhabdhab* between neither these nor those (4:143) is not neutral: to desire a way between distinguishing is *ḥaqqan* disbelief.

**And We Have Prepared for Disbelievers a Humiliating Punishment**

The preparation *wa aʿtadnā li al-kāfirīna ʿadhāban muhīnā* — and We have prepared, made ready, for disbelievers a humiliating, degrading, debasing punishment — was explained with *aʿtadnā* — prepared, as the humiliating punishment was prepared for disbelievers where prayer was guarded under arms (4:102: *We have prepared humiliating punishment for disbelievers*). For those given a portion who hide bounty (4:37: *humiliating punishment for disbelievers*), and will be for those who oppose the Messenger (4:115: *humiliating punishment* implicit). *ʿAdhāban muhīnā* — humiliating punishment — was read as humiliation corresponding to the *ʿizzah* — honour — they sought among disbelievers as allies (4:139) where *all honour belongs to Him completely* — the honour sought among the wrong company becomes humiliation prepared. The sūrah has shown that the intentions to deceive God while He outwits (4:142) and to deceive the Prophet while grace protects (4:113) end in humiliation where deception’s honour is inverted. Where the sūrah says *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God clear proof against yourselves?”* (4:144) — *sulṭān mubīn* — preparation of humiliating punishment is the proof made sanction, because proof against yourselves was made clear by distinguishing.

**A Verse That Completes Distinction With Verdict**

The sūrah has shown that belief was commanded as comprehensive — *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before* (4:136) — steadfast, not selective, as the Way of Abraham pure (4:125) was not selective among associates. To be selective among messengers is to undo that comprehensive faith. The sūrah has shown that those who believe and do good are in Gardens true where promise is *ḥaqq* (4:122), while those who disbelieve are in Hell without escape (4:121); humiliating punishment is the disbeliever’s analog to honour sought. The phrase *aʿtadnā* — prepared — was linked to *“We have prepared humiliating punishment for disbelievers”* where guarded prayer stands (4:102): as prayer under arms guards against the enemy who wishes you neglect for a sweep (4:102), humiliating punishment guards against the theology that wishes you accept half the messengers and reject half as compromise. Elsewhere the Book ties that guard to *“Gardens under rivers where they abide forever”* (4:122) — comprehensive faith is the Gardens’ price, distinction its loss, and the comparison steadies the choice.
verses.152:
> As for those who believe in Allah and His messengers—accepting all; rejecting none—He will surely give them their rewards. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful

**Those Who Believe in God and Messengers — Accepting All, Rejecting None**

The verse states *wa alladhīna āmanū bi Allāhi wa rusulihī wa lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum* — and those who believe, have faith, in God and His messengers and did not make distinction between any of them, any one among them. *Āmanū bi Allāhi wa rusulihī* was explained as the comprehensive faith just commanded — *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures He revealed before* (4:136) — now as description of its people. *Wa lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum* — and did not make distinction between any one of them — was read as the opposite of *wishing to make distinction between God and messengers saying we believe in some and disbelieve in some desiring a way between* (4:150) where verdict was *true disbelievers, humiliating preparation* (4:151). To not distinguish between any messenger was explained as to accept all — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David We gave Psalms”* (4:163) — all are God’s, none rejected. The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven yet demanded greater — *show God visible* from Moses (4:153) — and then took calf; distinguishing among messengers is that demand’s theology: to accept Moses but not Jesus or Muhammad ﷺ is modern calf after clear signs. To not distinguish was also linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — comprehensive belief is part of that good, as *millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* (4:125) included all prophets in Abraham’s way.

**He Will Surely Give Them Their Rewards**

The promise *ulāʾika sawfa yuʾtīhim ujūrahum* — then to those — the comprehensive believers — He will surely, will soon, give them their rewards, their wages — was explained with *sawfa* — will, soon — certainty as the emigrant’s secured wage (4:100) and great reward for commanding charity (4:114) and great reward for being with believers after repentance (4:146). *Ujūrahum* — their rewards, wages — was read as *ajr* — wage — the same *ajr* that hypocrites sought as *ʿizzah* among disbelievers (4:139) but belong to Him completely (4:139) and are both rewards with Him (4:134) — the believers’ wage is from Him, not from company sought. The verse generalises the promise where *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) — the comprehensive believer is that doer. And *“who is better than those who submit face doing good following Abraham?”* (4:125) — submission includes accepting all messengers, so reward is friendship as Abraham was taken *khalīl* (4:125). Early notes linked *ujūrahum* to *“God wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26): wages are the mercy guided to.

**And God Is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — And God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, was ever — was explained with *Ghafūr* — much forgiving, covering — and *Raḥīm* — ever merciful — the pair that seals grateful faith not punished (4:147), seeking forgiveness found (4:110), and universal pardon for less than association (4:116). To seal comprehensive belief with *Ghafūr Raḥīm* was read as that those who believe in all messengers still have faults needing cover, as the sūrah has shown that strivers need forgiveness among ranks (4:96) and emigrants find havens though weakness remains (4:100). *Ghafūr Raḥīm* here contrasts with *ʿadhāban muhīnā* — humiliating punishment prepared for true disbelievers (4:151) — showing that distinction’s wage is humiliation, comprehensiveness’s wage is forgiveness and mercy besides reward. Where the sūrah says *“He does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) and *“you will never be wronged even speck on date stone”* (4:124), the comprehensive believer’s reward is the atom not wronged yet multiplied many times; the Seal says the Multiplier is Forgiving, Merciful.

**A Verse That Follows True Disbelief With True Belief**

Placed after *they are indeed true disbelievers, We have prepared for disbelievers humiliating punishment* (4:151), this verse follows true disbelief with true belief and its opposite preparation: not humiliating punishment prepared but rewards given and forgiveness, mercy. The sūrah has moved from the passage on women, settlement, enrichment (4:127–130) through universal command to be mindful (4:131), trusteeship, capability, both rewards (4:131–134), standing for justice (4:135) with five articles of faith (4:136), oscillation without forgiveness or way (4:137), announcement of painful to hypocrites (4:138), alliance for honour (4:139), sitting where mocked as like them (4:140), waiting between winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted, lazy prayer (4:142), torn between (4:143), alliance giving clear proof (4:144), lowest depth without helper (4:145) except four — repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere (4:146) — the principle *why punish if grateful and faithful?* (4:147) — the discipline of loud evil except by wronged (4:148) and pardoning though capable (4:149) — distinguishing between God and messengers desiring a way between (4:150). Here the opposite distinction — not distinguishing between any messenger — is rewarded. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) names comprehensive acceptance as the just faith.
verses.153:
> The People of the Book demand that you ˹O Prophet˺ bring down for them a revelation in writing from heaven. They demanded what is even greater than this from Moses, saying, “Make Allah visible to us!” So a thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf for worship after receiving clear signs. Still We forgave them for that ˹after their repentance˺ and gave Moses compelling proof

**The People of the Book Demand a Book From Heaven**

The verse opens *yasʾaluka ahlu al-kitābi a tunazzila ʿalayhim kitāban mina al-samāʾi* — the People of the Book ask you, demand of you, that you bring down upon them a book from the sky, a revelation in writing from heaven. *Ahlu al-kitābi* — People of the Book — was explained as Jews and Christians given Scripture before you — the same before you commanded to be mindful (4:131) — whose wishes are not the measure (4:123) and who were given a portion yet trade it for misguidance (4:44). *Yasʾaluka* — ask, demand — was read as challenging demand, as the sūrah has shown that they demand what is greater than this from Moses — *“make God visible”* — a demand that exceeds bringing a book from heaven. *An tunazzila kitāban mina al-samāʾ* — to bring down a book from heaven — was explained as requesting a written revelation descending as sheets, a physical book, as the Meccans demanded signs and as earlier they asked Moses to show God. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and that God bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166); to demand a book from heaven as condition is to condition belief on spectacle. Early reports noted this demand followed the Prophet’s recitation of comprehensive faith (4:152): they said, if you are among messengers, bring a book as Moses brought tablets, otherwise we make distinction as before (4:150) — the sūrah exposes demand as continuation of distinguishing.

The consequence *fa akhadhat-humu al-ṣāʿiqatu bi ẓulmihim* — so the thunderbolt seized them, struck them, for their wrongdoing — was explained with *ṣāʿiqah* — thunderbolt, striking — the same punishment that seized others who demanded signs with wrongdoing. *Bi ẓulmihim* — for their wrong, injustice — was read as that demand for visible God was injustice, as associating is far straying (4:116) and defying the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose (4:115). *Thumma ittakhadhū al-ʿijla min baʿdi mā jāʾathumu al-bayyinātu* — then they took the calf for worship after clear signs came to them — was explained with *ʿijl* — calf — the golden calf worshipped while Moses was on the Mount, after receiving *bayyināt* — clear signs, evidences — the staff, the sea parted, the Mount raised over them (4:154). Elsewhere the chapter notes they invoke female gods besides Him as Satan (4:117) and slit ears and alter creation (4:119); calf worship is the same — altering creation of respected animal into object of worship, then worshipping it.

**Still We Forgave Them and Gave Moses Compelling Proof**

The mercy *fa ʿafawnā ʿan dhālika wa ātaynā Mūsā sulṭānan mubīnā* — still We pardoned them for that, after their repentance. We gave Moses clear, compelling, manifest authority, proof — was explained with *ʿafawnā* — We pardoned, effaced — the same root *ʿAfuww* — Ever-Pardoning (4:99, 4:149) — who pardons though Most Capable (4:149). The chapter has already noted that whoever wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110) and that the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99); here the calf-takers were forgiven after repentance where *“kill yourselves”* after calf was commanded (2:54). *Sulṭānan mubīnā* — clear warrant, compelling proof — was explained as the manifest authority Moses was given: tablets, the Mount raised, the *bayyināt* — clear signs — the sūrah will enumerate as Mount raised for covenant, *“enter the gate with humility, do not break Sabbath, firm covenant”* (4:154). The phrase *sulṭān mubīn* appears where hostile turners are given clear warrant over them (4:91) and where giving God clear warrant against yourselves is warned (4:144); here Moses’ *sulṭān mubīn* is the proof against those who demanded greater than a book.

*Arinā Allāha jahratan* — show us God manifest, visibly, openly — was explained as demand for theophany, to see the Lord with eyes, as the sūrah elsewhere recounts *“they said, O Moses, we will not believe until we see God plainly, so the thunderbolt seized them”* (2:55).
verses.154:
> We raised the Mount over them ˹as a warning˺ for ˹breaking˺ their covenant and said, “Enter the gate ˹of Jerusalem˺ with humility.” We also warned them, “Do not break the Sabbath,” and took from them a firm covenant

**We Raised the Mount Over Them for Their Covenant**

The verse states *wa rafaʿnā fawqahumu al-ṭūra bi mīthāqihim* — and We raised the Mount — *al-Ṭūr* — Sinai, the mountain — over them, above them, because of their covenant, for breaking their covenant. *Rafaʿnā fawqahum* — We raised above them — was explained as God lifting Sinai over the Children of Israel as canopy until they accepted the covenant at Moses’ return, after the calf after clear signs had been forgiven and Moses given compelling proof — *sulṭānan mubīnā* (4:153). *Bi mīthāqihim* — for their covenant, with their covenant — was read as because the covenant required lifting as warning, as the sūrah has shown that *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126) and He is *Muḥīṭ* — encompassing (4:126) — the Mount raised is His ownership displayed. The sūrah has traced *mīthāq* — covenant — from the firm commitment of marriage — *mīthāq ghalīẓ* (4:21) — to treaty with covenanted peoples (4:90, 4:92) — to the firm covenant with the Children of Israel. To raise a mountain over them for breaking it was explained as the visible *sulṭān mubīn* that Moses was given (4:153) made physical, so that the covenant not kept remains above until kept.

**And We Took From Them a Firm Covenant**

The closure *wa akhadhnā minhum mīthāqan ghalīẓā* — and We took from them a firm, strong, solemn covenant — was explained with *ghalīẓ* — firm, weighty, strong — the same *mīthāq ghalīẓ* taken from women upon marriage (4:21) where dowry is not taken back unjustly — here the covenant with the community at Sinai. *Akhadhnā* — We took — was read as divine taking as witness, as *“God bears witness to what He sent”* (4:166) — the covenant is witnessed by the Mountain raised and by the gate entered. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); the firm covenant is the Book’s predecessor where the Mount was the witness. Early reports noted that the firmer the covenant, the firmer the punishment for breaking it — the thunderbolt struck them for demand greater than a book (4:153) — yet the *ʿafw* — pardoning — after calf showed the covenant also carries forgiveness where sought (4:110). The firm covenant was also linked to *taqwā* commanded to those before you and you (4:131) — *be mindful* — the covenant is the form of that *waṣiyyah*.

**The Firm Covenant Above as Guardian**

The image — Mount above them for covenant — was explained as that the sūrah’s ownership — *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126) — becomes canopy, as prayer under arms was canopy guarded (4:102) and trusteeship suffices (4:132). The firm covenant — *ghalīẓ* — that is taken from them parallels the firm commitment taken from wives where wealth is entrusted (4:21); both teach that God’s earth is spacious (4:100) but covenant is not spacious to break. The verse generalises the sūrah’s warning *do not consume wealth unjustly* (4:29) into *do not transgress the Sabbath* — both are limits. The next verse will name the breaking: for breaking their covenant, rejecting His signs, killing prophets unjustly, saying *our hearts are unreceptive* — He sealed hearts for disbelief, so they believe only few — (4:155).

*Udkhulū al-bāba sujjadan* — enter the gate in prostration, bowing, humbled — was read as the entry into Jerusalem after wandering, where *“enter the gate with humility and say *ḥiṭṭa* — relief, forgiveness — We will forgive and increase the doers of good”* (2:58).

To enter humbly was explained as the opposite of invoking female gods besides Him (4:117). To be told *lā taʿdū fī al-sabti* — do not transgress the Sabbath, do not exceed limits on the seventh day — was read as that the Sabbath was made test for them, as the sūrah elsewhere recounts the Sabbath-breaking town turned to apes (7:166).
verses.155:
> ˹They were condemned˺ for breaking their covenant, rejecting Allah’s signs, killing the prophets unjustly, and for saying, “Our hearts are unreceptive!”—it is Allah Who has sealed their hearts for their disbelief, so they do not believe except for a few—

**For Breaking Covenant, Rejecting Signs, Killing Prophets**

The verse opens *fa bi mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum wa kufrihim bi āyāti Allāhi wa qatlihim al-anbiyāʾa bi ghayri ḥaqq* — so for their breaking their covenant. Rejecting His signs, and killing the prophets — *anbiyāʾ* — without right. *Bi mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum* — for their breaking their covenant — corresponds to the firm covenant taken at the Mount raised over them and the gate with humility and Sabbath restraint (4:154): where Mount was raised for covenant, they broke it. *Wa kufrihim bi āyāti Allāhi* — and rejecting, covering His signs — was explained as denying the *bayyināt* — clear signs — after which calf was taken (4:153) and Mount raised (4:154): staff, sea, manna, cloud, tablets — all *sulṭān mubīn* Moses was given. *Wa qatlihim al-anbiyāʾa bi ghayri ḥaqq* — and killing prophets without right, unjustly — was explained as murdering some prophets where *“whenever a messenger came with what souls desired not, you grew arrogant, some you denied, some you killed”* (2:87), culminating later with try on Jesus, son of Mary, messenger of God (4:157). The sūrah has traced murder’s weight: devouring orphans’ wealth is fire (4:10), killing a believer intentionally is Hell with anger and curse (4:93), throwing sin on the innocent bears slander (4:112) — killing prophets without right is the furthest throw: to throw God’s word back by killing its carrier. The phrase was linked to *“they were condemned for breaking covenant”* as the sūrah’s ledger where *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123).

**It Is God Who Has Sealed Hearts for Disbelief**

The correction *bal ṭabaʿa Allāhu ʿalayhā bi kufrihim* — rather, it is God who has sealed, stamped, upon them, over hearts, for their disbelief, because of their disbelief — was explained as divine sealing after human rejection. *Bi kufrihim* — for their *kufr*, because of their covering — was explained as that He left to stray where they pursued what they chose: *We will let them pursue what they chose* (4:115) after defying the Messenger. *whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way* (4:88, 4:143) — sealing is that leaving. The phrase was linked to *“God has condemned them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except few”* (4:46) where some Jews take words out of context — sealing there also followed distortion. The sūrah has shown that *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — sealing is not where gratitude and faith are, but where *kufr* repeats.

**So They Do Not Believe Except for Few**

The outcome *fa lā yuʾminūna illā qalīlā* — so they do not believe — will not believe — except for a little, except a few — was explained with *qalīl* — little, few — as little belief after sealing, as the sūrah says *we took calf after clear signs yet forgave* (4:153) — some repented — and *but those well-grounded in knowledge among them believe in what was revealed to you and before you* (4:162) — few stand firm. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever believes in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards”* (4:152) — the few who believe except few are those who accepted all without distinction (4:150–152). *Illā qalīlan* — except a few — was linked to the beginning where *“you were divided into two groups about hypocrites while God allowed regression because of misdeeds”* (4:88) — few remained straight. The exception preserves hope where the lowest depth for hypocrites also allowed *except those who repent* (4:146): sealing is not absolute where a few believe.

The next verses will continue that condemnation: for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary. Boasting *we killed the Messiah, son of Mary, messenger of God* — but they killed not nor crucified — it was made to appear so — they have no knowledge, only assumptions — they certainly did not kill him (4:156–157).
verses.156:
> and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary

**And for Their Denial and Outrageous Accusation Against Mary**

The verse continues *wa bi kufrihim wa qawlihim ʿalā Maryama buhtānan ʿaẓīmā* — and for their denial, their *kufr*, and their word against Mary, their saying upon Mary as a tremendous, mighty slander — *buhtān ʿaẓīm*. *Bi kufrihim* — for their denial — was explained as continuation of the accumulated causes for condemnation — breaking covenant, rejecting signs, killing prophets unjustly, saying hearts are *ghulf* sealed for disbelief (4:155) — now denial as such and slander against Maryam. *Wa qawlihim ʿalā Maryama buhtānan ʿaẓīmā* — and their saying against Mary as mighty slander — was explained with *buhtān* — slander, calumny, false accusation that bewilders — the same *buhtān* and manifest sin borne by whoever throws sin on the innocent (4:112), now against the innocent Maryam, mother of the Messiah. *ʿAẓīm* — mighty, tremendous, great — was explained as that slander against Maryam is not private insult but defamation of the *ṣiddīqah* chosen, the Word through her — *“the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was but messenger of God and His Word through Mary and spirit from Him”* (4:171), whose mother was *“above women of the worlds”* in reports. Those who consume orphans’ wealth consume fire (4:10) and throwing sin on the innocent bears slander (4:112); to slander Maryam with unchastity — accusing the pure who was given a spirit — is the throw of sin upon the purest, therefore *ʿaẓīm*. Early reports noted that the Jews who rejected Jesus accused Maryam of *zina* — fornication — to deny his messengership, as they denied all messengers where distinguishing is true disbelief (4:151); the verse names the slander as *buhtān ʿaẓīm* because it combines denial of a prophet with defamation of his mother.

Placed after broken covenant, rejecting signs, killing prophets, saying hearts are *ghulf* sealed (4:155), this verse continues the same condemnation with the next instance: denial and mighty slander against Mary. Demand for a book from heaven and the greater demand — *show God visible* — were struck, followed by the calf after clear signs yet forgiven (4:153). The Mount raised for firm covenant (4:154); slander against Mary is the next breaking: after calf — idol — after rejecting signs, they reject the sign of Mary’s purity and Jesus’ birth without father as Word. The later reminder that *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David We gave Psalms”* (4:163) — all accepted without distinction (4:152) — shows that to slander Mary is to reject that chain that includes Jesus. The verse was linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — Mary believed and did good; to accuse her is to refuse that good. For the weak this is protective: where orphan women deprived yet wished to marry are protected from being married for profit (4:127), Mary the most deprived — alone — is protected by God naming slander against her as *ʿaẓīm*.

**The *Buhtān* That Mirrors Throwing Sin on the Innocent**

The word *buhtān* — mighty slander — was explained to mirror *iḥtamala buhtānan wa ithman mubīnā* — bears slander and manifest sin — where one throws sin on the innocent (4:112). There the innocent was a neighbour Jew accused of theft; here the innocent is Maryam, accused to deny messengership. Earlier passages note that *“there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation”* (4:114); slander of Mary is the evil secret talk that has no good. Elsewhere the Book teaches that *“He does not like loud negative speech except by wronged”* (4:148) — accusation against Mary is negative speech not by wronged but by wrongdoer, therefore not allowed, therefore not liked, therefore *ʿaẓīm*. That same teaching was linked to *“He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing”* (4:148): the accusers of Mary voiced *buhtān ʿaẓīm* where they were not wronged but wronging.
verses.157:
> and for boasting, “We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of Allah.” But they neither killed nor crucified him—it was only made to appear so. Even those who argue for this ˹crucifixion˺ are in doubt. They have no knowledge whatsoever—only making assumptions. They certainly did not kill him

**Boasting — We Killed the Messiah, Son of Mary, Messenger of God**

The verse continues *wa qawlihim innā qatalnā al-masīḥa ʿĪsā ibna Maryama rasūla Allāhi* — and for their saying, their boast, *indeed we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of God*. *Qawlihim* — their saying — was explained as continuation of *“and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary”* (4:156) — now the boast. *Innā qatalnā al-masīḥa* — we killed the Messiah — *masīḥ* — anointed, Messiah — was read as Jesus, *ʿĪsā ibnu Maryam*, whose mother was slandered as *buhtān ʿaẓīm* (4:156) and whose son they claim to have killed. *Rasūla Allāhi* — the messenger of God — was explained as their own designation with irony: they say *messenger of God* mockingly while claiming to have killed him, as they said *our hearts are ghulf* (4:155) mockingly while hearts were sealed for disbelief. The sūrah has shown that killing prophets without right is part of condemnation (4:155) — to boast of killing the Messiah is the apex: to claim murder of a messenger sent without distinguishing (4:152) and of the Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171). Early reports noted this boast was by Jews who did not kill Jesus but claimed credit, while the try was by Roman authority at their instigation; the Qur’anic *we killed* attributes the pride to them as the planners, as plotting is attributed though God is with them (4:108).

The addition *wa inna alladhīna ikhtalafū fīhi la fī shakkin minhu mā lahum bihī min ʿilmin illā ittibāʿa al-ẓann* — and surely those who disputed, differed, about him — about him, crucifixion — are surely in doubt about him, in *shakk* — doubt, suspicion — not having any knowledge about it except following assumption, conjecture — was explained with *ikhtalafū* — to differ — the same difference the community was warned not to make between God and messengers (4:150) and not to fall into other than believers’ path (4:115). *La fī shakkin minhu* — in doubt about him — was read as that those who argue for *we killed* are not agreed: some say killed, some say crucified, some say neither, all in *shakk*, as the sūrah elsewhere says those given a portion distort words (4:46). *Mā lahum bihī min ʿilmin illā ittibāʿa al-ẓann* — they have no knowledge whatsoever except following *ẓann* — assumption — was explained as that their claim lacks *ʿilm* — knowledge — the sūrah has contrasted *ẓann* with *ḥaqq* — *promise ever true* (4:122) versus delusion (4:120) — *ẓann* is Satan’s currency. Where God bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge (4:166) and angels bear witness, the crucifixion claim is *ittibāʿ al-ẓann* — following conjecture — not witness.

**They Certainly Did Not Kill Him**

The seal *wa mā qatalūhu yaqīnan* — and they certainly did not kill him, not in certainty — was explained with *yaqīn* — certain, firm, sure — negated as *they killed him not with certainty* — they have no certain killing, and *they certainly did not kill him* — emphatic. The adverb *yaqīnan* was read as again negating the boast *qatalnā* — we killed — with certainty’s opposite: not only did they not kill, they have no certainty that they did. The sūrah has shown that *“He wills to make clear”* (4:26), *“taught you what you did not know”* (4:113), *“most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation”* (4:114) — boasting murder is not clear but doubtful. The decisive word is that they did not kill him in truth, as the next verse says *rather God raised him to Himself, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:158). For the weak this is an anchor: where loud negative speech is allowed to the wronged (4:148) and pardoning is higher (4:149), loud boasting *we killed the messenger* is the loudest *sūʾ* not allowed where no wrong was done to the boaster.
verses.158:
> Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise

**Rather God Raised Him to Himself**

The verse states *bal rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayhi* — rather, nay, but God raised him, lifted him, up to Him, to Himself. *Bal* — rather — was explained as correction to *they killed him not nor crucified, it was made to appear* (4:157), where boasting *we killed the Messiah, son of Mary, messenger of God* was negated; *rather* His raising is the truth. *Rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayhi* — God raised him to Him — was explained as God lifting Jesus alive to Himself, as He raised the Mount over them for covenant (4:154) — raising Mount as warning, raising Jesus as honour — the sūrah’s two raisings: one over breakers to frighten, one of the messenger to preserve. *Ilayhi* — to Him, to Himself — was read as to His presence, to the heavens, as the sūrah elsewhere says *“He raised him to Himself”* and the sūrah says *O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Me”* (3:55). Early reports noted that Jesus was raised while his likeness was cast on another; the *shubbiha lahum* — made to appear — is explained by *rafaʿahu* — raised. Scripture has shown that God suffices as Trustee (4:132) and bears witness with His knowledge (4:166); raising the messenger is His trusteeship executed, as He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet here removes the messenger from killers and brings him to Himself, preserving the line of revelation. The phrase was linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — raising is the Gardens’ prototype: honour of nearness.

**And God Is Almighty, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAzīzan Ḥakīmā* — And God is Almighty, All-Powerful, All-Wise, was ever — was explained with *ʿAzīz* — Almighty, Mighty, invincible — the One who can raise against killers, as He is *Qadīr* — Most Capable to remove humanity (4:133) and *Qadīr* to pardon though capable to punish (4:149) — here *ʿAzīz* is capability to protect messenger where boasters claim killing. *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — was read as wisdom that made likeness to appear to boasters while raising, that let disputants remain in doubt following assumption (4:157). That will make his future testimony decisive. *ʿAzīz Ḥakīm* was also the seal for messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity have no excuse after messengers (4:165), showing that raising Jesus preserves the messenger lineage until the final messenger — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him”* (4:163) — all sent by the Almighty, All-Wise. Where the sūrah says *all honour belongs to Him completely* (4:139) sought by taking disbelievers as allies, Jesus raised to Him is the honour given to the messenger whose *ʿizzah* boasters thought they ended.

**A Verse That Follows Not Killed With Raised**

Placed after thunderbolt, calf, pardon, Mount, gate, Sabbath, firm covenant, then breaking, rejecting, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf*, denying, slandering Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed nor crucified, it was made to appear, disputants in doubt, no knowledge but assumption, certainly not killed (4:153–157), this verse follows *not killed* with *raised*. The sūrah has shown that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* (4:126, 4:131) — raising to Him is raising within His ownership; His heavens are the *maḥīṭ* — encompassing (4:126) — that can receive. The sūrah has shown that *“He does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) — to raise the messenger whom they wrongly boasted killing is not wronging the atom but preserving it. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) sees boasting murder as the worst secret talk made loud boast; raising is its rebuttal as public honour.
verses.159:
> Every one of the People of the Book will definitely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Judgment Jesus will be a witness against them

The verse states *wa in min ahli al-kitābi illā la yuʾminanna bihī qabla mawtihī* — and there is none among the People of the Book except he will surely believe in him before his death, before their death, before his. *In min ahli al-kitābi illā* — there is none among People of the Book except — was explained as universal quantifier: every one of the Jews and Christians given Scripture before you (4:131) will believe. *La yuʾminanna bihī* — will surely believe in him — was read with emphasis: the same *la* + *nūn* as Satan’s vow, now as God’s oath. Belief will be in Jesus — *ʿĪsā ibnu Maryam* — the Messiah whom they boasted killing but did not, whom God raised to Himself (4:157–158), the Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171). *Qabla mawtihī* — before his death — was read two ways: before the death of the Person of the Book — each will believe when death nears and truth becomes clear, as *“repentance not accepted when death is starting and he cries now I repent”* (4:18) — too late. And before the death of Jesus himself upon his return before the Hour, when he will descend and break cross, as reports state (Bukhārī 3448; Muslim 155). The sūrah has shown that those who distinguish between God and messengers saying we believe in some and disbelieve in some desire a way between (4:150) — they are true disbelievers (4:151). This belief before death is the undoing of that distinguishing, as the People of the Book finally accept Jesus as messenger not god.

**And on the Day He Will Be a Witness Against Them**

The second clause *wa yawma al-qiyāmati yakūnu ʿalayhim shahīdā* — and on the Day of Standing, of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them, upon them — was explained with *shahīd* — witness — the same witness as *“We will bring a witness from every community and bring you as witness against yours”* (4:41) where the Prophet ﷺ is witness against his community. *“God bears witness and angels bear witness”* (4:166) — here Jesus will be witness against those who made distinction. *ʿAlayhim* — against them, upon them — was read as that Jesus will testify: they said we killed the Messiah, we slandered Mary with mighty *buhtān* (4:156), they said our hearts are *ghulf* (4:155) — he will witness that they knew and denied, as the soul-takers will ask *what were you doing?* (4:97). *Yawma al-qiyāmati* was explained as the Day about which there is no doubt where He will gather you (4:87) and gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140); witness on that Day decides gathering. Classical notes added that his being *shahīd* against them fits his raising: he who was raised above boasting murder now descends as witness that murder did not occur, and the *shubbiha lahum* — made to appear — will be clarified by the one raised.

**Before His Death — Two Times for Witness**

The phrase *qabla mawtihī* was explained to keep two times for witness: before the death of each of the People of the Book — at the threshold where angels take souls and ask *what were you doing?* (4:97) — truth becomes clear but too late as repentance at death is not accepted (4:18). And before the death of Jesus upon his return — a communal time where the People of the Book will believe while still alive before the Hour, as *“there are messengers We told you and others We did not”* (4:164) shows knowledge is with Him. To say *every one will believe in him before his death* was therefore read not as claim that all die as believers — because humiliating punishment was prepared for true disbelievers (4:151) — but as that at death’s veiling removed, each will see, yet seeing after sight is too late for those who increased in disbelief (4:137).

The next verses will turn from history to law: forbidden foods to Jews for wrongdoing and hindering, taking interest despite prohibition, consuming wealth unjustly — painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but those well-grounded in knowledge who believe in what was revealed to you and before — to them great reward (4:160–162).
verses.160:
> We forbade the Jews certain foods that had been lawful to them for their wrongdoing, and for hindering many from the Way of Allah

**We Forbade the Jews Certain Foods For Their Wrongdoing**

The verse states *fa bi ẓulmin mina alladhīna hādū ḥarramnā ʿalayhim ṭayyibātin uḥillat lahum* — so for wrongdoing, injustice, from those who became Jews, became *hādū*, We forbade them good things, pure foods, that had been lawful for them. *Bi ẓulmin mina alladhīna hādū* — for wrong, injustice, from those who are Jews — was explained as the same *ẓulm* that struck them with thunderbolt for demand greater than a book (4:153) — *because of their wrongdoing* the Mount was raised (4:154), covenant broken, signs rejected, prophets killed without right, hearts claimed *ghulf* sealed (4:155), Mary slandered with mighty *buhtān* (4:156), boasted killing Messiah not killed (4:157). *Ḥarramnā ʿalayhim ṭayyibātin uḥillat lahum* — We forbade them good things that had been permitted — was explained as foods once *ḥalāl* made *ḥarām* as discipline, as Levitical prohibitions of certain fats and meats that remain in Jewish law — the sūrah elsewhere says *“every food was lawful to Children of Israel except what Israel forbade himself before Torah”* (3:93) — here additional forbidding is for *ẓulm*. *Ṭayyibāt* — good, pure, wholesome — was read as the good that was forbidding is not evil in itself — the foods are *ṭayyib* — pure — but forbidden as recompense, as the sūrah says *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) — here reward is forbidding of *ṭayyibāt*. The sūrah has shown that *“We forbade certain foods for wrongdoing”* is counterpart to *“We forgave them after calf yet gave Moses clear proof”* (4:153): forgiveness for calf did not cancel consequence for ongoing wrong.

**And For Hindering Many From the Way of God**

The addition *wa bi ṣaddihim ʿan sabīli Allāhi kathīran* — and for their hindering, blocking, turning away many from the way, the path of God — was explained with *ṣadd* — to hinder, to bar, to turn away — the same *ṣadd* that hypocrites *turn away stubbornly* — *yaṣuddūna ṣudūdā* (4:61) — when told come to revelations and Messenger. That the sūrah’s noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26) are blocked where hindering occurs. *ʿAn sabīli Allāhi* — from God’s way, path — was read as the believers’ path (4:115) that was not to be left, the way of Abraham pure (4:125), the straight path He guides to through mercy and grace (4:175). *Kathīran* — many, much — was explained as many hindered: they hinder others by rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming hearts are *ghulf*, demanding visible God, taking calf. By legal forbidding that remains; the sūrah later says *“those who disbelieve and hinder from God’s way have certainly gone far astray”* (4:167) — far straying is hindering’s fruit. Early reports linked hindering to rabbis who concealed description of the Prophet ﷺ in Torah to keep followers, and to usury that consumes wealth unjustly (4:161) — hindering by economic oppression as well as doctrinal concealment. The sūrah has shown that *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah…”* (4:163) — all accepted without distinction (4:152) — hindering is the opposite: to block that acceptance.

**A Verse That Follows Boast Corrected With Law For Hindering**

Placed after the history of the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven, demanded visible God, were struck, took calf yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant taken, then breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slandering Mary with mighty *buhtān*, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death and witness on the Day (4:153–159), this verse follows boast corrected with law for hindering: for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way, We forbade them *ṭayyibāt* that had been lawful. The sūrah has shown that association is far straying (4:116) and defying the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose (4:115). Hindering many from God’s way is that far straying made social — not only straying self but blocking others, as Satan orders cutting and altering (4:119) to alter creation he blocks God’s creation. The forbidding of *ṭayyibāt* was read as the sūrah’s measure: as the emigrant finds many havens and abundance (4:100) — *saʿah* — the hinderer finds *ṭayyibāt* removed — narrowing where he narrowed others’ way. Where *“He wills to lighten burdens because humanity is weak”* (4:28) — lightening is giving *ṭayyibāt* — hindering many removes lightness.

Classical notes added that this forbidding is distinct from Israel’s self-forbidding before Torah (3:93) and that the final Book makes lawful *ṭayyibāt* again except what was forbidden as discipline, showing that the Qur’an’s *ḥalāl* restores where the Tawrāh’s discipline had narrowed, as the Prophet ﷺ was sent to remove burdens — *“he releases them from heavy burdens and yokes”* (7:157).
verses.161:
> taking interest despite its prohibition, and consuming people’s wealth unjustly. We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment

**Taking Interest Despite Prohibition and Consuming Wealth Unjustly**

The verse continues *wa akhdhihimu al-ribā wa qad nuhū ʿanhu wa aklihim amwāla al-nāsi bi al-bāṭil* — and their taking interest — *ribā* — though they were forbidden it, though prohibition had come. Their consuming people’s wealth wrongly, unjustly, by false means — *bi al-bāṭil*. *Akhdhihimu al-ribā* — their taking ribā — was explained as Jewry taking interest despite Torah forbidding — *“you shall not lend at interest to your brother”* — as earlier warnings against devouring wealth by false means (2:188), against consuming orphans’ wealth as fire (4:10). Against devouring wealth unjustly and killing yourselves though He is Merciful (4:29) make clear. *Wa qad nuhū ʿanhu* — though they were forbidden — was read as that *ribā* is not ignorance but disobedience after *sulṭān mubīn* — compelling proof — Moses was given (4:153) and Mount raised for firm covenant (4:154): where interest is forbidden yet taken, the Mount’s covenant is broken again. *Wa aklihim amwāla al-nāsi bi al-bāṭil* — and eating people’s wealth unjustly — was explained as consuming wealth by false claim, bribery, selling religion, concealing description of Prophet ﷺ for fee — a trade where those given a portion trade it for misguidance wishing you deviate (4:44) and hindering many from God’s way (4:160) includes economic harm. The two — *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* — were read as the sūrah’s pairing after forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for wrongdoing and hindering many (4:160): as those given a portion trade guidance, here they trade wealth by *ribā* and false consumption.

**We Have Prepared for Disbelievers Among Them a Painful Punishment**
