The seal *wa aʿtadnā li al-kāfirīna minhum ʿadhāban alīmā* — and We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful, aching punishment — was explained with *aʿtadnā* — prepared, made ready — as the same preparation for true disbelievers who distinguish between God and messengers — humiliating punishment prepared (4:151) — and for those who consume orphans’ wealth — Fire. For intentional killer — Hell, anger, curse (4:93). *Li al-kāfirīna minhum* — for the disbelievers among them, from among them — was explained as not all among them: as the sūrah will say *but those well-grounded in knowledge among them who believe in what was revealed to you and before* — to them great reward (4:162) — punishment is for *kāfirīn minhum* — disbelievers among them — not for every Jew, as *we forgave them after calf* (4:153) showed some forgiven. *ʿAdhāban alīmā* — painful punishment — was read as pain matching the pain of consuming fire (4:10), of humiliating punishment for ally seekers (4:102), of lowest depth without helper (4:145). Scripture has shown that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides Him”* (4:123) — *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* are evil rewarded accordingly — painful. Where the Book says *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) — interest even at atom of increase is measured and not wronging to punish, because it wrongs the single soul’s trust.

**A Verse That Follows Forbidding *Ṭayyibāt* With Forbidding Wealth**

Placed after *We forbade Jews certain good foods that had been lawful for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way* (4:160), this verse follows forbidding *ṭayyibāt* — pure foods — with forbidding wealth — *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* — for which painful punishment is prepared. That to God belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) shows that wealth taken by *ribā* is taken from His ownership unjustly, as female gods invoked besides Him (4:117) are taken from His worship unjustly. The law lightens because humanity is weak (4:28) yet does not license devouring wealth unjustly (4:29) — *ribā* is the lightening inverted: to make wealth increase by hardship on debtor. Earlier the Book praised charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) as the good secret talk; interest is the evil secret talk that devours. For the weak this is protective: where interest is taken from the debtor and wealth consumed unjustly from people, the sūrah that promised many havens to the emigrant (4:100) and enrichment to both after separation (4:130) declares that to take interest though forbidden will be painful punishment for disbelievers among them. Help is with the well-grounded who give alms (4:162).
verses.162:
> But those of them well-grounded in knowledge, the faithful ˹who˺ believe in what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ and what was revealed before you—˹especially˺ those who establish prayer—and those who pay alms-tax and believe in Allah and the Last Day, to these ˹people˺ We will grant a great reward

**But Those Well-Grounded in Knowledge Among Them**

The verse states *lākini al-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilmi minhum* — but those firmly grounded, deeply rooted, in knowledge, among them — among the People of the Book — whose litany was demand, thunderbolt, calf, breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, slander, boasting murder, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm*, taking *ribā* though prohibited, consuming wealth unjustly — among them the *rāsikhūn*. *Rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm* — firmly grounded in knowledge — was explained as those rooted deep so that wind does not move them, as the sūrah has shown that those who distinguish between God and messengers desire a way between (4:150) are not grounded. These are, as Abraham was *ḥanīf* following the upright (4:125) and as the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105). *Minhum* — among them — was read as not all among them: as the painful punishment was prepared for *kāfirīn minhum* — disbelievers among them (4:161) — great reward is for *rāsikhūn minhum* — grounded among them — keeping the sūrah’s balance: few believe except few (4:155) — here the few are named.

**Especially Those Who Establish Prayer and Pay Alms**

The detail *wa al-muqīmīna al-ṣalāta wa al-muʾtūna al-zakāta* — and especially those who establish, stand firm for, prayer — *muqīmīn* — and those who give, pay, alms — *zakāh* — was explained with two pillars: *iqāmat al-ṣalāh* — establishing prayer — the same *kitāban mawqūtā* — writ at fixed time (4:103) — shortened on travel (4:101), guarded under arms (4:102), remembered standing, sitting, lying (4:103), lazy to be seen by hypocrites (4:142) — the *rāsikhūn* establish it. *Wa al-muʾtūna al-zakāta* — and those who pay alms — was read as the opposite of *akhdh al-ribā* — taking interest though forbidden — and *akl bi al-bāṭil* — consuming wealth unjustly (4:161): to give *zakāh* is to release wealth, to take *ribā* is to increase it wrongly. Early reports noted the grammar — *al-muqīmīna* in accusative as praise, as Arabs single out the praised with accusative — showing special praise for those who establish prayer among the grounded. The sūrah has said *“charge your wealth by mutual consent, do not kill yourselves, He is ever Merciful”* (4:29) — *zakāh* is mutual consent’s alms. The pair was also linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122): establishing prayer and giving alms are the *ṣāliḥāt* — righteous deeds.

The seal *wa al-muʾminīna bi Allāhi wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri ulāʾika sa nuʾtīhim ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and those who believe in God and the Last Day — to these We will surely, will soon, grant a great, mighty reward — was explained with *yuʾminūna bi Allāhi wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri* as the two articles that anchor all — God and Last Day — without which Articles — denying God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day leads far astray (4:136) — belief incomplete; the *rāsikhūn* affirm them. *Ulāʾika sa nuʾtīhim ajran ʿaẓīmā* — to these We will grant great reward — was explained as the same *ajr ʿaẓīm* promised to those who command charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) and to the repentant sincere with believers (4:146) and to comprehensive believers (4:152) — the *rāsikhūn* who establish prayer and give alms are inclusive. The sūrah has shown that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — great reward is both — world as *murāgham* and *saʿah* and Hereafter as Gardens true. *Sa nuʾtīhim* — We will grant — was read as divine assurance that reward secured upon God as emigrant’s reward secured (4:100) — the same certainty.
verses.163:
> Indeed, We have sent revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ as We sent revelation to Noah and the prophets after him. We also sent revelation to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants, ˹as well as˺ Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon. And to David We gave the Psalms

The verse opens *innā awḥaynā ilayka kamā awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin wa al-nabiyyīna min baʿdih* — indeed We have inspired, revealed, to you as We inspired to Noah and the prophets after him. *Awḥaynā* — to inspire, to reveal, to convey — was explained as divine communication to heart, as the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and as *“O Prophet, have faith in God, Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before”* (4:136) — revelation is one chain. *Kamā awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin* — as We revealed to Noah — was read as that Nūḥ is first of the chain of law-giving messengers after Adam, as the sūrah earlier says *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* (4:126) — Noah’s ark upon water that belongs to Him is the first rescue of the single soul spread (4:1). *Wa al-nabiyyīna min baʿdih* — and prophets after him — was explained as that the revelation to you is not isolate but continuation, as Abraham pure — *ḥanīf* — was taken as friend (4:125) and his way is best faith. The verse generalises the sūrah’s lineage: from Noah through Abraham to you is one *waḥy* — revelation — whose truth was made clear where Mount was raised (4:154) and whose distinction not made is true belief (4:152).

The enumeration *wa awḥaynā ilā Ibrāhīma wa Ismāʿīla wa Isḥāqa wa Yaʿqūba wa al-asbāṭi wa ʿĪsā wa Ayyūba wa Yūnusa wa Hārūna wa Sulaymāna wa ātaynā Dāwūda zabūrā* — and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes — the *asbāṭ* — descendants — and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon. And to David We gave the Psalms — *Zabūr* — was explained as proof of universality. *Ibrāhīma … al-asbāṭ* — Abraham’s line — Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, tribes — was read as the *millata Ibrāhīma* — Way of Abraham upright (4:125) — made concrete: revelation to each branch, not only to the asking People of the Book who demanded a book from heaven (4:153) — the book has already come to many. *ʿĪsā* — Jesus — was read as the Messiah raised to Him (4:158), son of Mary slandered then son slain falsely — now placed among prophets revealed to, not god. *Ayyūba, Yūnusa* — Job, Jonah — were read as the tested: Job with patience, Jonah with repentance after abandonment — both *“We sent revelation”* to them as to you, showing that revelation includes trials. *Hārūna, Sulaymāna* — Aaron, Solomon — were read as brother-helper and king-prophet; Aaron with Moses where the Mount was raised, Solomon with kingdom where *“give them speck on date stone”* (4:53) — even kingdom with prophethood. *Wa ātaynā Dāwūda zabūrā* — and to David We gave Psalms — was explained as book singled: Psalms as *zabūr* — written, inscribed — among books before (4:136), showing that books before are many, not one book from heaven demanded. Where the sūrah says *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah”* — *kamā* — likeness is in source — all from Owner of heavens and earth (4:126) — and in purpose — to judge with truth.

Placed after the history — demand for a book from heaven, greater demand visible God, thunderbolt, calf yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, taking interest though forbidden, consuming unjustly, painful punishment for disbelievers among them. Grounded in knowledge among them believe in what was revealed to you and before, especially establishing prayer and alms, to them great reward (4:153–162), this verse follows demand with lineage: *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him*.
verses.164:
> There are messengers whose stories We have told you already and others We have not. And to Moses Allah spoke directly

**Messengers Whose Stories We Told You and Others We Did Not**

The verse states *wa rusulan qad qaṣaṣnāhum ʿalayka min qablu wa rusulan lam naqṣuṣhum ʿalayka* — and messengers, apostles, whose stories We have already narrated, cut, to you before. Messengers We did not narrate to you. *Rusulan* — messengers — was explained as the continuation of *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him… Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David We gave Psalms”* (4:163) — now as *recounted and not recounted*. *Qad qaṣaṣnāhum ʿalayka min qablu* — whose stories We have told you before — was read as those named in Qur’an — the chain from Adam to Jesus — told as proof that God bears witness with His knowledge (4:166). *Wa rusulan lam naqṣuṣhum ʿalayka* — and messengers We did not narrate — was explained as that knowledge is with Him who is Fully Aware encompassing everything (4:126) — He sent many more than told, because to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) — among all peoples He sent. The sūrah has shown that those well-grounded in knowledge believe in what was revealed to you and before (4:162) — even those messengers not recounted are among *mā unzila min qablika* — what was revealed before you (4:162) — and to believe accepting all, rejecting none (4:152) includes those not narrated, for their existence is asserted here. To know that some were not told was explained as humility: the Book does not claim to list all His sent, because to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) — among all, He sent, and He knows. The command to be mindful (4:131) therefore rests not on counting messengers but on trusting the Sender who sent many whose names only He encompasses as *Muḥīṭ* (4:126).

**And to Moses God Spoke Directly**

The addition *wa kallama Allāhu Mūsā taklīman* — and God spoke to Moses — *kallama* — speaking — *taklīman* — directly, with speech — was explained with *taklīm* — speaking mouth to ear without intermediary, the honour that Moses is *Kalīmullāh* — Speaker with God. *Taklīman* — emphatic verbal noun — was read as absolute direct speech, not inspiration as to Noah (4:163) — *awḥaynā* — but *kallama*. Early reports linked this to Sinai where Mount was raised over them for covenant (4:154) and where thunderbolt struck them for demand greater than a book — *show God visible* (4:153) — yet to Moses He spoke directly without seeing. The sūrah has shown that *“there is no knowledge except following assumption”* where boasters claim killing Messiah (4:157) — true knowledge is where He speaks, as He spoke to Moses. The verse was also linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — Moses’ direct speech is the witness that revelation is real, against the People of the Book demand *bring down a book from heaven* (4:153) — revelation already spoken.

**A Verse That Follows Revelation Lineage With Limit of Narration**

Placed after *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him… Psalms to David* (4:163), this verse follows lineage with limit of narration: some narrated, some not narrated, and Moses spoken to directly. The sūrah has shown that *“We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful”* (4:131) — revelation before you is many; to not narrate some is not to deny them, as the sūrah says *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) — He knows those sent. The sūrah that warns not to make distinction between messengers (4:150–152) says even those not narrated are included in not distinguishing: to accept all messengers includes the unnamed. The sūrah that warns not to take disbelievers as allies instead of believers (4:144) and describes lowest depth without helper (4:145) makes direct speech to Moses the helper for the weak: where you were told to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), here is the Speaker who can be referred to.
verses.165:
> ˹All were˺ messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity should have no excuse before Allah after ˹the coming of˺ the messengers. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise

**Messengers Delivering Good News and Warnings**

The verse states *rusulan mubashshirīna wa mundhirīna* — messengers, apostles, as bearers of good news and warners, givers of glad tidings and warnings. *Mubashshirīn* — bearing good news — and *mundhirīn* — warning — were explained as the two faces of revelation already named: Gardens forever for those who believe and do good where promise is true (4:122) — good news — and Hell without escape for followers of Satan’s delusion (4:121), painful punishment for hypocrites (4:138), humiliating punishment for true disbelievers (4:151), painful punishment for disbelievers among the Book’s People for *ẓulm* and *ribā* (4:161) — warnings. *Rusulan* — messengers — includes those whose stories We told you before and those We did not narrate. To Moses He spoke directly (4:164), and those given Psalms to David (4:163), and the chain from Noah through Abraham to Jesus (4:163) — all were *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn*. The sūrah has shown that those who believe accepting all, rejecting none, will be given rewards (4:152), and that those well-grounded believe in what was revealed to you and before (4:162) — good news is for them. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector”* (4:123) — warning is for him.

**So Humanity Should Have No Excuse Before God After Messengers**

The purpose *li allā yakūna li al-nāsi ʿalā Allāhi ḥujjatun baʿda al-rusuli* — so that there be not for humanity against God an argument, excuse, plea, after the messengers — was explained with *ḥujjah* — argument, proof, excuse — the same *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant — given against hostile turners (4:91) and that you give against yourselves if you take disbelievers as allies (4:144) and compelling proof Moses was given (4:153) — here humanity’s *ḥujjah* against Him is removed. *Baʿda al-rusuli* — after the messengers — was read as after the lineage from Noah to you — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah”* (4:163) — there is no *“we did not know”* left, because He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet He sent messengers first. Early reports linked this to the sūrah’s *“He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26) — clarity is via messengers, so excuse is cut. The phrase was linked to *“on Resurrection Day the Messiah will be witness against them”* (4:159) — witnesses are *rusul* against their peoples, as *“We will bring witness from every community and you as witness against yours”* (4:41) — the witness is the *ḥujjah*. Where the hypocrites sought to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142) and argued *we believe in some and disbelieve in some desiring a way between* (4:150) — they claimed a *ḥujjah* of compromise; the verse says none remains.

**A Verse That Follows Lineage With Purpose**

Placed after *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Psalms to David* (4:163), *messengers whose stories We told you and others We did not. To Moses He spoke directly* (4:164), this verse follows lineage with purpose: all were messengers delivering good news and warnings so that humanity have no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise. The sūrah that asks *“was not God’s earth spacious enough to emigrate?”* (4:97) and promises many havens (4:100) says messengers are the spaciousness of excuse removed, as earth is the spaciousness of refuge opened. For the weak this is clarifying: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement is best (4:128), good news is that settlement pleasing to Him is great reward (4:114), warning is that inclining completely leaving hanging is Hamm; both were told before excuse remains.
verses.166:
> Yet ˹if you are denied, O Prophet,˺ Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you—He has sent it with His knowledge. The angels too bear witness. And Allah ˹alone˺ is sufficient as a Witness

**If You Are Denied, God Bears Witness to What He Sent Down**

The verse opens *lākini Allāhu yashhadu bi mā anzala ilayka* — yet, but, rather, God bears witness, testifies, to what He has sent down, revealed, to you. *Lākini* — yet. — was explained as reply to *“humanity should have no excuse after messengers”* (4:165) where Almighty, All-Wise sends good news and warnings; if after that they deny you — *yet if you are denied, O Prophet* — God bears witness. *Yashhadu bi mā anzala ilayka* — bears witness to what He sent down to you — was explained as that the sūrah’s lineage — *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Psalms to David* (4:163), messengers told and not told, Moses spoken to directly (4:164) — all sent as *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn* so no excuse (4:165) — is witnessed by Him who sent: *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126). *Anzala ilayka* — sent down to you — was read as the Qur’an sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and as the instruction about orphan women already recited (4:127) — all are *mā anzala ilayka*. The sūrah has warned *whoever disobeys, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* (4:131) — to deny the One who bears witness is to deny the Owner to whom all belongs.

**And God Alone Is Sufficient as Witness**

The seal *wa kafā bi Allāhi shahīdā* — and God alone is enough, enough, as Witness — was explained with *shahīd* — witness — the same *shahīd* as the Bringing of witness from every community (4:41) and Jesus as witness against them (4:159) — here the Supreme Witness suffices. *Kafā bi Allāhi shahīdā* was read as that where People of the Book demand a book from heaven as sign and hypocrites desire a way between distinguishing (4:150) and where night plotters hide from people but He is with them (4:108) — His witness suffices. The phrase was also the sūrah’s answer to *“with Him are both rewards, He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing”* (4:134): He who hears and sees suffices as Witness because witnessing is hearing and seeing. Where the sūrah says *“He is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132) and *“sufficient as Guardian and Helper”* (4:45) — to be enough as Witness is to be the Trust upon whom judgment by Book (4:105) rests.

**A Verse That Follows No Excuse With Sufficient Witness**

Placed after *messengers as good news and warnings so humanity have no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:165), this verse follows no excuse with enough witness: yet if you are denied, God bears witness to what He sent to you — He sent it with His knowledge — angels too bear witness — He alone suffices as Witness. The sūrah has traced *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant — Moses was given (4:153), given over hostile turners (4:91), that you give against yourselves if you take allies instead of believers (4:144); witness is the *sulṭān* that makes warrant true. The sūrah that asks *“who is more truthful than God in speech?”* (4:122) — none — says His *shahādah* — witness — is most truthful. For the weak this is an opening: where you were told to verify reports through Messenger and authority (4:83) and to be sure before fighting (4:94) and to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135), the witness that your verification stands is His witness and angels’ — enough. That you need not be hanging between neither these nor those (4:143) waiting to see.
verses.167:
> Those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah have certainly strayed far away

**Those Who Disbelieve and Hinder From God’s Way — Far Astray**

The verse states *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāhi qad ḍallū ḍalālan baʿīdā* — surely those who disbelieve and hinder, bar, turn others from God’s way, path, have certainly gone far, strayed far away. *Kafarū* — to disbelieve, to cover — was explained as denial after messengers as good news and warnings removed excuse (4:165) and after enough witness bears witness with His knowledge and angels (4:166). *Wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāhi* — and hinder from God’s way — was explained with *ṣadd* — to block, to hinder, to turn away — the same hindering as *We forbade Jews certain good foods for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way* (4:160) — there *bi ṣaddihim ʿan sabīli Allāhi kathīran* — hindering many — here *ṣaddū* — hindering — as act of those who disbelieve. *Sabīli Allāhi* — God’s way, path — was read as the noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26), the believers’ path not to be left (4:115), the straight path He guides to through mercy (4:175), the Book sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) — all are God’s way. *Qad ḍallū ḍalālan baʿīdā* — have certainly gone far astray, strayed far away — was explained as *ḍalāl baʿīd* — far straying — the same seal as *whoever associates has gone far astray* (4:116) and *whoever denies God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day has gone far astray* (4:136) — to disbelieve and hinder is that far. Early reports linked *ṣaddū* to Jews who concealed description of the Prophet ﷺ and to hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) and to those who deny revelation being ridiculed yet sit with mockers (4:140) — hindering is both doctrinal concealment and social sitting.

**A Verse That Follows No Excuse and Sufficient Witness With Far Straying**

Placed after *messengers as good news and warnings so humanity have no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:165), *yet if you are denied, God bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge, angels too bear witness, He alone suffices as Witness* (4:166), this verse follows no excuse and enough witness with far straying for those who disbelieve and hinder from God’s way. The sequence — lineage from Noah through Jesus to you (4:163), messengers told and not told, Moses spoken to directly (4:164), purpose so no excuse (4:165), enough witness (4:166) — now the verdict for deniers and hinderers: they have gone far. Scripture notes that *“neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book”* (4:123) — grace not by wish — and *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — to hinder from His way is to hinder from both rewards where both are with Him whose ownership is heavens and earth (4:126). Elsewhere the principle that *“whoever earns sin earns only upon himself”* (4:111) is qualified here: hindering adds others’ misguidance to earnings — therefore *baʿīd* — far.

**Disbelief Alone and Disbelief Plus Hindering**

The pairing — *kafarū* — disbelieved — and *ṣaddū* — hindered — was explained to show two degrees: disbelief alone is straying, disbelief plus hindering is far straying. The principle that *“whoever does evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) shows that disbelief alone will be *yujza bihī* — rewarded accordingly; hindering adds to it, as throwing sin on innocent adds slander to original sin (4:112). Forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* plus *ṣadd kathīr* — hindering many — (4:160) shows that *ṭayyibāt* removal corresponds to double cause; here *ḍalālan baʿīdā* is for *kufr* plus *ṣadd*. Where the Book says *“do not incline entirely leaving the other suspended”* (4:129) — hindering the suspended from right is the household *ṣadd* — and *“settlement best”* (4:128) — settlement is opposite of hindering. For the weak this is protective: where you are hindered — the helpless who cannot find way (4:98) — the hinderer’s far straying is declared, not yours.
verses.168:
> Those who disbelieve and wrong themselves—surely Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to any path

**Those Who Disbelieve and Wrong Themselves — Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

The verse states *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ẓalamū lam yakuni Allāhu li yaghfira lahum wa lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — surely those who disbelieve and wrong, do injustice, will not be — He will not — forgive them nor guide them to any path, way. *Kafarū* — disbelieved — and *ẓalamū* — wronged — was explained with *ẓulm* — wrongdoing, injustice — as addition to *kufr*: disbelief plus hindering from God’s way (4:167) is wronging selves and others, as *“whoever commits evil or wrongs themselves”* (4:110) and *“whoever earns sin earns only upon himself”* (4:111) — wronging here is *ẓulm* that exceeds self. *Lam yakuni Allāhu li yaghfira lahum* — He will not forgive them — was explained with *li yaghfira* — to forgive — withheld where *shukr* and *īmān* would remove need for punishment (4:147) — here disbelief and wrong persist. *Wa lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — nor guide them to any path, way, road — was read as no guidance to *ṭarīq* — way — the same *sabīl* believers follow (4:115) and God guides to noble ways (4:26). To be not guided to any *ṭarīq* is to be left where *“whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way”* (4:88, 4:143) — no way. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever believed then disbelieved then believed then increased”* (4:137) — He will neither forgive nor guide them to the Right Way — there increased disbelief after oscillation removed forgiveness and guidance; here disbelief plus wrong does. Early reports linked *ẓalamū* to those who disbelieve and also wrong the Prophet by concealing his description, taking interest though forbidden (4:161), consuming wealth unjustly, claiming *we killed Messiah* (4:157) — wrongs upon denial, each increasing the unforgiven burden.

**Not Forgiven Nor Guided to Any Path — The Two Denied**

The two denials — *lam yakun li yaghfira* and *lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — were explained as the Book’s two gifts denied: forgiveness that effaces — *ʿAfuww* — and guidance that shows way — *Hidāyah*. The promise that whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110) shows that forgiveness denied here is where seeking is absent; and that *“had it not been for grace they would have deceived you yet they deceive only themselves”* (4:113) shows guidance denied where deception persists. That *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) links forgiveness to Gardens and guidance to the straight path He guides to through mercy and grace (4:175); to deny both is to close both abodes. For the weak this is clarifying: where helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) were not among those who disbelieve and wrong but among those who cannot find way (*ḥīlah, sabīl*), forgiveness and guidance are hoped; here case is opposite — able, disbelieving, wronging, hindering.

The phrase *wa lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — nor guide them to any path — with indefinite *ṭarīqā* — any way — was explained as no path toward mercy remaining, because *ṣirāṭ mustaqīm* — straight path — He guides to through mercy (4:175) is the only *ṭarīq* to Gardens. To be not guided to any *ṭarīq* is to be not guided to that. The declaration that *“He can remove you O humanity and bring others”* (4:133) frames removal as where no *ṭarīq* remains. And *“whoever defies the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose then burned”* (4:115) shows that leaving to chosen path is not guiding to true path.

Though only *“those who disbelieve and wrong — He will neither forgive nor guide them to any path,”* the verse holds the gate open one sentence: except Hell’s way — as the sūrah’s pattern holds — lowest depth without helper except those who repent (4:145–146) — the gate is repentance not asserted here because disbelief and wrong persist.
verses.169:
> except that of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever. And that is easy for Allah

**Except That of Hell — To Stay There Forever**

The verse completes *illā ṭarīqa Jahannam khālidīna fīhā abadan* — except the way, the path of Hell, staying, abiding, in it forever and ever. *Illā ṭarīqa Jahannam* — except the path of Hell — was explained as the only *ṭarīq* — way — to which those who disbelieve and wrong — not forgiven, not guided to any path (4:168) — will be guided: Hell’s way. *Ṭarīq* — path, way — was read as *sabīl* — the sūrah’s path language — noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26), believers’ path not to be left (4:115), associations far straying (4:116), disbelief plus hindering far astray (4:167) — now the *ṭarīq* guided to is Hell’s, as *“whoever defies the Messenger and follows other than believers’ path We will let pursue what he chose then burn, evil destination”* (4:115) — burning is that path. *Khālidīna fīhā abadan* — staying in it forever and ever — was explained with double emphasis — *khālidīn* and *abadan* — the same double for Gardens for those who believe and do good (4:122) — now for Hell’s path where *“they will have Hell as home and find no escape”* (4:121) — no *maḥīṣ*. The sūrah has shown that *“they are true disbelievers, humiliating punishment prepared for disbelievers”* (4:151) — humiliating is Hell’s path; and *“lowest depth of Fire, you will never find helper”* (4:145) — lowest depth is that path’s place. *Abadan* — forever ever — was linked to the sūrah’s promise where Gardens forever (4:122) is for belief and good, here forever for disbelief and wrong — the only *ṭarīq* left is lasting.

**A Verse That Completes Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

Placed after *those who disbelieve and wrong — He will neither forgive nor guide them to any path* (4:168), this verse completes neither forgiven nor guided with except Hell’s path forever, and that is easy for Him. The litany from demand for a book from heaven (4:153) through thunderbolt, calf, pardon, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, taking interest though forbidden, consuming unjustly, painful punishment for disbelievers among them. Grounded among them to great reward, then lineage, messengers told and not, directly spoken, good news and warnings so no excuse, enough witness, those who disbelieve and hinder far astray, disbelieve and wrong not forgiven nor guided — now except Hell’s path forever easy — shows that excuse removed and witness enough leaves Hell’s path as the only remaining for persisters. For the weak this is an anchor: where helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) were not among those who disbelieve and wrong but among those who cannot find *ḥīla* or *sabīl* — Hell’s path is not for helpless but for hinderers and wrongers — the easy for Him is not arbitrary but measure.

The word *illā* — except — was explained to keep Hell’s path as the only *ṭarīq* left where any other *ṭarīq* would be mercy and guidance. To be guided to Hell’s path is not guidance as *hidāyah* to mercy but as *tawlīyah* — letting pursue what he chose (4:115) — the sūrah’s leaving to stray (4:88, 4:143). The sūrah has shown that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — Hell’s path forever is the other reward’s opposite; Gardens true (4:122) is the *hidāyah* path, Hell forever (4:169) is the allowed stray path. The verse generalises the sūrah’s *yasīr* — easy — where *“burn in Fire, that is easy for God”* (4:30) — devouring wealth is cousin to consuming people’s wealth unjustly and taking *ribā* (4:161) — all are *yasīr* to punish as all are *muḥīṭ* to know. The next passage will turn from history’s litigants to humanity: O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth from your Lord. Believe for your own good, if you disbelieve then to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:170) — belief’s call where Hell’s path easy is alternative.

The next verses will address humanity and People of the Book directly: the Messenger has come with truth (4:170), do not go to extremes about faith (4:171), Messiah not too proud to be servant nor angels nearest (4:172) — all are the alternative path — belief and good, mercy and grace, straight path (4:174–175) — versus Hell’s easy.
verses.170:
> O humanity! The Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good. But if you disbelieve, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise

**O Humanity — The Messenger Has Come With Truth From Your Lord**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu qad jāʾakumu al-rasūlu bi al-ḥaqqi min rabbikum* — O humanity, the Messenger — *al-rasūl* — the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ — has certainly come to you with the truth, the true, from your Lord. *Yā ayyuhā al-nāsu* — O humanity — was explained as second great humanity address after *“O humanity, be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) and *“O humanity, He can remove you and bring others if He wills, He is Most Capable”* (4:133) — now *“O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth.”* *Qad jāʾakumu al-rasūlu* — has certainly come to you the Messenger — was read as fulfilment of the chain — *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Psalms to David* (4:163), messengers told and not, Moses spoken to directly (4:164), messengers as good news and warnings so no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise (4:165), enough witness to what He sent with His knowledge and angels witness (4:166) — the Messenger is the told messenger. *Bi al-ḥaqqi* — with truth, as truth — was explained as that He came with true content and true descent, as the Book was sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and as God’s promise is true, whose word more truthful? (4:122). *Min rabbikum* — from your Lord — was read as from the Owner to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) who is Lord who created from single soul (4:1) — truth from Him.

**So Believe For Your Own Good**

The call *fa āminū khayran lakum* — so believe, have faith, it is better for you, good for you, as good — was explained with *khayran lakum* — better for you, good for you — not for Him. The addressee, as He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) though you disobey — to Him still belongs all. *Āminū* — have faith, believe — was read as comprehensive faith — *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before* (4:136) — steadfast, not wavering, not distinguishing between God and messengers desiring a way between (4:150) — to be among those who accept all, rejecting none, to be given rewards (4:152). *Khayran lakum* was linked to *“Gardens forever, promise ever true”* (4:122) — belief’s *khayr* is Gardens and great reward promised to the grounded (4:162) and to those who hold fast to Him guided through straight path (4:175). To believe is to get the havens promised to the emigrant (4:100) and enrichment after separation (4:130) — *khayran lakum* is both world and Hereafter. Early reports added that the *fa* — so — makes belief the response after the Messenger has come with truth and after excuse removed (4:165) and witness enough (4:166) — belief is not speculation but response.

The warning *wa in takfurū fa inna li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — but if you disbelieve, cover, then indeed to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — was explained as that disbelief does not harm the Owner: as *We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful, if you disbelieve to Him still belongs all, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* (4:131) — here *if you disbelieve* after the Messenger has come with truth, the same ownership remains. *Li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth — was read as that disbelief after the Messenger’s truth is like the earlier demand greater than a book — *show God visible* — answered with thunderbolt and Mount raised (4:153–154) — to demand while ownership is His is disbelief against Owner. He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — punishment is not His need; ownership after disbelief says the same — disbelief impoverishes the disbeliever, not the Owner. The clause was also linked to *“except that of Hell to stay forever, and that is easy for Him”* (4:169) — easy where ownership is all — Hell’s path easy is within that belonging.

**And God Is All-Knowing, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAlīman Ḥakīmā* — And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, was ever — was explained with *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — hearing disbelief and belief, knowing whether *khayran lakum* — better for you — is chosen — *He is All-Aware of what you do* (4:135) — and *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — who sent messengers as good news and warnings so no excuse (4:165) and took Mount for covenant and sent Book with truth to judge (4:105) — wisdom is that the Messenger came with *ḥaqq* from Lord. *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* was also the seal for *“whoever earns sin earns only upon himself, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise”* (4:111) — His knowing and wisdom guarantee that belief and disbelief are measured as not wronging an atom (4:40) and not wronging a speck (*naqīrā* — 4:124). To call to humanity — *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu* — to believe for your good, yet He is Self-Sufficient, All-Knowing, All-Wise, shows belief is medicine not debt.
verses.171:
> O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes regarding your faith; say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of Allah and the fulfilment of His Word through Mary and a spirit ˹created by a command˺ from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, “Trinity.” Stop!—for your own good. Allah is only One God. Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son! To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs

The verse opens *yā ahla al-kitābi lā taghlū fī dīnikum wa lā taqūlū ʿalā Allāhi illā al-ḥaqq* — O People of the Book, do not go to extremes, exceed limits, in your religion. Say nothing about God except the truth. *Lā taghlū* — do not exceed, go to extremes — was explained with *ghuluww* — excess beyond limit, as the sūrah earlier forbade association not forgiven though what is less is for whom He wills (4:116) and forbade distinguishing between God and messengers desiring a way between (4:150) — to make *ʿĪsā* god is excess, to deny him is neglect. *Wa lā taqūlū ʿalā Allāhi illā al-ḥaqq* — say nothing about God except truth — was explained as that He is enough as Witness (4:166) who bears witness with His knowledge, and whose word none is more truthful than (4:122): to say about Him without truth is to claim witness without knowledge. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); *ghuluww* is to judge without that showing. Early reports noted that Christians exceeded in Jesus as Jews did in slandering Mary with *buhtān ʿaẓīm* (4:156); the middle is *ḥaqq* — truth — that Jesus is servant honoured, not god.

The definition *innamā al-masīḥu ʿĪsā ibnu Maryama rasūlu Allāhi wa kalimatuhū alqāhā ilā Maryama wa rūḥun minhu* — the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of God and the fulfilment, execution, of His Word — *kalimah* — cast to Mary and a spirit — *rūḥ* — from Him, created by command from Him — was explained with three. *Rasūlu Allāhi* — messenger of God — was read as the chain’s continuity: *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Jesus… to Moses He spoke* (4:163–164), all messengers delivering good news and warnings so no excuse (4:165) — Jesus is among them. *Kalimatuhū alqāhā ilā Maryama* — His Word He conveyed to Mary — was explained as *“Be”* — *kun* — He said to Mary, as creation from a word, without father, as *“He creates what He wills when He decrees He says Be and it is”* — the *kalimah* is command not offspring. *Wa rūḥun minhu* — and a spirit from Him, created by command from Him — was explained as *rūḥ* — spirit — from Him as *“We breathed into her Our spirit”* (66:12), given, not part of Him — the sūrah later says *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee”* — the spirit belongs to Him. Where the sūrah says *“We have prepared for true disbelievers humiliating punishment”* (4:151) for distinguishing, and *“those who believe in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards”* (4:152) — this definition is the acceptance of Jesus as messenger among messengers, not god among gods.

The glorification *subḥānahu a yakūna lahū walad* — glory be to Him, exalted is He, that He should have a son, that there be for Him a child — was explained with *subḥānahu* — glory, exaltation — as the Book’s *tasbīḥ* for the One to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126, 4:131, 4:170). *An yakūna lahū walad* — that He should have a son — was read as impossibility for the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) who can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) — a son is not needed. *Lahū mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — was explained as that ownership denies need for son: *“if you disbelieve, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise”* (4:170) — after the Messenger has come with truth — Trinity divides ownership. *Wa kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* — and He suffices as Trustee — was read as that *wakīl* suffices as Guardian without son, as the oppressed cry for *walī* and *naṣīr* from grace (4:75) — guardian is Him, not third of three. The sūrah has shown that *“He is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132) — three is not needed for trusteeship.

Placed after *O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth. Believe for your own good, if you disbelieve to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise* (4:170), this verse follows humanity’s call with People of the Book’s correction where the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven and greater — visible God — took calf yet were forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant taken, then breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but raised (4:153–158).
verses.172:
> The Messiah would never be too proud to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels nearest to Allah. Those who are too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together

The verse states *lan yastankifa al-masīḥu a yakūna ʿabdan li Allāhi wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — the Messiah — *al-masīḥ* — Jesus, son of Mary, messenger and Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171) — would never disdain, be too proud, to be a servant, slave, to God, nor would the angels nearest — *al-muqarrabūn* — those brought near. *Lan yastankif* — never be too proud, never disdain, never refuse out of pride — was explained with *istinkāf* — pride that refuses service, as the sūrah has shown that those too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together (now). As earlier *Satan was proud* — *istakbara* — refusing prostration. *An yakūna ʿabdan li Allāhi* — to be a servant to God — was read as *ʿubūdiyyah* — servitude — the rank of every messenger in lineage — *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Jesus taught* (4:163) — all are servants. *Wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — nor the angels nearest — was explained as *muqarrab* — those brought near — *“the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest”* — the highest creatures — Messiah, whose mother was slandered with mighty *buhtān* (4:156). Angels who bear witness with His knowledge (4:166) and who stood witness for Mount raised (4:154) — are servants. The sūrah has shown that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee”* (4:171) — servants belong to Him; to claim the Messiah is beyond servitude is *ghuluww* — going to extremes (4:171) — the Messiah himself would never claim it.

**Those Too Proud to Worship Him Will Be Gathered Before Him**

The warning *wa man yastankif ʿan ʿibādatihī wa yastakbir fa sa yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamīʿā* — and whoever is too proud, disdains, to worship Him, serve Him. Is arrogant, will be gathered, mustered, to Him, toward Him, all together — was explained with *yastankif* — too proud — and *yastakbir* — arrogant, magnifies self — pair already in Satan, cursed (4:118) — who said *I will surely take a share* (4:118). *ʿAn ʿibādatihī* — from His worship, His servitude — was read as that *ʿubūdiyyah* is not debasement but honour, as Abraham taken as *khalīl* (4:125) was servant, as Moses spoken to directly (4:164) was servant, as angels nearest are servants. *Fa sa yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamīʿā* — He will gather them to Him all together — was explained with *ḥashara* — to gather, to muster — the same gathering as *He will gather you on the Day about which there is no doubt* (4:87) and *He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) and *those who disbelieve and wrong, He will not forgive nor guide except Hell’s path forever* (4:168–169) — the too proud are gathered for reckoning.
verses.173:
> As for those who believe and do good, He will reward them in full and increase them out of His grace. But those who are too proud and arrogant, He will subject them to a painful punishment. And besides Allah they will find no protector or helper

The verse opens *fa ammā alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti fa yuwaffīhim ujūrahum wa yazīduhum min faḍlihī* — as for those who believe and do good, do righteous deeds, He will repay, fulfil, their rewards fully and increase them out of His bounty, grace. *Āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt* — faith and righteous deeds — was explained as the sūrah’s shorthand for the faithful: opposed to those too proud to worship Him (4:172) and those who disbelieve and hinder far astray (4:167). *Fa yuwaffīhim ujūrahum* — He will fulfil their wages, repay fully — was read with *waffā* — to give in full, to complete — the same root for *“God does not wrong even an atom, if it is good He multiplies”* (4:40) — fulfilling is not wronging even speck (*naqīrā* — 4:124) — the atom not wronged is the wage given full. *Wa yazīduhum min faḍlihī* — and increase them out of His grace, bounty — was explained with *faḍl* — grace, bounty — the same *faḍl* without which a group would have deceived you yet they deceive only themselves (4:113). *“great is His favour upon you”* (4:113) — increase is from grace, not debt, as Gardens forever where promise is true (4:122) — increase is Rivers under, not cut. Early reports linked increase to *“He will admit them into Gardens … under rivers flow”* and to abundant Havens for emigrant (4:100) — world and Hereafter.

**And Besides Him They Will Find No Protector or Helper**

The closure *wa lā yajidūna lahum min dūni Allāhi waliyyan wa lā naṣīrā* — and they will not find for themselves besides Him, apart from Him, any protector, guardian, nor helper — was explained with *walī* and *naṣīr* — the same pair the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45) and that hypocrites sought among disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) — the too proud sought *ʿizzah* among disbelievers and among pride itself. Will find no *walī* and no *naṣīr* besides Him where punishment is. *Min dūni Allāhi* — besides Him, apart from Him — was read as that no female god invoked (4:117) and no Satan as guardian taken instead of Him (4:119) and no disbeliever as ally (4:144) will avail on the Day where all are gathered before Him all together (4:172). The sūrah has said *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — protection besides Him is not needed where both rewards are with Him; to seek it is to find none. Where the sūrah says *“He is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:171) — Messiah’s case — the too proud find no trustee.

**A Verse That Follows Gathering With Repaying and Punishing**

Placed after *the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest. Those too proud and arrogant will be gathered before Him all together* (4:172), this verse follows gathering with repaying and punishing: as for those who believe and do good — fulfilled wages and increase from grace; but those too proud and arrogant — painful punishment, no protector or helper besides Him. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) — fulfilled wages is that entry. And *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides Him”* (4:123) — painful where disbelief and wrong are — now applied to pride. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) sees *istinkāf wa istikbār* — being too proud and arrogant — as the pride that deviates most, because *ʿubūdiyyah* — servitude — is the sūrah’s ethic: to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135) is servitude, to not incline completely leaving hanging (4:129) is servitude, to verify before fighting (4:94) is servitude.
verses.174:
> O humanity! There has come to you conclusive evidence from your Lord. And We have sent down to you a brilliant light

**O Humanity — Conclusive Evidence Has Come From Your Lord**

The verse states *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu qad jāʾakum burhānun min rabbikum* — O humanity, there has certainly come to you a proof, evidence, demonstration, from your Lord. *Yā ayyuhā al-nāsu* — O humanity — was explained as third great humanity address after *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* (4:1) and *“if He wills He can remove you and bring others”* (4:133) and *“the Messenger has come with truth from your Lord. Believe for your own good”* (4:170) — now *“conclusive evidence has come.”* *Qad jāʾakum* — has certainly come to you — was read with emphasis: the evidence has arrived, not pending, as lineage from Noah through Jesus to you (4:163) was already sent as *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn* so no excuse remains (4:165) — now evidence. *Burhānun min rabbikum* — proof from your Lord — was explained with *burhān* — conclusive proof, demonstration — the same root *brh* as clarity where *He wills to make clear* (4:26) and *taught you what you did not know* (4:113) — *burhān* is the Prophet ﷺ himself with miracles and the Qur’an as proof. Early reports linked *burhān* to the Prophet, while *nūr* — light — after is Qur’an, showing two proofs: messenger and book. The sūrah has shown that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126) — proof from your Lord who owns and encompasses is the most near. The phrase was linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — proof’s purpose is Gardens, as *“O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth, so believe for your own good”* (4:170) — better for you.

**And We Have Sent Down to You a Brilliant Light**

The second clause *wa anzalnā ilaykum nūran mubīnā* — and We have sent down to you a clear, brilliant, manifest light — was explained with *nūr* — light — *mubīn* — clear, manifest — the same *nūr* and *mubīn* as *sulṭān mubīn* — compelling proof — Moses was given (4:153) and as clear light where association is not forgiven (4:116) — light shows far straying. *Anzalnā ilaykum* — We sent down to you — was read as the Qur’an sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) — light shows judgment, as the Mount raised (4:154) was physical light of proof. *Nūr mubīn* was explained as Qur’an that makes clear, as *“He wills to lighten burdens”* (4:28) — light lightens; the sūrah that taught prayer at fixed time (4:103) as *kitāban mawqūtā* — light times. Early reports added that the *burhān* and *nūr* are the two witnesses: God bears witness with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166) — His knowledge is light, angels’ witness is proof. Where the sūrah says *“do not go to extremes regarding faith, say nothing but truth”* (4:171) — do not say Trinity — truth is the light that makes extremes visible as extremes, as Satan’s promises only delusion (4:120) are darkness.

**A Verse That Follows Humanity’s Call With Complement**

Placed after *O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth. Believe for your own good* (4:170), *O People of the Book, do not go to extremes, Messiah was but messenger, Word through Mary and spirit from Him, do not say Trinity* (4:171), *Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest, those too proud will be gathered then repaid in full and increased or punished painful without protector* (4:172–173), this verse follows humanity’s call and messiah’s correction with its complement: conclusive evidence has come from your Lord — messenger — and brilliant light sent down — Qur’an. The sūrah has shown that those who disbelieve and hinder far astray (4:167), disbelieve and wrong not forgiven nor guided except Hell’s path forever easy (4:168–169) — light is the opposite hindering: to send light is to unhinder. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) — light is the *najwā* made good: the Book’s light as charity. For the weak this is an opening: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement is best (4:128), light shows settlement; where helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99), light shows pardon hoped is light; where emigrant finds many havens (4:100), light shows havens.
verses.175:
> As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the Straight Path

**Those Who Believe and Hold Fast — Admitted Into Mercy and Grace**

The verse states *fa ammā alladhīna āmanū bi Allāhi wa iʿtaṣamū bihī fa sa yudkhiluhum fī raḥmatin minhu wa faḍlin* — as for those who believe in God and hold fast, cling, to Him, He will admit, will enter them, into mercy from Him and grace, bounty. *Āmanū bi Allāhi* — believe in God — was explained with comprehensive faith — *have faith in God, Messenger, Book and Scriptures, angels, Last Day* (4:136) — steadfast, not wavering, not distinguishing (4:150–152) — the faith that accepts all messengers whose stories told and not (4:164) after lineage from Noah through Jesus (4:163). *Wa iʿtaṣamū bihī* — and hold fast, cling, to Him, to it — was read with *iʿtiṣām* — holding fast — the same *iʿtiṣām* that repentant hypocrites must do — *hold fast to God* (4:146) — and that those well-grounded do — establishing prayer (4:162) — and that the emigrant to God has reward secured (4:100). *Iʿtaṣamū bihī* was explained as *bih* — to Him, to it — both: to God and to His rope — the Qur’an — the brilliant light — *nūr mubīn* — evidence — *burhān* (4:174) — and to the Book sent with truth to judge between people (4:105). *Fa sa yudkhiluhum fī raḥmatin minhu wa faḍlin* — He will admit them into mercy from Him and grace — was explained with *raḥmah* — mercy — and *faḍl* — grace, bounty — the two that make Gardens true (4:122) — mercy as forgiveness for faults, grace as increase. The sūrah has said *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — admission into mercy and grace is the Appreciative’s response to holding fast. Where *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — mercy and grace are those rewards.

**And Guide Them to Himself Through the Straight Path**

The second promise *wa yahdīhim ilayhi ṣirāṭan mustaqīman* — and He will guide them to Him, toward Him, through, as, the straight — upright, direct — path — was explained with *yahdīhim ilayhi* — guide them to Him, toward Him — not only to Gardens but to Himself, as the emigrant emigrates to God and Messenger (4:100) — reward falls upon Him. *Ṣirāṭ mustaqīm* — straight path — was explained as the sūrah’s path — noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26), believers’ path not to be left (4:115), the path He guides to through mercy (now), as the sūrah wills to make clear, guide, turn. *Mustaqīm* — straight, upright — was read as the opposite of *ghuluww* — going to extremes (4:171) — Trinity and denial both deviate; straight is middle — Messiah as servant not god, Mary pure not slandered, Moses spoken to directly — true. The sūrah has shown that *“the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant”* (4:172) — servitude is straight; to be too proud is deviant. *Yahdīhim ilayhi* was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, promise ever true”* (4:122) — Gardens are mercy and grace guided to Him.

**Mercy and Grace Guided Through Straight Path**

The pair *raḥmah minhu wa faḍl* — mercy from Him and grace — was explained as mercy that pardons the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) — *ʿAfuww Ghafūr* — and forgives the mistaken by fasting (4:92) — and grace that gives many havens to the emigrant (4:100) — *murāgham kathīr wa saʿah* — and great reward to the grounded (4:162) — *ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and repays doers of good in full and increases out of grace (4:173). *Yahdīhim ilayhi ṣirāṭan mustaqīman* was linked to *“He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26–28) — making clear is *burhān* and *nūr* (4:174), guiding to noble ways is *ṣirāṭ mustaqīm* now, turning in mercy is *raḥmah minhu wa faḍl*. To be guided to Him through straight path is to be among those who believe and do good in Gardens where promise is true (4:122) — straight is the sūrah’s law for orphans, women, inheritance, trust, prayer, judgment, charity, Abraham, settlement, enrichment — all are straight.
verses.176:
> They ask you ˹for a ruling, O Prophet˺. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling regarding those who die without children or parents.” If a man dies childless and leaves behind a sister, she will inherit one-half of his estate, whereas her brother will inherit all of her estate if she dies childless. If this person leaves behind two sisters, they together will inherit two-thirds of the estate. But if the deceased leaves male and female siblings, a male’s share will be equal to that of two females. Allah makes ˹this˺ clear to you so you do not go astray. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things

**They Ask You for a Ruling Regarding One Without Children or Parents**

The verse opens *yastaftūnaka quli Allāhu yuftīkum fī al-kalālati* — they ask you, seek your ruling, your *fatwā* — say, God gives you ruling about the *kalālah* — the one who dies without children or parents, without direct ascendant or descendant. *Yastaftūnaka* — they ask you — was explained as second asking in the sūrah after *“they ask you regarding women, God instructs you, instruction already recited concerning orphan women deprived yet wished to marry, helpless children, orphans’ rights, whatever good you do is well known to Him”* (4:127) — now they ask about *kalālah*. *Quli Allāhu yuftīkum* — say, God instructs you, gives ruling — was read as that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126) — so He instructs, as evidence and light have come from your Lord (4:174) — instruction is light. *Fī al-kalālati* — about *kalālah* — was explained with *kalālah* — one who leaves neither parent nor child, the one whose line is cut at both ends, whose estate is therefore to siblings, as the sūrah earlier said *“you will inherit half of what your wives leave if childless. If they have children then one-fourth… And if a man or woman leaves neither parents nor children but only a sibling then…”* (4:12) where *kalālah* rule began for maternal siblings — here it is extended to paternal/full siblings. Early reports noted this verse was among the last revealed, answering Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s illness where he was *kalālah* without parent or child, asking about his sisters’ shares — the sūrah’s closing is personal.

The details *in imruʾun halaka laysa lahū waladun wa lahū ukhtun fa lahā niṣfu mā taraka wa huwa yarithuhā in lam yakun lahā walad* — if a man dies, perishes, is destroyed — *halaka* — leaves no child. Has a sister, then for her is half what he leaves, and he — her brother — inherits her — all of her — if she dies childless — were explained with two mirrors. *Imruʾun halaka* — a man perishes — *laysa lahū waladun* — he has no child — was read as the *kalālah* male. *wa lahū ukhtun* — and has a sister — one sister alone. *fa lahā niṣfu mā taraka* — for her half what he leaves — after gift and debt, as obligatory shares (4:7: little or much, obligatory) — half for one female, as earlier one female alone inherits one-half (4:11) where daughter alone half — here sister half. *Wa huwa yarithuhā in lam yakun lahā walad* — and he inherits her — her brother inherits all of her estate if she dies childless without parent — was explained as that brother as sole sibling inherits entirety where sister alone half — the imbalance was read as not unfair because sibling inheritance here is for full/paternal siblings where male’s share will be equal to two females where together (next). Where no child the brother assumes clan protection, as the single soul spread into humanity (4:1) — brother inherits all to sustain ties. The sūrah has shown that inheritance is *farīḍah* — obligation (4:11) — and that limits set by God admit to Gardens (4:13) and exceeding casts into Hell (4:14) — *kalālah* shares are limits.

**If Two Sisters — They Inherit Two-Thirds**

The case *fa in kānatā ithnatayni fa lahumā al-thuluthāni mimmā taraka* — but if the two — sisters — are two, then for them two-thirds of what he leaves — was explained with *ithnatayni* — two sisters together — as the female pair, as earlier *if you leave only two or more females, their share is two-thirds* (4:11) where daughters two-plus two-thirds — here sisters two two-thirds. *Mimmā taraka* — of what he leaves — after gift and debt, as *“after fulfilment of gifts and debts without harm”* (4:12) — harm not to heirs. The sūrah has shown that shares for men and women whether little or much are obligatory (4:7), that orphan women deprived yet wished to marry are protected (4:127), that helpless children are stood for with justice (4:127): sisters as *kalālah* heirs are that justice applied at death without child or parent. Early notes added that two sisters as *kalālah* share two-thirds leaving one-third to others where present; the sūrah’s light — *We have sent down brilliant light* (4:174) — makes that clear so you do not go astray.

The seal *yubayyinu Allāhu lakum a taḍillū wa Allāhu bi kulli shayʾin ʿalīm* — God makes clear to you, explains, lest you go astray. You do not stray, and God has perfect knowledge of all things, of every thing — was explained with *yubayyinu lakum* — He makes clear to you — the same *yubayyin* as *“He wills to make clear to you, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26) and *burhān* and *nūr mubīn* — evidence and brilliant light — have come (4:174) — now *kalālah* clear. *An taḍillū* — lest you go astray, so you do not stray — was read as that inheritance without clarity would be *ẓulm* — wrongdoing — and *ṣadd* — hindering many from God’s way — the same wrong for which *ṭayyibāt* were forbidden (4:160); to make clear is to prevent straying. *Wa Allāhu bi kulli shayʾin ʿalīm* — and God has perfect knowledge of every thing, of all things — was explained with *bi kulli shayʾ* — of every thing — the same *muḥīṭ* — encompassing everything (4:126) — knowledge that counts every *walad* — child — and every *ukht* — sister — and every *akh* — brother — and every gift and debt without harm, as He is Fully Aware of everything (4:126) and All-Aware of what you do (4:128, 4:135) — the One who owns heavens and earth (4:126, 4:131) knows *kalālah* shares. The sūrah that began with single soul spread into humanity (4:1) and commanded honouring ties, ends with ties’ shares at death where single soul’s line is cut at both ends — *kalālah* — yet ties remain as siblings. God makes clear so you do not stray, as He is *ʿAlīm* of all.
